# Technical Manual 

## COMPANY PROFILE 

Herbs of Gold is proudly Australian owned and grown. Born in 1989 as a humble herbal liquid product company, we now boast a comprehensive range of more than 100 herbal, vitamin, mineral and nutrient formulations that come in tablet, capsule, powder and liquid forms to suit people of all ages and stages of life. 

For over 30 years, we have been devoted to producing a 'gold standard' range of therapeutic herbal and nutritional supplements that are both innovative and of the highest quality. Our passion is to capture the best nature has to offer, drawing from the wisdom of the past and combining it with the knowledge of the future, and using this to develop therapeutic supplements that support the ongoing health of both the body and the mind. 

Our team of highly qualified, experienced naturopaths, herbalists and nutritionists formulate products that are clean and free from as many binders and fillers as possible, priding ourselves on our strong vegan-friendly range that is both low allergy and free from artificial colours, flavours, sweeteners and preservatives. 

## QUALITY ASSURANCE 

Health food and pharmacy retailers have come to know and trust Herbs of Gold for its quality, integrity and reliability. Our products undergo rigorous testing at each step of the manufacturing process, from the selection of raw materials right through to the manufacture of finished goods. Each of our products meet stringent guidelines for safety and quality, guidelines set not only by us here at Herbs of Gold, but also by the Australian Government. 

## TECHNICAL SUPPORT 

In addition to providing our customers with quality products, at Herbs of Gold we are also firm believers in providing our customers with a quality experience. Our friendly staff are always here to help, from our sales team and training representatives who support you in store, through to our customer service, technical and accounts teams who are here to support you over the phone. 

Herbs of Gold has a focus on education to back our therapeutic formulas and provide retailers with all the information they need to recommend products that suit their customers’ needs and ensure their customers return time and time again. 

## THE FUTURE 

Herbs of Gold strives to be the leader in high-quality, innovative over-the-counter supplements. We choose to partner with selected health food stores and pharmacies in order to provide consumers with access to quality advice to achieve the best health outcome.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Acetyl L-carnitine is the acetylated form of the amino acid L-carnitine and occurs naturally in the body where it is synthesised in the brain, liver and kidneys. 

- The major difference between acetyl L-carnitine and carnitine is that acetyl L-carnitine is more easily absorbed from the gut, and more readily crosses the blood-brain barrier. 

- The richest sources of carnitine are meat, poultry, fish and dairy products, while grains, vegetables and fruits contain relatively small amounts placing vegetarians at risk of primary deficiency. 

- The L-isomer of carnitine is the biologically active form, whereas the D-isomer may compete with L-carnitine for absorption and transport. 

- Carnitine acts as an antioxidant in the cell membrane and protects tissues from oxidative damage. 

## Fat metabolism & energy production 

- Acetyl L-carnitine supports energy production and fat metabolism. It facilitates the uptake of acetyl CoA into the mitochondria during fatty acid oxidation, which allows the body to turn fat into energy. It also assists the transport of fat across the cell membranes in muscle tissue for use as an energy source. 

- Acetyl L-carnitine is most concentrated in tissues that use fatty acids as their primary fuel, such as skeletal and cardiac (heart) muscle. In this regard, L-carnitine plays an important role in energy production by conjugating fatty acids for transport into the mitochondria for beta oxidation. 

## Cognitive function 

- Acetyl L-carnitine supports cognitive function and brain function. 

- Acetyl L-carnitine can traverse the blood-brain barrier and modulate phospholipid metabolism, synaptic morphology and transmission, enhancing the synthesis and release of neurotrophic factors, neurohormones and multiple neurotransmitters which helps support cognitive function. Improvement in cognitive function may be connected to processes influenced by the brain’s energy production[1] . 

- Acetyl L-carnitine serves as a precursor to acetyl coenzyme A and contributes acetyl groups to acetylcholine. Acetyl L-carnitine also seems to promote acetylcholine release and increases choline acetyltransferase activity. 

- Acetyl L-carnitine may have neuroplasticity effects in some regions of the brain. It can increase levels of brain-derived neurotrophic factor and the release of glutamate, an excitatory neurotransmitter that plays an important role in learning and memory. 

- In an open-label, randomised study, 30 individuals with fatigue were given 2g/day of acetyl L-carnitine for 24 weeks. Significant improvements in mental fatigue and attention concentration were seen in the acetyl L-carnitine group. Two weeks after discontinuing treatment 52% of individuals experienced worsening of fatigue[2] . 

## Muscle health & post-exercise recovery 

- Acetyl L-Carnitine supports muscle performance and aids post exercise recovery. Due to its role as a transporter of long-chain fatty acids across the mitochondrial membrane for beta-oxidation, L-carnitine supports endurance exercise, which requires the use of long-chain fatty acids as an energy substrate. L-carnitine can enhance exercise performance by increasing fatty acid oxidation in skeletal muscle, thereby reducing muscle glycogen usage and increasing overall exercise capacity. 

- Multiple studies have examined the favourable effects of L-carnitine on reducing exercise-induced hypoxia, subsequent muscle damage and delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS)[3] . 

- A single-blind study in 6 untrained subjects found that 3g/day of L-carnitine significantly reduced pain, tenderness and CK release after 20-minute eccentric effort compared to placebo. This effect was attributed to the vasodilatory properties of L-carnitine that improves energetic metabolism of hypoxic/damaged muscles[4] . 

- Both chronic and acute supplementation with L-carnitine, with or without protein during training, have been reported to enhance exercise capacity and endurance at a dose of 1-2g/day[5] . 

## Sperm health 

   - Acetyl L-Carnitine supports sperm health by improving sperm motility and reducing the levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in seminal fluid and improving semen quality[6] . 

   - L-carnitine is highly concentrated in the epididymis and sperm where it plays a role in promoting sperm motility, maturation and fertilisation. Due to its antioxidant activity, it helps protect sperm against oxidative damage, reduces apoptosis in spermatogenic cells and inhibits sperm aggregation. L-carnitine is used by spermatozoa for mitochondrial beta-oxidation of fatty acids for use as an energy source. 

   - A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial involving 89 males with low sperm quality found that 2g of L-carnitine daily significantly improved sperm concentration and motility over the course of 2 months[7] .

## **Acetyl L-Carnitine** 

- In a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 56 males with asthenozoospermia (reduced sperm motility) were given a combination of 2g of L-carnitine and 1g of acetyl L-carnitine daily. After 6 months of therapy, increases in total and forward sperm motility was observed compared with placebo group[8] . 

## Nerve health 

- Acetyl L-Carnitine supports healthy nervous system function and nerve conduction. 

- Preclinical studies have demonstrated a central anti-nociceptive action, both in neuropathic and nociceptive pain models. Acetyl L-carnitine operates via several mechanisms, inducing regeneration of injured nerve fibres, reducing oxidative stress, promoting DNA synthesis in mitochondria and increasing nerve growth factor (NGF) concentrations in neurons, thus promoting neurite extension. 

- Acetyl L-carnitine provides acetyl groups for acetylcholine synthesis, thus exerting a cholinergic effect. Acetyl L-carnitine also influences functional aspects of serotonergic, noradrenergic and GABA neurotransmission. 

- A systematic review and meta-analyses assessing the efficacy and safety of acetyl L-carnitine on peripheral neuropathic pain concluded that acetyl L-carnitine had a moderate effect in reducing pain, with a dosage of 2g/day proving most beneficial[9] . 

## Mood support 

- Studies performed on animal and cellular models suggest that acetyl L-carnitine influences neuroplasticity, membrane modulation and neurotransmitter regulation, with serotonergic and possibly dopaminergic activity, which plays an important role in supporting healthy mood balance[10] . 

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Caution with anticoagulants/antiplatelets – L-carnitine may theoretically potentiate drug effects and increase the risk of bleeding. Monitor. 

- Caution with levothyroxine – L-carnitine may theoretically decrease effectiveness of levothyroxine. Monitor thyroid function. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- Not recommended in pregnancy due to a lack of safety data. 

- Caution in individuals with chronic liver disease or epilepsy. 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- Acetyl L-carnitine is well tolerated at the recommended dose. 

- Mild gastrointestinal symptoms, including abdominal cramps diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting and heartburn may occur.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Activated B Complex contains therapeutic doses of all B vitamins. It contains: 

- Riboflavin-5-phosphate, the active form of vitamin B2. 

- Pyridoxal 5-phosphate (PLP), the active form of vitamin B6 (PLP is the most common form of B6 found in human tissue). 

- Methylfolate, the active form of folic acid. 

- Methylcobalamin (mecobalamin), the metabolically-active coenzyme form of vitamin B12. 

- As B vitamins are water soluble, regular daily intake is required to support general health. B vitamins work synergistically in the body and are, therefore, best taken together. 

- Vitamins B2 and B3 support liver detoxification and are involved in antioxidant enzyme systems that help maintain tissue antioxidant defences. Vitamin B2, as a cofactor of glutathione reductase, helps recycle the important antioxidant glutathione. 

- Folate and B12 are important for cell growth and replication. 

- Activated B Complex helps prevent dietary B viatmin deficiencies. 

- Activated B Complex is suitable for preconception, pregnancy and breastfeeding to help meet the increased nutritional requirements. It provides 400 micrograms of methylfolate, also known as 5-methyltetrahydrofolate (5-MTHF), to support healthy foetal development. 

## Energy 

- B vitamins support energy production and help relieve fatigue. They are required for the metabolism of dietary carbohydrates, proteins and fats and the production of energy in every cell. 

- Vitamin B1 is an essential coenzyme in the production of energy and is stored in muscles, where it plays a central role in energy production. 

- Vitamin B2 is an essential part of the coenzymes flavin mononucleotide (FMD) and flavin-adenosine dinucleotide (FAD) that play central roles in cellular respiration and the production of ATP in the mitochondria. 

- Vitamin B3 is a component of the reduced and oxidised forms of the coenzyme nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH2 and NAD, 

   - respectively), both of which are involved in energy metabolism. 

- Vitamin B5, as CoA, transfers fatty acids into the mitochondria for energy production. 

- Vitamin B12 is involved in the synthesis of the citric acid cycle intermediate, succinyl-CoA, necessary for energy production. 

- B vitamins support healthy exercise capacity. Athletes and people who engage in vigorous exercise have an increased requirement for B vitamins. 

## Nervous system 

- B vitamins support healthy nervous system function. They are required for the synthesis of neurotransmitters such as acetylcholine, norepinephrine, dopamine, GABA and serotonin and help maintain healthy mood. 

- B vitamins support the stress response. Deficiencies have been linked to mild anxiety and mood changes. Requirements for B vitamins increase during times of physical and mental stress. 

- Vitamin B1 is located in the nerve cell membrane and is important for the transmission of nerve impulses. It plays a role in the metabolism of several neurotransmitters, including acetylcholine, GABA and serotonin. 

- Vitamin B5 is known as the “anti-stress vitamin” as it supports adrenal function and is involved the production of adrenal hormones. It is also necessary for the production of acetylcholine. 

- Vitamin B6 is important for the synthesis of lipids that form the myelin sheath surrounding nerves and is required for the formation of several neurotransmitters including serotonin, dopamine, GABA and norepinephrine. Pyridoxine is a cofactor in the conversion of tryptophan to serotonin and deficiency is associated with mood alterations. 

- Vitamin B12 and methylfolate are essential for healthy brain and memory function. Supplementation with 400 micrograms of folate has been positively associated with improved results in the Word List Memory Test and Constructional Recall Test scores[1] . Low B12 status is associated with more rapid cognitive decline in older adults[2] . 

- Vitamin B12 is essential for the synthesis of myelin, the protective sheath surrounding many nerves and is important for healthy

## Cardiovascular system 

- B vitamins, particularly B6, B12 and folate, help maintain blood health and a healthy cardiovascular system. 

- Vitamins B6, B12 and folate are necessary for oxygen transport in red blood cells. B6 is involved in haemoglobin synthesis and B12 and folate are required for the formation of red blood cells. 

- Vitamin B6, B12 and methylfolate help maintain a healthy cardiovascular system by maintaining healthy homocysteine levels. High levels of homocysteine are associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Methylcobalamin and methylfolate facilitate the conversion of homocysteine to methionine. Vitamin B6 is a cofactor in the conversion of homocysteine to cystathionine. Maintenance of healthy homocysteine levels correlates to heart, brain and cognitive health. 

- In one double-blind, randomised, controlled trial, daily supplementation with 400 micrograms methylfolate resulted in a significant decrease in homocysteine concentration after 4 weeks of intervention[4] . 

## Methylfolate vs folic acid 

- Activated B Complex contains methylfolate (5-MTHF), the active form of folate. Folate is the generic term for a large family of chemically similar compounds known as vitamin B9. Folic acid is a synthetic form of the vitamin and must be reduced to methylfolate for use in the body. 

- After ingestion, both dietary folate and synthetic folic acid need to undergo a complex conversion, via a multistep pathway in the liver, to their active forms. Methylfolate is the active form of folate in the body and accounts for approximately 98% of folates in human plasma. Supplemental methylfolate is directly available and does not need to be metabolised. 

- High dose supplementation of folic acid can delay the appearance of the haematological symptoms of a B12 deficiency. Methylfolate is a good alternative to folic acid as it does not mask vitamin B12 deficiency symptoms and thus B12 deficiency is more likely to be diagnosed and treated. 

- Methylene-tetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) is an enzyme that converts folate into its active form. Several polymorphisms, or gene variations, exist which can affect folate metabolism and significantly 

increase the risk of folate deficiency in affected individuals, even when meeting the recommended daily intakes. 

- The most common mutation is the MTHFR C677T mutation. Individuals who are heterozygote (one copy of the gene) for the MTHFR C677T mutation (2-16% white population)[5] have a 40% reduction in activity of the MTHFR enzyme and individuals who are homozygote (two copies of the gene) have about a 70% reduction in activity. Lower levels of MTHFR enzyme reduces the production of methylfolate and is the most common risk factor for both high homocysteine and neural tube defects. In people with MTHFR polymorphisms, methylfolate appears to be the supplement of choice, as it does not require conversion. 

- Activated B Complex contains methylfolate as Quatrefolic[®] , the glucosamine salt of (6S)-5-methyltetrahydrofolate. Quatrefolic[®] is an active form of folate, immediately available for its biological action without being metabolised in the body. Quatrefolic[®] has high bioavailability and is more bioavailable than other forms of methylfolate, including the calcium salt. Rat studies show that the glucosamine salt is 12% better absorbed than the calcium salt[6] and human studies show that it is 10% better absorbed[7] . 

## Methylcobalamin 

- Activated B Complex contains methylcobalamin (mecobalamin), the metabolically-active coenzyme form of vitamin B12 that is readily bioavailable for use in the body. Commonly-used cyanocobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 that does not occur naturally in foods and needs to be converted to methylcobalamin for use in the body. Methylcobalamin differs from cyanocobalamin in that the non-toxic cyanide molecule is replaced by a methyl group. 

- Methylcobalamin appears to have better uptake by neurons than cyanocobalamin and may, therefore, be a better option for nervous system disorders. Studies show that methylcobalamin can improve nerve conduction and promote nerve and axonal regeneration, has neuro-protective properties and can protect against glutamateinduced neurotoxicity[8] . 

- The elderly, strict vegetarians and vegans are at increased risk of vitamin B12 deficiency. Vitamin B12 is only found in foods of animal origin, so a vegetarian diet is likely to be deficient in B12. The absorption of B12 from the diet is dependent on adequate stomach acid and intrinsic factor, secretion of which declines with age, placing many elderly people at risk of deficiency. People with poor digestive function and those on acid-suppressing medications are also at an increased risk of deficiency.

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Caution with cholestyramine and colestipol (hypolipidaemic agents) - may decrease the absorption of vitamin B3 and folate. Separate dose by at least 4-6 hours. 

- Caution with phenobarbital and phenytoin (anticonvulsants) - high 

- doses of vitamin B6 or folate can decrease their efficacy. Monitor. 

- Caution with L-Dopa - vitamin B6 increases the peripheral metabolism of levodopa and may lower levodopa levels for CNS penetration, resulting in reduced levodopa effects. The effect of pyridoxine is prevented by administration of a dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor (e.g. benserazide, carbidopa) with levodopa, as is common clinical practice. 

- Caution with antiepileptic and anticonvulsant medications – folic acid may reduce serum levels of these medications. Patients should take folate only under the supervision of a health professional. 

- Caution with methotrexate (folic acid antagonist) - co-administrate with folate may reduce the effects. Patients should take folate only under the supervision of a health professional. 

- Caution with tetracycline hydrochloride (antibiotic) - B vitamins may reduce drug bioavailability. Separate dose by at least 2 hours. 

- Several medications may deplete folate status, including trimethoprim (antibiotic), pyrimethamine (antimalarial), triamterene (blood pressure), sulfasalazine (for ulcerative colitis) and oral contraceptives. 

- Several medications can decrease the absorption of vitamin B12 or increase the risk of deficiency, such as acid-suppressing medications (proton-pump inhibitors e.g. omeprazole and histamine2 (h2)-receptor antagonists), metformin (hypoglycaemic), oral contraceptives, neomycin (antibiotic) and colchicine (anti-gout). 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- B vitamins are stimulatory in nature. To avoid any sleep interferance, avoid taking before bed. 

- Taking at night may result in more vivid dreams (vitamin B6). 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- Supplemental B vitamins may cause nausea or mild gastrointestinal upset if taken on an empty stomach. Best taken with food to reduce risk. 

- Riboflavin can impart a bright yellow colour to urine.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is a water-soluble vitamin that is essential for DNA synthesis, cell reproduction, carbohydrate metabolism, immune health, nervous system health and cardiovascular health. 

- Activated B12 Spray contains methylcobalamin (mecobalamin), the metabolically-active coenzyme form of vitamin B12 that is ready for use in the body. Commonly used cyanocobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 that does not occur naturally in foods and needs to be converted to methylcobalamin for use in the body. Methylcobalamin differs from cyanocobalamin in that the nontoxic cyanide molecule is replaced by a methyl group. 

- Vitamin B12 is mostly obtained from animal protein in the diet, with high levels found in organ meats, sardines, oysters, egg yolk, fish, beef, cheese and milk. 

- Activated B12 Spray supports energy production in the body. Vitamin B12 is involved in the synthesis of the citric acid cycle intermediate, succinyl-CoA, necessary for energy production. 

- Activated B12 Spray provides high-strength vitamin B12 in each spray, which can be easily administered under the tongue as an alternative to oral and sublingual tablets to help prevent a vitamin B12 deficiency. Activated B12 Spray has a natural mixed berry flavour and is naturally sweetened with Stevia for compliance. 

## Nervous system & brain health 

- Vitamin B12 is essential for nervous system health and an adequate intake is essential for normal neurological function. It is essential for the synthesis of myelin, the protective sheath surrounding many nerves. Additionally, B12 is involved in the synthesis of neurotransmitters and, in conjunction with folate, is involved in S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe) production, which is involved in healthy mood. 

- Vitamin B12 supports brain health and healthy cognition. The European Food Safety Authority concluded that there is a causeand-effect relationship between the dietary intake of vitamin B12 and contribution to normal neurological and psychological functions[1] . Low B12 status is associated with more rapid cognitive decline in older adults[2] . 

- Methylcobalamin appears to have better uptake by neurons than cyanocobalamin and may, therefore, be a better option to support nervous system health. Studies show that methylcobalamin can improve nerve conduction and promote nerve and axonal regeneration, has neuro-protective properties and can protect against glutamate-induced neurotoxicity[3] . 

## Cardiovascular system & blood health 

- Activated B12 Spray helps maintain blood health and a healthy cardiovascular system. 

- Vitamin B12 is necessary for red blood cell production and for the synthesis of haemoglobin, which carries oxygen in red blood cells throughout the body. 

- Vitamin B12, together with folate and vitamin B6, helps maintain healthy homocysteine levels in the body by facilitating the conversion of homocysteine to methionine. High homocysteine levels are associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes. 

- A double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised, cross over study in 55 healthy vegetarians investigated the impact of 500 micrograms of vitamin B12 on cardiovascular function. Of the 55 subjects, 35 (70%) had suboptimal serum B12 levels. Supplementation with 500 micrograms of vitamin B12 daily significantly increased serum vitamin B12 (p<0.0001) and lowered plasma homocysteine (p<0.05). Supplementation also improved brachial flow mediated dilation (FMD) (p<0.0001)[4] . 

## B12 absorption 

   - Activated B12 Spray delivers vitamin B12 sublingually, where it can be absorbed directly into sublingual capillaries, bypassing the digestive tract. 

   - In contrast, oral vitamin B12 administration requires sufficient stomach acid and intrinsic factor in order to be absorbed. Sublingual administration is beneficial for those with poor digestive function and is an alternative to oral (swallowed) tablets and intramuscular injections. 

   - The elderly, strict vegetarians and vegans are at increased risk of vitamin B12 deficiency. Vitamin B12 is only found in foods of animal origin, so a vegetarian diet is likely to be deficient in B12. The secretion of stomach acid declines with age, placing many elderly people at risk of deficiency. People with poor digestive function and those on acid-suppressing medications are also at an increased risk of deficiency. 

   - An intervention study compared the efficacy of sublingual and oral administration of 500 micrograms of vitamin B12 in 30 subjects with B12 deficiency. After 4 weeks, B12 increased in both the sublingual and oral supplementation groups (p=0.0001), with no significant difference between the group[5] .

## **Activated B12 Spray** 

- A recent (2019) retrospective analysis compared the efficacy of sublingual B12 to intramuscular B12 in restoring B12 levels. Data was pulled from 4281 patients with a diagnosed vitamin B12 deficiency. Of these, 830 (19.3%) were given intramuscular injections and 3451 (80.7%) were given sublingual tablets, each at a dose of 1000 micrograms cobalamin. The mean standard deviation difference between levels before and after B12 administration was significantly higher in the sublingual group versus the intramuscular injection group (252 ± 223 vs. 218 ± 184ng/L, p<0.001). Sublingual administration significantly increased the odds ratio for increasing serum B12 levels compared to the intramscular group (p<0.001)[6] . 

As Activated B12 Spray delivers vitamin B12 sublingually, it is reasonable to assume similar absorption efficacy to tablet sublingual forms.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Folate is the generic term for a large family of chemically similar compounds known as vitamin B9. Folic acid is a synthetic form of folate used to fortify foods and in supplements. 

- Methylfolate is the active form of folate. After ingestion, both dietary folate and synthetic folic acid need to undergo a complex conversion via a multistep pathway in the liver to their active form. Folic acid itself has no biological functions unless it is reduced to dihydrofolate and tetrahydrofolate. Folate from animal sources is present in a ‘free form’ and is readily absorbed, but folate in plants exists in conjugated forms which require deconjugation by zinc-dependent enzymes in the gut prior to absorption. 

- Methylfolate is the active form of folate in the body and accounts for approximately 98% of folates in human plasma. Supplemental methylfolate is directly available and does not need to be metabolised. 

- Activated Folate 500 helps prevent dietary folate deficiency. Studies comparing methylfolate and folic acid supplementation have found the two compounds to be comparable in physiological activity, bioavailability and absorption at equimolar doses[1] . However, there is some evidence that methylfolate may be more effective than folic acid in improve folate status. A double-blind, randomised, placebocontrolled study investigated the effect of supplementing with folic acid and methylfolate and measured the resulting increase on red blood cell folate concentration, an indicator of folate status. The increase in red blood cell folate was significantly higher in the group receiving methylfolate than the group receiving the same dose of folic acid (p=0.001)[2] . 

## Quatrefolic[®] 

- Activated Folate 500 contains methylfolate as Quatrefolic[®] , the glucosamine salt of (6S)-5-methyltetrahydrofolate. Quatrefolic[®] is an active form of folate, immediately available for its biological action without being metabolised in the body. 

- Quatrefolic[®] has higher bioavailability than folic acid and is more bioavailable than other forms of methylfolate, including the calcium salt. Rat studies show that the glucosamine salt is 12% better absorbed than the calcium salt[3] . A crossover study comparing the bioavailability of a single oral dose of 400mcg of folate as glucosamine salt (Quatrefolic[®] ) to the calcium salt in healthy adults found that Quatrefolic[®] had 10% higher bioavailability[4] . 

## Functions of folate 

- Folate is essential for cell growth and replication. Without folate, living cells cannot divide. Folate-containing coenzymes are essential to the 

production of DNA and RNA in growing and dividing cells. Rapidly dividing cells, such as blood cells and cells lining the digestive tract, are particularly dependent on folate. Folate helps maintain red blood cell health. 

- Folate helps the body metabolise proteins. 

- Activated Folate 500 supports brain health, cognitive function and memory. In a study of 100 adults with mild cognitive impairment and 121 normal adults, folate intake was positively associated with the Word List Memory Test and Constructional Recall Test scores[5] . 

- Activated Folate 500 helps support emotional wellbeing. Quatrefolic[®] crosses the blood-brain barrier and enters the central nervous system where it sustains the release of neurotransmitters including serotonin, norepinephrine and dopamine. 

## Cardiovascular health & homocysteine 

- Methylfolate is well studied for its ability to lower levels of homocysteine, a strong predictor of cardiovascular risk, and therefore contribute to cardiovascular health. Increased homocysteine is a risk factor for adverse cardiovascular events and adverse pregnancy outcomes. 

- Methionine, an amino acid from dietary protein, is converted to homocysteine in the body. As homocysteine is a toxic metabolite, the body remethylates homocysteine back to methionine via an enzyme methionine synthase, which requires methylfolate as the methyl donor and vitamin B12 as a cofactor[6] . 

- A double-blind, randomised, controlled intervention trial in 144 females compared 2 doses of methylfolate (208 micrograms or 406 micrograms) with 400 micrograms of folic acid for their ability to lower homocysteine levels during 24 weeks of supplementation. Homocysteine levels decreased in a similar amount in all three supplemental groups (p<0.001) and the authors concluded that methylfolate is an adequate alternative to folic acid in reducing homocysteine concentrations[7] .

## MTHFR 

- Methylene-tetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) is an enzyme that converts folate into its active form. Several polymorphisms, or gene variations, exist which can affect folate metabolism and significantly increase the risk of folate deficiency in affected individuals, even when meeting the recommended daily intakes. 

## **COMPANION PRODUCTS** 

   - Activated Sublingual B12 

   - Hawthorn 4500 

   - Pregnancy Plus 1-2-3 

   - Ubiquinol 150mg 

- The most common mutation is the MTHFR C677T mutation. Individuals who are heterozygote (one copy of the gene) for the MTHFR C677T mutation (2-16% white population)[9] have a 40% reduction in activity of the MTHFR enzyme and individuals who are homozygote (two copies of the gene) have a 70% reduction in activity. Lower levels of MTHFR enzyme reduces the production of methylfolate and is the most common risk factor for both high homocysteine and neural tube defects, since increased plasma homocysteine causes a delay in the closure of the neural tube and thus indirectly NTD. If the mother is a homozygote for this mutation, the risk of NTD is 2-fold; if both mother and foetus are homozygotes, the risk of NTD increases 6- to 7-fold[10] . 

- In people with MTHFR polymorphisms, methylfolate appears to be the supplement of choice as it does not require conversion. 

## Vitamin B12 

- High dose supplementation of folic acid can delay the appearance of the haematological symptoms of a B12 deficiency. Methylfolate is advantageous as it does not mask a vitamin B12 deficiency and thus B12 deficiency is more likely to be diagnosed and treated.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Alpha Lipoic acid is a powerful antioxidant that regenerates other antioxidants, including vitamin E, vitamin C and reduced glutathione, and has metal-chelating activity. Both fat and water soluble, it is readily absorbed from the gut and crosses cellular and blood-brain membrane barriers. 

- Antioxidants are molecules that inhibit oxidation of other molecules. Oxidation is a chemical reaction that can produce free radicals in the body. These free radicals can start a chain reaction that potentially leads to damage within DNA, proteins and lipids in cell membranes. 

- Direct antioxidants bind directly to a free radical, whereas indirect antioxidants recycle direct antioxidants and help cells produce antioxidant enzymes. Alpha Lipoic acid can directly and indirectly scavenge free radicals in the body. 

- Alpha Lipoic acid contains an asymmetric carbon molecule, meaning it can exist as one of two possible optical isomers, also called enantiomers. These enantiomers are mirror images of each other and exist as R-Lipoic acid and S-Lipoic acid. Alpha Lipoic 300 contains a mixture of 50% R and 50% S-Lipoic acid (R,S-alpha Lipoic acid). Almost twice as much R-alpha-Lipoic acid is absorbed as the S-alpha-Lipoic acid with oral supplementation. Combining S-Lipoic acid with R-Lipoic acid helps with the absorption. 

## Energy production 

- Alpha Lipoic 300 supports energy production. It is an essential cofactor for coenzyme complexes involved in energy production, playing a role in carbohydrate metabolism in the mitochondrial citric acid cycle to produce adenosine triphosphate (ATP). 

## Glucose uptake 

- Alpha Lipoic 300 helps support the cellular uptake of glucose. Alpha Lipoic acid plays a key role in the citric acid cycle, acting as a coenzyme for pyruvate and a-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase to regulate glucose metabolism and regulates insulin sensitivity. 

## Nerve health 

- Alpha Lipoic 300 supports nervous system function and nerve health. Due to the potent antioxidant effect of alpha Lipoic acid, it can reduce free radical damage to the peripheral nerves. 

- A double-blind, randomised trial compared the effects of alpha Lipoic acid (ALA) to acetyl L-carnitine (ALC) on 64 individuals with sciatic nerve pain associated with a herniated disc. Participants in group 1 (n=33) received ALC 1180mg/day; participants in group 2 (n=31) received ALA 600mg/day for 60 days. Both groups experienced significant improvements in neuropathic symptoms, however, ALA was statistically superior to ALC[1] . 

- A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial examined the effect of 600mg, 1200mg and 1800mg/day of ALA in 181 patients with polyneuropathy. Significant improvements in stabbing and burning pain were noted in all ALA groups after 5 weeks of administration. The 

mechanisms of the rapid improvement may be related to improved nerve flow mediated by the antioxidant action of ALA[2] . 

## Blood vessel health 

- Alpha Lipoic 300 maintains blood vessel health. 

- Blood vessels are lined with vascular endothelial cells which form the physical barrier between blood and the vessel wall and play a role in vasodilation and constriction. 

- The elasticity of the vessel wall is regulated by nitric oxide (NO) which is produced by endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS). Loss of eNOS activity causes endothelial dysfunction leading to decreased vasodilation and vascular inflammation. 

- Alpha Lipoic acid can significantly improve endothelial function, increase NO synthesis and prevents loss of eNOS phosphorylation to support healthy vasodilation[3] . 

## Mild migraines 

- In a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 54 migraine patients with and without aura were given 600mg/day of ALA for 3 months. The group receiving ALA reported a reduction in migraine attack frequency, headache days and headache severity compared to placebo[4] . 

- In an open-label cohort study, 32 people suffering from migraines received 400mg of ALA twice daily for 6 months, in addition to ongoing treatment. A significant reduction was seen in the number of attacks. One potential mechanism by which ALA may reduce migraine attacks is via its potent antioxidant effect, as migraines have been linked to oxidative stress[5] . 

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Caution with hypoglycaemic medication - alpha Lipoic acid may have an additive effect. Monitor blood sugar levels. 

- Alpha Lipoic acid has metal chelating activity - separate dose from copper, zinc and manganese by 3 hours. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- Caution using high doses or long-term during pregnancy due to a lack of safety data. Alpha Lipoic acid has been used safely during pregnancy at doses up to 600mg daily for up to 4 weeks. 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- None noted at the recommended dose.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Astra Recharge is a combination of herbs, including high-strength Astragalus and the mushroom Reishi. This unique formula supports recovery from illness, targeting the multi-faceted symptom picture of debility, low energy, poor immune health and brain fog as well as increased stress and poor sleep. 

- Astra Recharge is suitable to be used either during the winter months following illness, or at any time during the year to support recovery from general debility and fatigue and in times of high stress. 

- Astra Recharge contains Holixer™, a clinically studied extract of Ocimum tenuiflorum (Holy basil), to relieve the symptoms of stress, promote body adaptation to stress and improve sleep quality. 

- Astra Recharge also contains the mushroom Reishi. Reishi is listed among the superior tonics in the oldest surviving Chinese materia medica and has been considered “the mushroom of immortality” in China, Japan, Korea and other Asian countries for more than 4000 years. 

## Immune health 

- Astra Recharge contains Astragalus, Siberian ginseng and Reishi, supporting immune system health and healthy immune system function. 

- Astragalus and its saponins have immune-modulating activity by stimulating macrophage activity and enhancing B- and T-cell activity[1] . 

- Siberian ginseng is a medicinal plant originating from Russia, northern areas of Korea, Japan and China, and grows naturally in the wild in the cold to moderate climates of East Asia. Typically, the root of the plant is used, containing the active constituents eleutherosides A-M, which are chemically distinct glycosides. Siberian ginseng supports immune health by increasing T-helper cells and natural killer (NK) cell activity[2] . 

- Siberian ginseng supports recovery from illness. It is used as a tonic to either prevent the body from becoming run-down, or to restore it to a better state of wellbeing following a period of illness. 

- Reishi contains both polysaccharides and β-glucans, known to have strong immunomodulating action, including the activation of immune effector cells such as T cells, macrophages and NK cells[3] . 

- Reishi also has a long history of use in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) to reduce excess mucus, loosen chest phlegm and relieve cough. 

- Schisandra is considered one of the 50 fundamental herbs of TCM, used traditionally to reduce and relieve cough. 

## General debility and mental clarity 

- General debility is a state of general weakness or fragility that may be a result of either illness, stress or poor sleep. General debility is often accompanied by a melting pot of symptoms including low energy levels, weariness or fatigue, poor concentration, focus and mental clarity and poor immune health. 

- Astra Recharge supports mental concentration, focus and clarity, which can be beneficial for individuals experiencing brain fog, either because of recent infection or from general debility. 

- Siberian ginseng has been approved by the Commission E for use in times of fatigue and debility, declining capacity for work or concentration, and during convalescence[4] . Similarly, the World Health Organisation (WHO) recommend Siberian ginseng as a restorative tonic for enhancement of mental and physical capacities in cases of weakness, exhaustion and tiredness and during convalescence[5] . 

- A randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, crossover study found that 625mg of Siberian ginseng twice daily significantly improved selective memory, cognitive function and wellbeing over 3 months compared to placebo (p<0.02). Individuals taking Siberian ginseng also noted improvements in wellbeing and levels of physical activity[6] . 

## Stress 

- Astra Recharge contains selected herbs, including Astragalus and Siberian ginseng, to support a healthy stress response in the body.

- Siberian ginseng is considered an adrenal adaptogen, reducing the extent of the fight or flight reaction, ultimately reducing the exhaustive effects of long-term stress[1] . 

- Russian studies on Schisandra’s adaptogenic effects have been performed since the 1950s in athletes, telegraphists, airline attendants and soldiers. In one study, Schisandra was shown to increase adaptive capability of flight attendants carrying out long, non-stop flight (seven to nine hours)[2] .    - Vitamin C 1000 Plus 

   - Vitamin D3 1000 

- The WHO recommend Schisandra as a general tonic for treating fatigue associated with illness[4] . 

- Astra Recharge also contains the proprietary ingredient Holixer™ to relieve the symptoms of stress and promote sleep quality. 

- Holixer™ was clinically studied in 100 healthy male and female volunteers aged 18–65 years in an 8-week, two-arm, parallel-group, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. Prior to the study participants had been experiencing both stress for longer than a month and sleep problems. Participants received either 125mg of Holixer™ twice daily, or placebo and were evaluated using validated self-reporting questionnaires. 

- Compared to placebo, Holixer™ supplementation was associated with a 37% reduction in perceived stress as assessed by the Perceived Stress Score (PSS) (p=0.003), while at week 8 concentrations in hair cortisol were 66% lower than the control group receiving placebo. 

- In addition, supplementation with Holixer[TM ] was associated with a buffered stress response in acute stress, as demonstrated by significantly lower concentrations in salivary cortisol (p=0.001) and salivary amylase (p=0.001). 

- In relation to sleep, there was a statistically significant 48% decrease in the Athens Insomnia Scores from baseline to week 8 (p=0.010)[5] . 

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Contraindicated with sirolimus - Schisandra increases concentrations in the blood which increases the risk of adverse effects. 

- Caution with immunosuppressant medication given the immune stimulating nature of the formula. 

- Caution with drugs metabolised by the CYP3A4 enzyme - Schisandra may potentiate the effects. Monitor. 

- Caution with midazolam (benzodiazepine) - Schisandra increases the amount of drug in the body, increasing the risk of side effects. 

- Caution with heart or blood pressure medications, including Digoxin - concurrent use with Siberian ginseng may increase drug effects. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- Contraindicated during pregnancy and breastfeeding as specific safety data is lacking. 

- Astragalus is not recommended for use during the acute stage of an infection. 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- Reishi and Schisandra may cause mild gastrointestinal discomfort such as abdominal discomfort, heartburn, gastric discomfort, nausea, dyspepsia, flatulence or bloating in sensitive individuals. 

- Some reports of potential blood pressure increase have been documented in hypertensive patients when using Siberian ginseng. However, a causal relationship to the use of Siberian ginseng has not been established.

- B Sustained Release contains therapeutic doses of all 8 B vitamins including B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B12, biotin (B7) and folic acid (B9), as well as choline, inositol and vitamin C. 

   - Vitamin B5, commonly called the anti-stress vitamin, is involved in the synthesis of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine. Acetylcholine plays an important role in adrenal function and is required for the proper functioning of the adrenal cortex and the synthesis of steroid hormones, namely cortisone. 

- B Sustained Release is specifically formulated to slowly release nutrients into the digestive tract in a continuous manner over an extended period of time, rather than all at once. 

- B vitamins perform essential, inter-related roles in the body to enable cellular functioning, as well as acting as co-enzymes in a vast array of catabolic and anabolic enzymatic reactions. Their most important role is to convert carbohydrates, protein and fat into energy. 

   - Vitamin B6 is involved in the conversion of tryptophan to niacin, the synthesis of GABA in the central nervous system as well as the metabolism of serotonin, norepinephrine and dopamine. 

   - Folic acid and vitamin B12 play an important role in the development, differentiation and functioning of the CNS through methionine-homocysteine metabolism. Methionine is activated to S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe), which is indispensable for the synthesis of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA), proteins, neurotransmitters and hormones. 

- Choline and inositol are both members of the B vitamin family. Choline is necessary for the structure and function of cells and inositol is involved in the transport and metabolism of fats. 

- B vitamins are not synthesised by the body and therefore must be taken through the diet. 

- Typically, B vitamins are synthesised by plants, however, humans obtain most of their B vitamins from higher up the food chain in foods of animal origin, such as meat, dairy and eggs. 

   - Serotonin and dopamine are neurotransmitters that play a role in an individual’s mood and well-being. Dopamine plays a role in emotional responses, while serotonin contributes to feelings of wellbeing and happiness. 

- B vitamins are water soluble, meaning the body is unable to store them in large amounts. As such, regular daily intake is required to support general health. 

   - Specifically, vitamin B12 is essential for the proper functioning and development of the brain and nerve cells. It is required for the myelin sheath that covers and protects the nerves of the central and the peripheral nervous system, ensuring fast and effective nerve-impulse transmission. 

- B vitamins work synergistically in the body, so are best taken together. 

- Several factors increase the requirements for B vitamins, including dietary choices, pregnancy, certain medications and alcohol use. 

- Vitamin C supports a healthy stress response in the body and plays a crucial role in adrenal function. The adrenal glands contain the highest concentration of vitamin C in the body. 

## Energy production 

- B Sustained Release supports energy production. The B vitamins collectively function as coenzymes involved in mitochondrial energy production, supporting normal digestion and the conversion of food into energy. 

## Cardiovascular health 

   - B Sustained Release maintains cardiovascular system health and blood health. 

- B vitamins are essential for the proper functioning of the Krebs cycle in the mitochondria. The Krebs cycle is responsible for producing adenosine triphosphate (ATP), the primary energy carrier in all cells. 

- Vitamins B6, B12 and folic acid are required for homocysteine metabolism and assist the conversion of homocysteine to methionine. High homocysteine levels are associated with a higher risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. 

## Nervous system health 

- B Sustained Release supports healthy nervous system function. 

   - Vitamins B6, B12 and folic acid are important for the production of red blood cells, cell growth and cell reproduction. Vitamins B6 and B12 are also required for the synthesis of haemoglobin, the oxygencarrying pigment in red blood cells. 

- Vitamins B1, B5, B6, B12 and folic acid play an important role in the synthesis of neurotransmitters to support the function and health of the nervous system.

- Vitamin C is a co-factor in enzymes directly involved in the synthesis of collagen, while also providing antioxidant protection against UVinduced photodamage. Vitamin C is actively accumulated into the epidermal and dermal cells of the skin. 

## Cognitive function 

- B Sustained Release contains high-strength folic acid and vitamin B12 to support cognitive function and brain health. 

- More than 77 cross-sectional studies including more than 34 000 subjects have reported a significant association between low blood levels of folate and vitamin B12 and poor cognitive function[1] . 

## Pregnancy 

- B Sustained Release is suitable in pregnancy and breastfeeding to help meet the increased nutritional demands. It provides a daily dose of 400 micrograms of folic acid which, if taken daily for one month before conception and during the first trimester of pregnancy, helps to prevent neural tube defects such as spina bifida and anencephaly. 

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Contraindicated with pyrimethamine (antimalarial) – folate may reduce drug effectiveness. 

- Caution with tetracycline antibiotics - concurrent administration with B2 and B12 may decrease the effectiveness of the medication. Separate dose by 2 hours. 

- Caution with chloramphenicol (broad spectrum antibiotic) – folic acid and B12 may impact drug metabolism. Separate dose by 2 hours. 

- Caution with anticholingeric drugs - these drugs reduce the absorption of vitamin B2. Separate dose. 

- Caution with carbamazepine and primidone – vitamin B3 and folate may impact drug metabolism, resulting in increased drug levels in the body. Monitor use. 

- Caution with amiodarone – vitamin B6 may increase the risk of drug induced photosensitivity. Separate doses by at least 2 hours. 

- Caution with levodopa – vitamin B6 may reduce drug effects. However, this effect is prevented by the administration of a dopadecarboxylase inhibitor (e.g. benserazide, carbidopa) with levodopa, as is common clinical practice. 

- Caution with phenobarbital/phenobarbitone and phenytoin (anticonvulsants) - vitamin B6 and folate may reduce serum concentrations of these drugs. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- B vitamins are stimulatory in nature. To avoid any sleep interference, avoid taking before bed. 

- Taking at night may result in more vivid dreams (vitamin B6). 

- Caution if there is a history of renal calculi (kidney stones) - vitamin C (ascorbic acid) may increase the risk of recurrence of calcium oxalate calculi. 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- Supplemental B vitamins may cause nausea or mild gastrointestinal upset if taken on an empty stomach. Best taken with food to reduce the risk. 

- Riboflavin can impart a bright yellow colour to urine.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Berberine ImmunoPlex provides a blend of herbs standardised to contain 109.26mg berberine per tablet from Phellodendron and Barberry. 

   - In vitro studies have shown berberine has antifungal activity against Candida spp. and Cryptococcus neoformans strains, possibly by altering mitochondrial membranes and reducing biofilm formation[6] . 

- Berberine is an isoquinoline plant alkaloid that belongs to the structural class of protoberberines. Protoberberine alkaloids include berberine (the major alkaloid), jatrorrhizine, palmatine, columbamine. Berberine represents one of the most studied among the naturally occurring protoberberine alkaloids[1] . 

   - Berberine extracts have demonstrated in vitro growth inhibition of Giardia lamblia, Trichomonas vaginalis and Leishmania donovani[7, 8] . 

   - A recent 2020 systematic review and meta analyses of 13 clinical trials showed that the addition of berberine to standard triple therapy improved the eradication rate of Helicobacter pylori, with improved symptom remission rate, accelerated ulcer healing and reduced adverse events in groups using berberine at doses ranging between 120-500mg[9] . 

- Berberine has a distinctive yellow colour and bitter flavour and is naturally found in the bark, roots and rhizomes of various medicinal plants including Phellodendron, Barberry, Indian barberry, Golden seal and Chinese goldthread. 

- Berberine ImmunoPlex also contains Pau d’arco, a well-known antifungal herb. Pau d’arco and its constituents lapachol and β-lapachone have demonstrated in vitro activity against various Candida species including Candida albicans and Candida tropicalis[10] . Bark extracts of Pau d’arco have also shown broad-spectrum activity in vitro, specifically active against most fungal strains[11] . 

## Antimicrobial 

- The stem bark of Phellodendron and Barberry contain isoquinoline alkaloids, including berberine, the primary active constituent responsible their pharmacological activity. 

- Phellodendron is traditionally used in Chinese medicine to ‘dispel and remove heat toxins’ and ‘detoxify and disinfect’. It is traditionally used for infections due to the presence of berberine. 

   - The mechanism of action may involve interference with the fungal cell membrane[12] . Napthoquinones, active components in Pau d’arco, are inhibitors of the electron chain transport and acts by uncoupling oxidative phosphorylation, thus inhibiting ATP synthesis in the fungal cell. 

- In vitro research shows that berberine has antimicrobial effects including antibacterial and antifungal activity[2,3] . It has shown in vitro antibacterial activity against a wide variety of microorganisms including Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, fungi and protozoa[4] . 

   - Several constituents found in Pau d’arco have also demonstrated antibacterial activity in vitro, including lapachol, β-lapachone and anthraquinone-2-carboxylic acid. These isolated compounds have shown activity against Helicobacter pylori, Clostridium perfringens, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Streptococcus faecalis, Enterococcus and Bacillus species, and various strains of Staphylococcus aureus[13,14] . 

- Preliminary research suggests berberine might inhibit bacterial sortase, a protein responsible for anchoring Gram-positive bacteria to cell membranes[5] .

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Cholesterol is a fat-like substance that is naturally produced by the body and found in the diet in eggs and animal products that are rich in fat, such as meats and full-fat dairy foods. 

- Cholesterol is essential for many of the body’s metabolic processes, including the production of hormones (oestrogen, testosterone and adrenal hormones) and vitamin D and is necessary for the structure of cell membranes and to produce bile acid, to digest fat. It is not necessary to consume cholesterol in the diet as the body can produce sufficient cholesterol to meet its needs. 

- Cholesterol is transported around the body in the blood attached to lipoproteins. There are two main types of lipoproteins: low-density lipoprotein (LDL) and high-density lipoprotein (HDL). LDL (considered ‘bad’ cholesterol) carries most of the cholesterol that is delivered to cells, while HDL (‘good’ cholesterol) helps remove excess cholesterol out of the cells, including cells in the arteries. Too much LDL in the bloodstream can lead to the development of fatty deposits in the arteries, causing narrowing of the blood vessels. 

- Bergamot Cholesterol Care helps maintain healthy cholesterol and supports cardiovascular system health. 

## Bergamot 

- Citrus aurantium (Bergamot) is a natural hybrid fruit derived from bitter orange and lemon, indigenous to Calabria, Italy. Essential oil obtained from the peel is used for its fragrant properties and provides the classic bergamot aroma associated with Earl Grey tea. 

- Bergamot has a unique composition of flavonoids, including neoeriocitrin, neohesperidin, naringin, melitidin and brutieridin, that are potent antioxidants and believed to be responsible for the fruit’s pharmacological effects. Citrus aurantium has the highest concentration of flavonoids compared to other citrus fruits[1] . 

- Bergamot Cholesterol Care contains 500mg of Citrus aurantium extract, equivalent to 75g fresh fruit juice, with 132.5mg of flavonoids per tablet. 

- Bergamot helps maintain healthy cholesterol. The exact mechanism of action is not clear, however, it is likely due to multiple mechanisms. Several flavonoids in Bergamot, including naringin, can activate AMPK, the central regulator of lipid and glucose metabolism. AMPK facilitates glucose uptake and prevents the accumulation of fat by modulating downstream-signalling components, such as acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC) and HMG-CoA reductase[2] . 

- Polyphenols in Bergamot, including naringin, melitidin and brutieridin, also act as HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, mimicking the action of statins and blocking the rate-limiting step in cholesterol synthesis. 

- Animal and human studies provide evidence of bergamot’s cholesterol-lowering effect. In one study, rats fed a typical Western diet high in fat and sugar for 6 months showed a 5-fold increase in fasting plasma triglyceride and an 8-fold increase in cholesterol levels compared with chow-fed rats. The addition of naringenin (naringin aglycon) to the diet significantly decreased total cholesterol and triglycerides by 50% and reduced atherosclerotic lesions by more than 70%[3] . 

- A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in 237 patients with hyperlipemia found that 500mg or 1000mg of Bergamot extract daily for 30 days inhibited HMG-CoA reductase activity, significantly reduced total cholesterol, LDL and triglycerides and moderately increased HDL[4] . 

- Bergamot has also been found to enhance the effects of statins. One study found that the addition of Bergamot to rosuvastatin significantly enhanced the rosuvastatin-induced effect on serum lipemic profile compared to rosuvastatin alone[5] . 

## Globe artichoke 

- Globe artichoke has a long history of use, dating back to ancient Greece and Rome. Traditionally, it is used in Western herbal medicine as a liver tonic, choleretic and cholagogue to increase bile flow. 

- The leaf contains phenolic acids, mainly caffeic acid derivatives (e.g. chlorogenic acid, cynarin), sesquiterpenes, lactones and flavonoids, phytosterols, inulin and free luteolin. 

- Animal studies have found that artichoke leaf extract can lower cholesterol, possibly by indirect modulation of HMA-CoA reductase activity. 

- A study in hamsters found that artichoke leaf extract significantly lowered total cholesterol by 15%, non-HDL cholesterol by 30% and triglycerides by 25% compared to controls[6] . 

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Caution with cholesterol-lowering medication – may have additive effects. 

- Caution with hypoglycaemic medication – may have additive effects. 

- Caution with colchicine (used in Gout) – Bergamot has been found to cause a small decrease in blood concentrations of the drug. 

- Caution with dextromethorphan (decongestant/antitussive) – Bergamot may increase drug absorption, which may increase the risk of side effects.

- Curcumin is the main active component found in Turmeric, present in concentrations between 3-5% and gives Turmeric its distinctive yellow colour. 

- Turmeric has a long history of use in Ayurvedic medicine as an anti-inflammatory and anti-arthritic. Its traditional use has been supported by scientific studies, showing curcumin to be responsible for the anti-inflammatory and anti-arthritic activity of Turmeric. 

- Curcuminoids are the active phenolic compounds in Turmeric. A mixture of three curcuminoids exist in Turmeric: monomolecular curcumin, demethoxycurcumin and bisdemethoxycurcumin, although these are collectively referred to as curcumin. 

- Meriva[®] curcumin is a clinically trialled curcumin formulation with improved bioavailability for enhanced absorption. Meriva[®] is comprised of these three curcuminoids to reflect the most typical ratio found in nature.

## Meriva[®] absorption 

- Curcumin is known to be poorly absorbed as it is only slightly soluble in water and is rapidly degraded at intestinal pH. 

- Bio Curcumin 5400 contains Meriva[®] curcumin, a patented phytosome delivery system where curcumin is bound to sunflower lecithin to create a phospholipid matrix. By embedding curcumin into a phospholipid complex, curcumin is shielded from water degradation and is stabilised in intestinal pH. The phospholipid matrix has a high affinity to cell membranes, increasing the cellular uptake of curcumin.

## Meriva[®] for mild arthritis 

- Meriva[®] curcumin relieves symptoms of mild arthritis at much lower doses than regular curcumin due to its superior bioavailability. Meriva[®] has been clinically trialled to increase joint mobility and reduce joint swelling, pain and inflammation associated with mild osteoarthritis. 

- A 3-month study evaluated the efficacy of Meriva[®] in 50 subjects affected by osteoarthritis (OA) confirmed by X-ray diagnosis. The subjects were randomly divided into two groups: group A received “the best available treatment” as recommended by the patients’ general practitioners or specialists, and group B received “the best available treatment” combined with 1g/day of Meriva[®] in two separate doses corresponding to 200mg curcumin per day. In the Meriva[®] group, the global WOMAC (Western Ontario and McMaster Universities) score decreased by 58%, with results showing a significant decrease in pain and stiffness. Increases in physical function at 2 months were observed, with further improvements at 3 months (p<0.05). Physical performance was improved in the Meriva[®] group as walking distance on the treadmill test was prolonged from 76m to 332m (p<0.05). A decrease in the inflammatory marker CRP was significant in both groups at 8 weeks, but the decrease in CRP was significantly greater in the Meriva[®] group. These positive results were complemented by secondary endpoints, namely the decrease in painkiller use (63% decrease in the Meriva[®] group vs 12% in the control group) and the decrease in gastrointestinal complications (69% decrease in Meriva[®] vs 15% in control)[2] . 

Figure 3. Effect of Meriva[®] on walking performance after 3 months of treatment. 

- A similar study design was used in an open, controlled study involving 100 individuals with OA conducted over an 8-month period. Subjects were divided into two groups: group A received “the best available treatment” as recommended by the patients’ general practitioners or specialists, and group B received “the best available treatment” combined with 1g/day of Meriva[®] . The study found statistically significant reductions in all markers of inflammation in the Meriva[®] group when compared to the control group. The results showed that the group treated with Meriva[®] experienced a statistically significant reduction in WOMAC scores that assessed pain, stiffness and physical function, with a decrease in non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAIDs) use and an overall improvement in quality of life[3] .

- The two aformentioned studies conducted by Belcaro et al. (2010) on individuals with osteoarthritis measured the effect of Meriva[®] on inflammatory markers. Significant reductions were seen in inflammatory markers including IL-1B, IL-6, ESR and CRP. 

- An in-vivo animal study showed Meriva[®] was able to down regulate the expression of a series of cytokines, enzymes and transcription factors involved in the inflammatory response. Gene expression was measured at baseline and after 4, 8 and 15 days of Meriva[®] administration in horses. Meriva[®] curcumin significantly inhibited the expression of COX-2, TNF-a, IL-1B and IL-6[5] .

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Biotin, also known as vitamin B7, forms part of the B vitamin family. Biotin is involved in cell growth, fatty acid production and in the metabolism of carbohydrates, fats and proteins. 

- Biotin is a water-soluble vitamin and is an essential cofactor for 5 carboxylase enzymes including: 

- Acetyl-coenzyme A (CoA) carboxylase 1 and acetyl-CoA carboxylase 2: binds bicarbonate to acetyl-CoA to form malonylCoA, required for the production of fatty acids. 

- Pyruvate carboxylase: critical for gluconeogenesis (formation of glucose from sources other than carbohydrates such as amino acids and fats). 

- Methylcrotonyl-CoQ carboxylase: essential step in the metabolism of the amino acid leucine. 

- Propionyl-CoA carboxylase: catalyses essential steps in the metabolism of amino acids, cholesterol and odd chain fatty acids. 

- Many foods contain small amounts of biotin and this depends greatly on the season. Foods that contain the most biotin include organ meats, eggs, fish, meat, seeds, nuts and certain vegetables including sweet potato. 

- Gastrointestinal enzymes break down the protein-bound forms of ingested biotin, which then undergo further processing by the enzyme biotinidase in the intestinal lumen to release free biotin. The free biotin is then absorbed in the small intestine and most biotin is stored in the liver and central nervous system. 

- A diet high in raw egg whites can lead to a biotin deficiency. Raw egg whites are high in avidin, a protein that binds to biotin and inhibits its absorption. Cooking denatures avidin, making it unable to interfere with biotin absorption. 

- Signs and symptoms of biotin deficiency include skin rashes, brittle nails, thinning hair or hair loss. 

- Pregnancy increases biotin requirements as the fetus requires biotin for carboxylase reactions and DNA replication. 

## Hair, skin & nails 

- Biotin 3mg supports hair, skin and nail health. It plays a role in the normal structure and function of skin and mucous membranes. Biotin is a coenzyme for carboxylase enzymes that are involved in fatty acid synthesis, branched-chain amino acid catabolism and gluconeogenesis, important for maintenance of healthy skin and hair.

- In one study, 71 subjects with brittle fingernails were given 2.5mg of biotin per day. Out of the 45 subjects that completed the study, 91% showed a definite improvement with firmer and harder fingernails after an average treatment of 5.5±2.3 months[1] . 

- Another study investigated the effects of 2.5mg/day of biotin on brittle and splitting fingernails. A total of 32 subjects were placed into 3 groups: group A was the control (n=10), group B comprised subjects with brittle nails (n=8) studied before and after biotin supplementation, and group C included subjects with brittle nails in whom the administration of biotin did not coincide exactly with the initial and terminal clipping of the nails (n=14). The thickness of the nails in group B increased significantly by 25% and group C by 7%. Splitting of the nails were reduced in groups B and C and the irregular cellular arrangement of the dorsal surface of brittle nails became more regular in all nails of group B and in 8 of 11 nails of group C. Results were seen after 6 to 15 months of biotin supplementation[2] .

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Breastfeeding Support contains two herbs, Fenugreek and Blessed thistle, to support milk supply in breastfeeding women. 

- Fenugreek and Blessed thistle are herbal galactagogues. A galactagogue is a substance that promotes the secretion and flow of milk. 

- A 2015 qualitative study found that Fenugreek and Blessed thistle were the two most commonly used herbal galactagogues[1] . 

## Breastfeeding 

- During pregnancy, breasts change and develop to be ready to supply milk. The amount of breastmilk usually increases a few days after the birth, when the milk “comes in”. 

- The first milk produced after the birth is called colostrum, which is more concentrated than mature milk and rich in protein and antibodies. It is gradually replaced by mature milk. 

- When a baby sucks at the breast, it stimulates nerves in the nipple that release hormones into the blood stream. Prolactin activates milkmaking tissues, while oxytocin causes the breast to let down the milk (“let-down reflex”). 

- Breastmilk is the normal food for babies, containing all the baby’s nutritional needs for the first 6 months of life, satisfying both hunger and thirst, and supporting the baby’s immune system. The act of breastfeeding also helps the baby’s jaw development. Breastfeeding benefits the mother by helping the uterus return to its normal size after childbirth. 

- One of the most common reasons mothers cease breastfeeding earlier than planned is because they feel they don’t have enough milk for their babies. 

## Fenugreek 

- Fenugreek is a herb native to the Mediterranean region, southern Europe and western Asia. It is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine as a nutritive tonic and galactagogue to increase breastmilk production in breastfeeding women. 

- The mechanism of action of Fenugreek on breastmilk is not fully understood, but it is suggested that Fenugreek stimulates sweat production, which then enhances milk secretion because the breast is a type of sweat gland. Fenugreek may also have oestrogenic activity. 

- Fenugreek also supports healthy appetite. 

## Blessed thistle 

- Blessed thistle supports breastmilk production in breastfeeding women. It is believed to work by stimulating the flow of blood to the mammary glands, thereby enriching milk flow. 

- Blessed thistle is a weed native to the Mediterranean that has been used for over 2000 years to stimulate appetite, aid digestion and as a galactagogue. According to Grieves, “it is chiefly used now for nursing mothers the warm infusion scarcely ever failing to procure a proper supply of milk. It is considered one of the best medicines which can be used for the purpose”[4] . 

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Caution with warfarin and other anticoagulant or antiplatelet drugs - Fenugreek may affect blood coagulation (based on an isolated case report). Monitor. 

- Caution with hypoglycaemic drugs - Fenugreek may have additive effects. Monitor blood glucose. 

- Caution with iron - Fenugreek can inhibit iron absorption. Separate dose by 2 hours. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- Contraindicated in pregnancy - Fenugreek can cause uterine contractions, increasing the risk of early labour or miscarriage. 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- None noted at the recommended dose.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Bulgarian Tribulus Complex contains a combination of Bulgarian and Indian Tribulus. Tribulus is a popular widespread herb found in China, southern Europe, eastern Asia and extending into western Asia. It has a long history of use in traditional medicine systems, including Chinese and Ayurvedic medicine. 

- Tribulus terrestris is the most commonly supplemented species of the Tribulus genera. A variety of compounds are present at varying ratios depending on the plant part used. The fruits and root plant parts contain a mixture of different steroidal saponins. 

- Steroidal saponins are considered to be the most important constituent responsible for the biological activity of Tribulus. They consist of a furostanol or spirostanol-based aglycone and an oligosaccharide attached to a steroid nucleus. The main chemical components of the fruit are steroidal saponins, protodioscin, tribulosaponins A and B, tribulosin and terrestrosina A–K. 

- The main furostanol saponins in Tribulus are protodioscin and prototribestin. Protodioscin is a steroidal saponin commonly seen as the main active constituent of Tribulus, comprising 45% of most dry extracts. Levels of protodioscin are not consistent as it greatly depends on the soil in which Tribulus is grown. For this reason, standardised Tribulus formulations are important. 

- Bulgarian Tribulus Complex is a standardised formulation with a total saponin content of ≥40% and contains over 300mg of protodioscin per tablet.

## Osteoporosis 

- Osteoporosis is a condition where bones become brittle, occurring when bones lose minerals, such as calcium, more quickly than the body can replace them, causing a loss of bone density. It is the most common bone disease in humans and increases the risk of fractures. Osteoporosis often has no symptoms and may not be diagnosed until a fracture occurs. 

- After 30 years of age, bone mass begins to decline in both men and women. Bones are in a constant state of turn over, with old bone being broken down by osteoclasts (resorption) and new bone being built by osteoblasts (formation). Osteoporosis occurs when there is a significant imbalance between new bone formation and bone resorption. 

- Risk factors for osteoporosis include: 

- Low level of physical activity 

- Smoking 

- Excessive alcohol intake 

- Excess body weight 

- Family history of osteoporosis 

- Low calcium intake 

- Low vitamin D levels/lack of sun exposure 

- Being female 

- Early menopause 

- Osteoporosis is common in Australia, with 1.2 million people estimated to have osteoporosis and a further 6.3 million with low bone density[1] . 

- While both men and women are at risk of osteoporosis, postmenopausal women, in particular, are at greater risk due to the rapid decline of oestrogen during menopause. When oestrogen levels decrease, bones lose calcium and other minerals at a much faster 

rate. As a result, bone loss occurs at approximately 2% per year for several years after menopause. Men also lose bone as they age, however testosterone levels in men decline more gradually so their bone mass usually remains adequate until later in life[2] . 

## Calcium for bone health 

- Calcium is essential for building bone and maintaining bone strength and bone mineralisation. Ninety-nine percent of the body’s calcium is located in the bone matrix. The remaining 1% is found in the blood and other fluids, and is essential for regulation of heartbeat, muscle contraction, release of neurotransmitters, nerve signaling and blood clotting. 

- Calcium homoeostasis is tightly regulated by parathyroid hormone (PTH), calcitonin and vitamins K and D. These hormones and vitamins determine the level of calcium absorption, excretion or retention via the kidneys and control bone remodeling. 

- Calcium, with vitamin D3, maintains bone health and healthy teeth. Calcium is stored in the teeth and bones, where it provides structure and strength. 

- Calcium is especially important for post-menopausal women to support bone health. The Cochrane Collaboration assessed the effects of calcium on bone density and fractures in postmenopausal women. The review covered 15 trials representing 1806 participants and concluded that calcium had a positive effect on bone density and was more effective than placebo in reducing rates of bone loss after two or more years of treatment[3] .

- When the algae dies-off and breaks down, it settles naturally on the seabed floor where the calcified remains are harvested, washed, dried and milled. Aquamin[TM] is sustainably sourced, with each step of harvesting controlled to ensure future generations can benefit from the resource. Aquamin[TM] is tested for heavy metals and is GMO-free. 

- Aquamin[TM] has a unique porous structure, which provides a large surface area for absorption and makes it easier to digest and absorb.
