## Calcium citrate 

- Calcium citrate is an organic form of calcium bound to citrate that is highly soluble and offers greater bioavailability than other forms of calcium. An early meta-analysis compared the absorption of calcium citrate to commonly used calcium carbonate. The analysis covered 15 studies involving a total of 184 subjects and concluded that calcium citrate is better absorbed than calcium carbonate by approximately 22-27%, either on an empty stomach or co-administered with a meal[6] . 

- A randomised, crossover study compared the single-dose bioavailability of 500mg elemental calcium from calcium citrate or calcium carbonate administered with a meal. Calcium citrate resulted in a 94% higher change in area under the curve for serum calcium and a 41% greater increment in urinary calcium. The study concluded that calcium citrate is more bioavailable than calcium carbonate when given with a meal[7] . 

- Calcium citrate is the preferable form of calcium where there are low levels of stomach acid (achlorhydria), as calcium carbonate requires an acidic environment in order to be absorbed. Low levels of stomach acid are commonly seen in the elderly, as stomach acid production declines with age. It is also seen in those taking acid-suppressing medication, such as proton pump inhibitors. 

## Vitamin K2 

- There are two forms of vitamin K: K1 (phylloquinone) and K2 (menaquinone), and each have very different actions in the human body. Vitamin K1 is the major dietary source of vitamin K, accounting for approximately 90% of total vitamin K intake. It is found in green leafy vegetables, including broccoli, kale and spinach, however, the bioavailability from food is low, less than 20%. 

- Vitamin K2 is a group structurally similar fat-soluble vitamins, known as menaquinones (MK), that differ in their isoprenoid chain lengths. The most important are MK-4 and MK-7. MK-7 is found in fermented foods such as cheese, yoghurt and natto, a fermented soybean product commonly eaten in Japan. Typical Western diets are deficient in K2. MK-7 has a half-life of approximately 72 hours, so it remains biologically active in the body longer than MK-4, which has a half life of about 1.5 hours. 

- MK-7 exists in two forms: as a trans-isomer and cis-isomer. The all-trans compound is the bioactive component. Cis compounds are biologically inactive or have reduced activity. Vitamin K2 created by some fermentation processes contains a mix of cis and trans forms. K2VITAL[TM] Delta is synthesised to produce an all-trans MK-7. 

- Vitamin K2 is unstable in organic-alkaline environments and is particularly susceptible to degradation when combined with minerals, notably calcium and magnesium. K2VITAL[TM] Delta is microencapsulated to ensure stability. The encapsulation features two water dispersible coatings that make the K2 resistant to harsh environments. 

- Vitamin K2’s main role in the body is calcium distribution – it directs calcium into the bones where it is needed and keeps it away from arteries. Vitamin K2 supports bone health, bone strength and bone integrity. 

- Vitamin K2 stimulates osteoblastic bone formation and inhibits osteoclastic bone resorption. It is essential for the ɣ-carboxylation of osteocalcin, a calcium-binding protein which stimulates mineralisation in bone tissue. 

- A 24-month randomised open label study investigated the effects of vitamin K2, 45 micrograms/day with 150mg elemental calcium in preventing the incidence of new fractures in osteoporosis. The incidence of fractures was higher in the control group than in the vitamin K2 group [30% versus 10%, (p=0.0273)][8] . 

- A study compared no supplementation, vitamin D3 800IU/day with calcium 1200mg/day, and vitamin K2 45 micrograms with vitamin D3 and calcium (at the same dose). The study showed that adding vitamin K2 to calcium and vitamin D3 reduced the lifetime probability of at least one fracture by 25%[9] . 

- A cross-sectional analysis of 1662 community dwelling elderly Japanese men aged 65 or over found that subjects with greater intake of natto had significantly higher BMD and lower risk of low BMD at the total hip and femoral neck, believed to be a result of the vitamin K2 content in natto[10] . 

- Similarly, a study in postmenopausal women found that natto consumption was associated with higher serum concentrations of MK-7 and identified a statistically significant inverse correlation between the incidence of hip fractures and natto consumption, suggesting the possibility that higher MK-7 levels resulting from natto consumption may contribute to the relatively lower fracture risk in Japanese women[11] .

- Contraindicated with integrase inhibitors (e.g. dolutegravir, elvitegravir, raltegravir – HIV therapy) – calcium decreases drug serum levels.

- Caution with thiazide diuretics – drug decreases urinary excretion of calcium, potentially increasing risk of hypercalcaemia. Monitor serum calcium levels.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Pau d’arco, also known as Red Lapacho or Taheebo, is a canopy tree native to the Amazon rainforest and can be found in tropical regions of South and Central America. Pau d’arco has been used by native Americans of Brazil, northern Argentina, Paraguay and Peru for over 1000 years, with a long history of medicinal use that pre-dates the Incas. 

- The bark of the Pau d’arco tree is hard and durable and well-known for its resistance to insect and fungal attack. 

- Pau d’arco is traditionally used in South American medicine to relieve symptoms of mild, superficial fungal skin infections. Traditionally, the bark/heartwood of Pau d’arco was prepared as a decoction or herbal tea and was prescribed for many ailments including fevers, sore throats, dysentery and snakebites as well as used topically for wounds and skin conditions. 

- Pau d’arco is also traditionally used in South American medicine to support gastrointestinal system health. 

- The inner stem bark of Pau d’arco naturally contains bioactive compounds called naphthoquinones and furanonapthoquinones that contribute significantly to the therapeutic activity of the herb. 

- Two main bioactive components have been isolated from Pau d’arco: lapachol and β -lapachone. These are key constituents responsible for the antifungal and antibacterial activity of Pau d’arco. The majority of research has focused on the lapachol component, however, other napthoquinones and their furano derivatives are likely to contribute to the therapeutic activity of Pau d’arco. 

- Candida Relief contains Pau d’arco sourced from Brazil that has been HPLC tested for lapachol content to identify the plant species. Pau d’arco is commonly found to contain adulterants, so proper herbal identification and quality testing is essential. 

## Candida 

- Candida albicans (Candida) is a yeast-like fungus that normally inhabits the human microbiome, is present in small amounts on the skin and can be found in the mouth, digestive and reproductive tract. 

- Candida is a harmless, commensal yeast that exists in harmony with other yeasts and bacteria and is only considered a fungal pathogen when there is an overgrowth in certain areas of the body. 

- Candida overgrowth can lead to a condition called candidiasis. There are several types of candidiasis, the most common being: 

- Oral/oropharyngeal/oesophageal thrush: yeast infection in the mouth, throat and oesophageal area. Symptoms include white spots inside the mouth and on the tongue, redness, soreness and difficulty swallowing. 

- Genital thrush: most commonly experienced by women and characterised by extreme itching, soreness and redness in the vaginal area, accompanied by white clumpy vaginal discharge. 

- In men, the symptoms include a red rash on the penis and itching and burning on the tip of the penis. 

- A number of factors can lead to candida overgrowth including disruption to the pH of the environment, antibiotic use, a weakened immune system and immunosuppressants. 

## Antifungal activity 

- Pau d’arco supports healthy immune system function and relieves the symptoms of candida. Pau d’arco and its constituents lapachol and β -lapachone have demonstrated in vitro activity against various Candida species including Candida albicans and Candida tropicalis[1] . Bark extracts of Pau d’arco have also shown broad-spectrum activity in vitro, specifically active against most fungal strains[2] . 

- The mechanism of action may involve interference with the fungal cell membrane[3] . Napthoquinones are inhibitors of the electron transport chain and act by uncoupling oxidative phosphorylation, thus inhibiting ATP synthesis. 

- Several constituents found in Pau d’arco have also demonstrated antibacterial activity in vitro, including lapachol, β -lapachone and anthraquinone-2-carboxylic acid. These isolated compounds have shown activity against Helicobacter pylori, Clostridium perfringens, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Streptococcus faecalis, Enterococcus and Bacillus species, and various strains of Staphylococcus aureus[4,5] . 

- β -lapachone and other napthoquinone compounds have shown activity against methicillin-resistant staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), offering a potential synergistic effect with antimicrobial drugs[6] .

- May increase the risk of bleeding. Discontinue use 2 weeks prior to surgery.

## Bone development 

- Bone formation in children begins very early in development, at about the third week of foetal life. Cartilage is produced in the shape of the future bone, then during the second trimester of pregnancy this cartilage turns to bone and begins to form the child’s adult-like skeleton. During pregnancy and breastfeeding, bone development and growth is supported by the mother’s calcium levels. However, once a child moves to a diet of solid foods, their calcium requirements need to be met through their diet. 

- Skeletal development is most rapid in infancy, with bones growing and strengthening in childhood. Approximately 40% to 60% of adult bone mass is accrued during the adolescent years, with 25% of peak bone mass acquired during the 2-year period when a child experiences their peak height growth. This peak bone mineral growth rate occurs on average at 12.5 years for girls and 14 years for boys. At age 18 years, approximately 90% of peak bone mass has been accrued. Childhood and adolescence, therefore, are critical periods for skeletal mineralisation[1] . 

- Maintaining adequate calcium intake during childhood is necessary for the development of maximal peak bone mass. Increasing peak bone mass is recognised as an important way to reduce the risk of 

osteoporosis in later life[2] . 

- Calcium homeostasis is tightly regulated by parathyroid hormone, phosphorous, vitamin K2 and vitamin D. Together they determine the level of calcium absorption, excretion or retention via the kidneys and control the bone remodelling process in the developing skeleton. 

- In addition to calcium intake, exercise is an important aspect of achieving maximal peak bone mass. There is evidence that childhood and adolescence may represent an important period for achieving long-lasting skeletal benefits from regular exercise[3] . 

## Bone growth & bone health in children 

- Children’s Calci Care assists healthy bone development and supports bone mineralisation and density in children. 

- Children’s Calci Care contains calcium which is required for the normal development and maintenance of bone. 

- Over 90% of the bodies total calcium levels are found in bone. Calcium is an essential mineral for bone remodelling, a life-long process in which old bone is removed from the body and replaced with new bone. The bone remodelling process involves the constant addition of calcium to the bone and removal of calcium from the bone and into circulation. 

- Vitamin K2 is a fat-soluble vitamin, essential for calcium distribution in the body. Vitamin K2 is crucial for bone building and bone strength, as it incorporates or binds calcium into bones, whilst driving calcium away from blood vessels. 

- Vitamin K2 is a group of compounds, known as menaquinones (MKs). MK-7 has high rate of absorption and bioavailability and is only obtained in the Western diet through the intake of fermented foods. 

- Vitamin D facilitates calcium absorption by attaching to specific vitamin D receptors (VDR) on target cells responsible for the synthesis of different proteins involved in calcium transport and utilisation. 

## Muscle health & function in children 

   - Children’s Calci Care contains calcium and vitamin D, important nutrients for muscle health and muscle strength in children. 

   - The contraction and relaxation of muscles occurs due to rapidly changing calcium concentrations within the cells of muscles, a biochemical process known as the calcium cycle. Adequate calcium is required for a balanced calcium cycle, necessary for the healthy functioning of muscles.

- Children’s Immune Care is a herbal and nutritional formula containing Echinacea, developed for children to support a healthy immune system.

## Immune system health 

- Children’s Immune Care contains Echinacea, vitamins C and D and zinc to maintain immune system health and support the immune system to fight illness in children. It also contains citrus bioflavonoids to support the absorption of vitamin C. 

- Echinacea possesses immune modulating, stimulating and enhancing effects in the body. It appears to promote the activity of the white blood cells macrophages, natural killer cells and T-lymphocytes and increases the secretion of interleukin-1 (another important component of the immune system) to help fight infection. 

- Vitamin D3 is the bioactive form of vitamin D, important for a healthy immune system as it enhances the activity of white blood cells. 

- Zinc, vitamin C, bioflavonoids and Acerola all act as antioxidants in the body to reduce free radicals and support immune system health. 

## Respiratory tract infections & common colds & flu 

- Upper respiratory tract infections (URTIs) are highly prevalent in children as their immune systems are immature, not reaching the full level of maturity until somewhere between 12-14 years of age. On average, children have 6 to 8 URTIs per year while adults have only 2-3[1] . 

- Children’s Immune Care contains Echinacea, traditionally used in Western herbal medicine to reduce the occurrence of symptoms of URTIs and relieve the symptoms of common colds and flu, including upper respiratory tract congestion. 

- Echinacea root is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine as a diaphoretic to relieve mild fever. Diaphoretic herbs induce sweating in the body to reduce body temperature.

- may have an antagonistic effect (theoretical).

- increase the blood thinning effects. Separate dose by 4 hours.

- Caution in iron overload conditions, such as thalassaemia major, haemochromatosis or sideroblastic anaemia, as vitamin C can increase iron absorption. 

- Stop taking a week before any surgery. 

- In rare circumstances, Echinacea may cause worsening of asthma. Monitor.

- None noted at the recommended dose.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Children’s Magnesium Care contains organically bound forms of magnesium with high bioavailability in the body. 

- Magnesium is an essential nutrient for over 300 enzymatic processes in the body, required for DNA replication, energy production, muscle contraction and relaxation, cardiac rhythm, vascular tone, DNA and RNA synthesis, carbohydrate, protein and fat metabolism, bone formation, cell signalling, neurological function and brain function. 

- Magnesium is found in green leafy vegetables, nuts, seeds, whole grains and cacao. Today’s farming and agricultural practices have led to a decline in the magnesium content in foods, with estimates that magnesium content has decreased by as much as 80-90% in vegetables such as lettuce and spinach[1] . 

- Fussy eating habits, food allergies or food intolerances can mean a child isn’t obtaining the recommended intake of magnesium each day. 

- Children’s Magnesium Care contains a therapeutic dose of 80mg of elemental magnesium per chewable tablet, helping to boost a child’s magnesium intake in order to meet recommended daily intakes. 

- Children’s Magnesium Care contains tooth friendly xylitol. Xylitol is a natural sweetener found mainly in fibrous fruits and vegetables. While sugar has a glycaemic index of 100, xylitol has a glycaemic index of 7, so it has a negligible effect on blood sugar levels. Xylitol is alkalising which creates an unfriendly environment for bacteria detrimental to tooth enamel. 

- Children’s Magnesium Care is suitable for children aged 4 years and up and can be used to support energy production, muscle, bone and nervous system health in growing children. 

## Energy production 

- Children’s Magnesium Care supports energy production in children. Magnesium is involved in the metabolism of carbohydrates and fats to produce energy and is critical for the manufacture of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) within cells. 

- Between the age of three years old and middle adolescence, the body uses approximately 1% to 2% of energy requirements for growth alone. 

## Nervous system health 

- Children’s Magnesium Care supports healthy nervous system function. Magnesium is required for nerve conduction, modulating the hypothalamic pituitary adrenal axis and reducing the release of adrenalin and noradrenalin, supporting a healthy stress response in the body. 

- Several studies have assessed serum magnesium levels in children displaying a range of symptoms including hyperactivity, disruptive behaviour, restlessness and difficulty focusing. In one such study, magnesium deficiency was found in 95% of children examined[2] . 

## Muscle health 

- Children’s Magnesium Care supports muscle health and muscle contraction function in children. 

- About 50% to 60% of all magnesium in the body is found in the skeleton, while the remainder is found in soft tissue, primarily muscle. 

- It is estimated that between 25% to 40% of normally developing children experience the discomfort associated with cramping, particularly in the legs during periods of rapid growth. Leg muscle cramping occurs as bones grow and skeletal alignment is altered, requiring the muscles to grow, stretch and accommodate to bodily changes, putting extra force on muscle fibres. 

- Adequate levels of magnesium can assist with cellular functioning and the relaxation of smooth muscle in periods of rapid growth. 

## Cardiovascular system health 

- Magnesium helps maintain cardiovascular system health and heart health. It is essential for cardiac muscle contraction and production of energy within the heart muscle. 

- Magnesium plays a role in the active transport of calcium and potassium ions across cell membranes, which is essential for nerve impulse conduction, muscle contraction and normal heart rhythm. It is also essential for the contractility of vascular smooth muscle cells in the arterial wall and influences endothelial function, thereby influencing vasodilation and vasoconstriction. 

## Bone health 

- Magnesium supports bone health and assists in the development and maintenance of bones and teeth. Up to 60% of total body magnesium stores resides in bone, binding at the surface of the hydroxyapatite crystals. Magnesium in bones serves as a reservoir of magnesium, which can be released from bone to maintain physiological extracellular concentrations when magnesium intake is low. 

- In a study of 63 healthy children aged 4 to 8 years, an isotope study of magnesium absorption measured bone mineral content in each of the subjects. Results showed the amount of magnesium consumed and absorbed were key predictors of the level of bone in children, even more so than calcium[3] .

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Caution with aminoglycoside antibiotics (e.g. gentamicin) - both it and magnesium affect muscle function, potentially leading to muscle weakness and side effects. Co-administration should be avoided. 

- Caution with quinolone and tetracycline antibiotics – magnesium forms insoluble complexes with drugs, decreasing drug absorption. Take drug 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium. 

- Caution with bisphosphonates – magnesium can form complexes with drug and reduce absorption. Separate dose by 2 hours. 

- Caution with potassium-sparing diuretics – these drugs also have magnesium-sparing properties which could, theoretically, lead to increased magnesium levels. Monitor. 

- Caution with skeletal muscle relaxants – magnesium can potentiate effects. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- High dose magnesium is contraindicated in individuals with compromised renal function and heart block. 

- Dose may be too high for children under 4 years of age. Tablets can be halved and dosed appropriately for younger children. 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- Magnesium can cause gastrointestinal irritation, nausea and diarrhoea at high doses and in sensitive individuals.

## Energy production 

- Children’s Multi Care contains vitamins B1, B2, B5, B6 and B12 to help in the conversion of food into energy. B vitamins are important for the production of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), a chemical form of cellular energy used by every cell in the body for metabolic processes. 

- Between the age of three years old and middle adolescence, the body uses approximately 1% to 2% of energy requirements for growth alone. 

## Antioxidant 

- Children’s Multi Care contains the antioxidant nutrients vitamin C, citrus bioflavonoids, vitamin E, selenium and zinc to help reduce free radicals in the body. 

- Vitamin C is the most important water-soluble antioxidant, providing important protection for cells against oxidative damage. The body does not store vitamin C, meaning regular intake of adequate fruits 

and vegetables is essential to maintain appropriate levels, which does not always occur in a child’s diet. 

- Vitamin E is the most important fat-soluble antioxidant, protecting vitamin C, vitamin A, red blood cells and essential fatty acids from free radicals. 

- Selenium is an important component of glutathione peroxidases 1-4, antioxidant enzymes that reduce potentially damaging reactive oxygen species (ROS). Zinc is an essential part of the antioxidant enzyme copper/zinc superoxide dismutase (Cu/Zn SOD). 

## Cognitive function & brain health 

- Children’s Multi Care contains iodine, important for supporting a child’s brain health and cognitive development. 

- Iodine is used by the thyroid gland to help regulate metabolism and for the development of both a child’s skeleton and brain. 

- To help in the management of adequate iodine levels, Australia and New Zealand introduced mandatory fortification of iodine in bread in 2009. 

## Nervous system 

- Children’s Multi Care contains vitamins B1, B2, B5, B6 and B12 to help support a healthy nervous system in children and assist in the synthesis of neurotransmitters. 

- Vitamin B6 is involved in the conversion of tryptophan to niacin, the synthesis of gamma aminobutyric acid (GABA) in the central nervous system as well as the metabolism of serotonin, norepinephrine and dopamine. 

- Vitamin B12 is required for the proper functioning and development of the brain and nerve cells. It is essential for the myelin sheath that covers and protects the nerves of the central and the peripheral nervous system, ensuring fast and effective nerve-impulse transmission. 

- Serotonin and dopamine are neurotransmitters that play a role in overall mood and wellbeing.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Probiotics are microorganisms proven to have health-promoting influences in humans. The term ‘probiotic’ means ‘for life’. 

   - The ecological balance of the intestinal microbiota can be disturbed by environmental or physiological factors, such as antibiotics, stress and diet. 

- Compared to the more resistant adult microbiome, a child’s microbiome is less resilient and more susceptible to changes in response to diet modifications, antibiotic treatment and other events such as illness. 

   - Children’s Probiotic 15 Billion helps maintain a balanced, healthy composition of the intestinal microbiota. 

   - Lactobacillus rhamnosus HN001, Bifidobacterium lactis HN019, Lactobacillus acidophilus La-14, Lactobacillus salivarius Ls-33, Lactobacillus paracasei Lpc-37 and Lactobacillus plantarum Lp-115 have displayed in vitro inhibition of common pathogens. 

- In order for probiotics to have a therapeutic effect, they need to have the following characteristics: gastric acid and bile salt stability; an ability to adhere to the intestinal mucosa; and an ability to colonise the intestinal tract. 

## Digestive system health 

- Children’s Probiotic 15 Billion contains 15 different strains that survive both stomach acid and bile and adhere to the intestinal mucosa. Good adherence to intestinal mucosa is important as it prolongs the time a probiotic strain can reside in the intestine, giving it an opportunity to modulate the immune response and protect against enteric pathogens by limiting their ability to colonise the intestine. 

   - Children’s Probiotic 15 Billion supports a child’s digestive health by maintaining beneficial intestinal flora, contributing to its ability to function normally. 

   - Children can suffer from many digestive related complaints while their digestive systems strengthen. A fully functional digestive system is a delicate balance while intestinal flora builds. This balance can be disrupted by diet, colds and flu and antibiotics. 

- Children’s Probiotic 15 Billion contains studied probiotic strains supplied by Danisco[®] , a supplier trusted by some of the world’s most recognised manufacturers. Danisco[®] utilises patented stabilisation technology to improve shelf-life and to stabilise the phospholipid bilayer of the probiotic cell membrane, so that all the strains are room-stable and do not require refrigeration. Children’s Probiotic 15 Billion also contains Bifidobacterium breve M16-V, a well-studied strain in infants and children. 

- Colonisation of the gut with appropriate microflora contributes to its ability to function normally. 

- Specifically, Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG has been shown to relieve functional pain in children suffering from irritable bowel syndrome symptoms. A double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled study found that supplementation with 6 billion CFU/day Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (two serves of Children’s Probiotic 15 Billion) led to a statistically significant reduction in both frequency (p<0.01), and severity (p<0.01) of abdominal pain[1] . 

## Intestinal microbiota 

- The gastrointestinal microbiota plays a critical role in nutritional, metabolic and immune functions in children and infants. 

   - Bifidobacterium breve is one of the predominant Bifidobacterium species present in the infant gut, widely recognised for its beneficial role in maintaining infant health. A study in infants found that supplementation with Bifidobacterium breve M16-V promoted the colonisation of the Bifidobacterium and the formation of a normal intestinal flora in infants[2] . 

- The human gastrointestinal tract is populated by bacteria, archaea, yeasts and fungi, which are collectively referred to as the gastrointestinal (GI) microbiota. The microbiota has several important functions in maintaining human health, including providing the host with nutrients and protecting from harmful microbes. It is involved in many metabolic processes, including the fermentation of undigested carbohydrates into short-chain fatty acids, lipid metabolism and vitamin synthesis.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Chromium is an essential trace mineral required for carbohydrate, protein and lipid metabolism. 

- Chromium is found in a wide variety of foods, but most sources only contain small amounts due to soil depletion, particularly in Australia. Food sources rich in chromium include organ meats, cheese, broccoli, green beans, spices and wine. 

- The absorption of chromium from the intestinal tract is low and can be enhanced by the intake of nutrients such as vitamin C and niacin. Chromium is stored in the liver, spleen, soft tissue and bone. 

- Diets high in simple sugars result in increased urinary chromium excretion in adults. This effect may be related to increased insulin secretion in response to the consumption of simple sugars compared to complex carbohydrates. 

- Stressors, such as elevated blood sugar, strenuous physical activity or work, infection and emotional and physical trauma, may increase the excretion of chromium. 

## Glucose metabolism 

- Chromium was first identified as ‘Glucose Tolerance Factor’, however, it was later discovered to be a complex of molecules found in the body comprised of chromium bound to single molecules of glycine, cysteine, glutamic acid, and two molecules of nicotinic acid.

- Caution with thyroxine – chromium can reduce drug absorption. Seperate dose by at least 3 hours.

- None noted at the recommended dose.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Clear Skin is a combination of traditional herbs with strong depurative actions to help relieve acne and minor skin conditions and support skin health. It also contains vitamin A, B6 and zinc to maintain skin health and wound healing. 

- Clear Skin contains vitamin A and zinc, potent antioxidants to reduce free radicals in the body. 

## Acne 

- Acne is a common skin condition that affects the face, back and chest and can affect self-esteem. It usually begins in the teenage years as hormone changes occur, however, it can persist into the 30s and 40s. 

- Acne is caused by inflammation of the hair follicles and appears as blackheads, whiteheads, pimples and cysts. In severe cases, acne can lead to permanent scarring. Acne occurs when the hair follicles get blocked by excess sebum, which is usually driven by androgens. Dead skin cells mix with the blockage and bacteria in the skin multiply which can cause pain and swelling (inflammation) beneath the blockages. 

- Factors that can exacerbate acne include stress, poor diet, being overweight, not getting enough exercise and hormonal shifts. It is very common for women to experience breakouts before their periods. 

## Skin health 

- Clear Skin contains Burdock and Yellow dock, herbs traditionally used in Western herbal medicine (WHM) to support skin health. These herbs are classed as depuratives. Depuratives, also known as alteratives and blood cleansers, improve detoxification and aid elimination channels via the kidneys, skin and mucous membranes to reduce the accumulation of metabolic waste production in the body. 

- Burdock and Yellow dock are depuratives that work principally via the liver and digestion and also support hepatic detoxification. 

- Burdock is also used in WHM as a diuretic to enhance urine output and a diaphoretic to induce sweating. Thus, it helps improve elimination via both the skin and kidneys. 

- Yellow dock is traditionally used in WHM as an alterative and depurative herb to support waste elimination via the skin. Yellow dock also has mild laxative effects, helping to support elimination 

- via the bowels. The Physiomedical Dispensatory (1869) states that “the greater portion of its power is expended upon the skin; but the gall ducts, small intestines, and kidneys, feel its impressions to a fair extent”[1] . 

- Calendula is traditionally used in WHM as an anti-inflammatory and vulnerary to support wound healing. 

- In addition to herbs, Clear Skin contains the nutrients vitamin A and zinc to support skin health. Vitamin A supports collagen formation and epithelial cell differentiation. 

- Zinc is an essential mineral for skin health and is necessary for connective tissue formation and wound healing. The skin contains 6% of total body zinc[2] . Zinc is also required for the hepatic synthesis of retinol binding protein, which is the transport protein of vitamin A. Therefore, insufficient zinc can result in the symptoms of a vitamin A deficiency, even with adequate vitamin A intake. 

## Acne & minor skin conditions 

- Clear Skin contains Burdock, traditionally used in WHM to relieve symptoms of acne and minor skin eruptions. 

- Traditionally, alteratives or depuratives are used for chronic skin conditions and work by purifying the blood and detoxifying and supporting eliminatory channels to reduce the accumulation of metabolic waste products. In modern herbalism, depuratives are the main herbs used for acne. Burdock, Yellow dock and Calendula are important depuratives for acne. 

- It is generally recognised that depuratives in high doses can cause a temporary exacerbation of symptoms. Strong depuratives, such as Burdock, can be combined with more eliminatory herbs, such as Yellow dock, to reduce the potential for exacerbation[3] . 

- Burdock is traditionally used in WHM to support waste elimination via the skin, relieve minor skin eruptions and relieve the symptoms of mild eczema. According to eclectic texts, the herb is indicated for dry, scaly skin eruptions and recurrent boils, especially with feeble circulation in the skin, as it gently stimulates the kidneys and promotes the elimination of waste material[4] . According to Grieves, Burdock root is “one of the best blood purifiers. In all skin diseases, it is a certain remedy and has effected a cure in many cases of eczema”[5] .

- One study found that the serum vitamin A and zinc levels were significantly lower in patients with acne than in age and sex matched healthy individuals in the control group (p<0.001). It also showed a negative correlation between acne severity and zinc levels[7] .

- URTIs are characterised by infectious pathogens that affect the sinuses, nasal passages, pharynx and larynx and are one of the most common reasons for a doctor visit. The majority of URTIs are caused by viral infections, though some are of bacterial origin, and are highly contagious with the ability to spread from person to person via droplets from an infected person coughing or sneezing.

- The common cold is a type of URTI, with more than 200 different viruses that can cause the infection. On average, an adult will get 2-4 colds every year. Symptoms can include sore throat, fever, sneezing, blocked or runny nose and cough. These symptoms are usually mild to moderately severe and usually resolve within 7-10 days.

## **Cold & Flu Strike** 

- Vitamin C and zinc support immune system function. Vitamin C is an immunostimulant and in vitro studies show it enhances the activity of natural killer cells, B-cells and T-cells. Zinc is important for the function of natural killer cells, phagocytes, macrophages and neutrophils and is essential for cytokine production and secretion. 

## Fever relief 

- Cold & Flu Strike contains herbs traditionally used to relieve mild fevers. 

- Elderberry is traditionally used in WHM as a diaphoretic to help relieve mild fevers. 

- Andrographis is used in both traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and traditional Ayurvedic medicine as an antipyretic to reduce mild fever. In TCM, Andrographis is considered a cold herb to clear heat and cool heat toxin in the lungs and stomach and thus help manage symptoms of the flu, such as cough and sore, swollen throats[9] . 

- In Ayurvedic medicine, Andrographis, known as Kalamegha, is considered to have the action “jvarahara”, which means “fever reducing” and is also used for general debility and convalescence after fevers[10] . 

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Caution with immunosuppression agents (e.g. cyclosporine) – Cold & Flu Strike may interfere with immunosuppression agents due to its immunostimulant activity. 

- Caution with anticoagulant and antiplatelet drugs - additive effects are theoretically possible as Andrographis has been shown to inhibit platelet aggregation in animals. Observe for increased bruising or bleeding. 

- Caution with NSAIDs, penicillamine, cefalexin and tetracycline and quinolone antibiotics - zinc forms complexes with these drugs, reducing absorption of both. Separate dose by 3 hours. 

- Caution with aluminium-based antacids - vitamin C increases the amount of aluminium absorbed. Separate dose. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- Contraindicated during pregnancy and breastfeeding. 

- Contraindicated in states of hyperacidity, especially duodenal ulcers (Andrographis). 

- Caution in individuals with autoimmune conditions. 

- Caution in individuals with bleeding disorders. Andrographis may inhibit platelet aggregation and increase the risk of bleeding. 

- Caution in people with conditions of iron overload, such as hemochromatosis, as vitamin C increases iron absorption. 

- Discontinue use one week before surgery. 

- Separate from mineral supplementation or coffee by 2 hours - coffee reduces zinc absorption and minerals may interfere with zinc absorption. 

- Andrographis in high doses long term may cause temporary loss of taste. 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- Side effects are rare. High doses of Andrographis can (rarely) cause gastric discomfort, anorexia and vomiting. Long-term high-dose Andrographis has been associated with temporary loss of taste sensation. 

- Andrographis may cause allergic reactions in some individuals. In the case of a severe reaction (such as anaphylaxis), stop use and seek immediate medical attention.

- Elderberry Echinacea & Olive Leaf 

- Mushroom 5 Complex 

- Probiotic 55 Billion 

- Zinc Forte + C

- Collagen consists of amino acids comprised of three polypeptide chains that wrap tightly around each other to form a triple helix molecule resembling a rope-like shape.  The rigid structure of collagen provides tensile strength and firmness to connective tissues around the body. 

- Approximately 28 types of collagen have been identified in the human body. Type I, II and III collagens are the most predominant types, each containing different proteins that serve specific roles and are distributed differently in the body: 

- Type I: most common type of collagen and mainly present in skin, bone, teeth, tendons, ligaments, vascular ligature and organs. 

- Type II: main structural component of cartilage tissue and provides flexibility and support to bone joints. 

- Type III: present in skin, muscle, vessels and reticular fibres of organ tissues such as the liver, spleen and lungs. 

- Over 90% of collagen in the body is comprised of type I and III collagen produced by fibroblasts (cells in connective tissues) and osteoblasts (cells that make bones). 

- The amino acids crucial for collagen synthesis and production are: 

- Glycine: most abundant amino acid found in collagen and synthesised by serine. 

- Proline: non-essential amino acid vital for collagen biosynthesis, strength and structure. 

- Lysine: essential amino acid involved in collagen formation.

## Collagen vs collagen peptides 

- Collagen in its natural state is referred to as native collagen. It is formed from three very long chains of over 1000 amino acids twisting into a helix conformation. In its full-length, unhydrolysed form, collagen is not an effective oral supplement as it is difficult to break down during digestion and too large to cross the intestinal wall. 

- Collagen peptides are short chain protein building blocks characterised by high levels of specific amino acids glycine, hydroxyproline, proline and alanine. This amino acid composition provides collagen peptides their unique bioactive properties not found with other protein sources. 

- Native collagen undergoes enzymatic hydrolysis to break the bonds in the polypeptide chain, creating a larger number of peptides with reduced weight and size, which increases bioavailability in humans. 

- Hydrolysed collagen peptides are very small molecules and offer a low molecular weight with increased solubility in water and enhanced digestibility and absorption. Collagen peptides are available as small, unique peptides characterised by a Hyp-Pro containing sequence and are quickly absorbed into the blood stream after intake. They act as important signal molecules to stimulate cells and provides building blocks to support connective tissue and musculoskeletal health.

## Joint health 

- A joint is an articulation where two bones are cushioned by cartilage and lubricated with synovial fluid. Joints are comprised of bone, muscles, synovium, cartilage and ligaments designed to bear weight and facilitate movement. 

- Collagen is a major component of connective tissue that makes up the cartilage, tendons and ligaments that provide structural integrity to the joints. Type II collagen is primarily found in the articular cartilage of joints. 

- Cartilage degradation can occur over time due to wear and tear, repeated movement and ageing.

- In a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, administration of 10g hydrolysed collagen to athletes with activity related joint pain improved joint symptoms after 24 weeks. ## Collagen 

- Collagen is the body’s most abundant protein, representing approximately 30% of total body protein. Collagen is a major structural component of connective tissue that makes up skin, hair, nails, ligaments, tendons, cartilage, teeth and bone. 

- Proline: non-essential amino acid vital for collagen biosynthesis, strength and structure. 

- Lysine: essential amino acid involved in collagen formation. 

- Proline and lysine are converted into their active forms, hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine, respectively, via hydroxylation. Hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine are major components of cross linkages in collagen and play a key role in collagen stability. Hydroxylation of proline and lysine is dependent upon adequate levels of vitamin C as a cofactor for collagen protein synthesis and repair. 

Figure 1: Structure of collagen fibres 

- Collagen consists of amino acids comprised of three polypeptide chains that wrap tightly around each other to form a triple helix molecule resembling a rope-like shape. The rigid structure of collagen provides tensile strength and firmness to connective tissues around the body. 

- Approximately 28 types of collagen have been identified in the human body. Type I, II and III collagens are the most predominant types, each containing different proteins that serve specific roles and are distributed differently in the body: 

- Type I: most common type of collagen and mainly present in skin, bone, teeth, tendons, ligaments, vascular ligature and organs. 

- Type II: main structural component of cartilage tissue and provides flexibility and support to bone joints. 

- Type III: present in skin, muscle, vessels and reticular fibres of organ tissues such as the liver, spleen and lungs. 

- Over 90% of collagen in the body is comprised of type I and III collagen produced by fibroblasts (cells in connective tissues) and osteoblasts (cells that make bones). 

- The amino acids crucial for collagen synthesis and production are: 

- Glycine: most abundant amino acid found in collagen and is synthesised by serine. 

## Collagen vs collagen peptides 

- Collagen in its natural state is referred to as native collagen. It is formed from three very long chains of over 1000 amino acids twisting into a helix conformation. In its full-length, unhydrolysed form, collagen is not an effective oral supplement as it is difficult to break down during digestion and too large to cross the intestinal wall. 

- Collagen peptides are short chain protein building blocks characterised by high levels of specific amino acids glycine, hydroxyproline, proline and alanine. This amino acid composition provides collagen peptides their unique bioactive properties not found with other protein sources.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- CoQ10 150mg contains Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) derived from natural fermentation by the bacteria Rhodobacter sphaeroides. 

- CoQ10 exists in two main forms (ubiquinone and ubiquinol), forming what is known as a redox reduction pair. This means they naturally cycle in the body from one form to the other as required by the cell, so that both energy production and oxidative balance can be maintained. 

- CoQ10 150mg contains ubiquinone, the oxidised form of CoQ10. After absorption, the body converts ubiquinone into ubiquinol, the active antioxidant form. Studies over 3 decades have shown the ubiquinone supports health and general wellbeing. 

- While CoQ10 is manufactured in the body, the endogenous production of CoQ10 requires several vitamin coenzymes, including vitamins B2, B6, B12, C, folic acid, niacin and pantothenic acid. 

- CoQ10 150mg is manufactured in rice bran oil, a stable, soy-free base. Rice bran oil has a high content of tocotrienols (antioxidants in the vitamin E family), which provide greater stability from oxidation than soy oil. 

- CoQ10 150mg is best given with food. Ubiquinone is insoluble in water and difficult to absorb on an empty stomach. Absorption is at least twice as effective when taken with a meal[1] . 

## Antioxidant 

- CoQ10 is a lipid-soluble antioxidant that helps protect the body from oxidative damage. Specifically, CoQ10 protects cell membranes from oxidation, supporting cell membrane integrity and cell functioning. 

- As an antioxidant, CoQ10 has a sparing effect on vitamin E and helps recycle vitamin E from its oxidised form to its active (antioxidant) form. 

- CoQ10 increases the resistance of LDL cholesterol to oxidation. Supplementation with exogenous CoQ10 leads to an increase in the ubiquinol content of LDL cholesterol and a corresponding decrease of LDL peroxidability. 

## Energy production 

- CoQ10 supports healthy energy levels. It is an essential component of mitochondria and plays a critical role in energy production within cells. 

- CoQ10 is concentrated in tissues with high energy requirements, such as the heart and skeletal muscle. Physical activity increases the body’s demand for energy and, therefore, CoQ10 and reduces muscle tissue levels of CoQ10. 

- Physical exercise also induces muscle damage associated with a high production of free radicals and pro-inflammatory mediators. Oral supplementation of CoQ10 during exercise has been found to reduce oxidative stress, increase total antioxidant status and modulate inflammatory signalling, which reduces subsequent muscle damage[2] . 

- CoQ10 supplementation supports healthy exercise capacity. A randomised, double-blind, crossover study in healthy sedentary men found that supplementation with 100mg CoQ10 showed performance-enhancing effects during repeated bouts of supramaximal exercise[3] . 

## Cardiovascular & heart health 

- CoQ10 helps maintain a healthy cardiovascular system and supports heart health through antioxidant activity, inhibition of LDL cholesterol oxidation and by the maintenance of optimal mitochondrial function. The heart is one of the most metabolically active tissues in the body and, therefore, has a high requirement for CoQ10 to support energy production. 

- CoQ10 supports healthy endothelial function. The endothelium is the single cell layer of tissue that forms the lining of blood vessels, heart and lymphatic vessels. A 2012 meta-analysis showed that treatment with CoQ10 significantly improved endothelial function assessed peripherally by flow-mediated dilation (p<0.0001)[4] . 

- CoQ10 helps maintain healthy blood vessels by inhibiting the oxidation of LDL cholesterol. 

## Mild migraine 

- CoQ10 can help reduce the frequency of migraines and headaches as well as the associated nausea and vomiting when taken as a preventative. 

- Migraines are thought to result, in part, from mitochondrial dysfunction and supplementing with CoQ10 supports healthy mitochondrial function. 

- An open-labelled trial investigated the effects of oral CoQ10 supplementation (150mg/day) over 3 months in healthy volunteers with a history of episodic migraine. Of the 31 patients that completed the study, 61.3% had a greater than 50% reduction in the number of days with migraine headache and 93.5% of patients had at least a 25% reduction in the number of days with migraine[5] . 

## Sperm health

## Statins 

- Statin medications, used to manage blood cholesterol levels, are associated with lower CoQ10 levels. CoQ10 and cholesterol share a common biosynthetic pathway. As a result, statins, which are potent inhibitors of cholesterol biosynthesis, also adversely affect CoQ10 levels. 

- Statin use is often associated with a variety of muscle-related symptoms known as myopathies, which may relate, in part, to the depletion of endogenous synthesis of CoQ10. A systematic review states that statins reduce plasma/serum CoQ10 levels by 16-54%[6] . 

- Several studies have found CoQ10 supplementation to have a beneficial effect on statin-related side-effects. One study found 30-day treatment with 100mg/day of CoQ10 reduced pain severity by 40% (p<0.001) and pain interference with daily activities by 38% (p<0.02)[7] . Another placebo-controlled study found that 50mg of CoQ10 twice daily decreased statin-related muscle symptoms in 75% of patients. Pain severity score decreased by 33.1% (p<0.001) and pain interference score reduced by 40.3% (p<0.001)[8] .

- Caution with warfarin. Conflicting reports have shown CoQ10 may decrease, increase or have no effect on the efficacy of oral anticoagulants. Use only under the care of a health professional and monitor INR values.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Cranberry is an antioxidant herb that supports urinary tract health and can help reduce the occurrence of medically diagnosed cystitis. 

- Cystitis is an inflammation of the bladder that almost always follows bacterial infection in the urine and is the most common type of urinary tract infection (UTI). 

- The most common symptoms of cystitis are frequent urge to urinate, burning or scalding sensation on urination, strong-smelling urine and pain in the lower abdomen. Escherichia coli (E. coli) is the most common bacterium responsible for UTIs. 

- UTIs are more common in women than in men, as the female urethra is only 4cm long, giving bacteria easy access to the bladder. Additionally, due to hormonal influences and changes in vaginal secretions, women are mores susceptible to infection during certain stages of the menstrual cycle, during pregnancy and during menopause. 

## Antioxidant 

- Cranberry and vitamin C are potent antioxidants that reduce free radicals formed in the body. Cranberry is also a rich source of vitamin C – it was used historically to treat scurvy due to its high vitamin C content. Vitamin C helps support healthy immune system function. 

## Urinary tract infections 

- Traditionally, Cranberry is used in Western herbal medicine to help reduce the occurrence of urinary tract infections. Native American Indians used Cranberry as both a food and a medicine for bladder and kidney problems. In the 1840s, German scientists made the connection between Cranberry and the incidence of urinary tract infections. Since then, there has been much research into Cranberry and its effects on urinary tract health. 

- Cranberry contains proanthocyanidins, which prevent the adherence of pathogenic bacteria, particularly E. coli, to the walls of the urinary tract. In vitro and animal studies demonstrate that Cranberry consumption inhibits the binding of bacterial strains to uroepithelial cells. 

- One in vitro study found that urine collected after Cranberry consumption prevented adhesion of 31 (80%) of the 39 isolates and 19 (79%) of the 24 antibiotic-resistant isolates in bioassays, while pre-consumption urine failed to prevent adhesion in any sample. Anti-adhesion activity was seen within 2 hours and persisted for up to 10 hours following Cranberry ingestion[1] . 

- One study looked at 373 women with a history of recent UTI and the effect of 240mL Cranberry juice (equivalent to 65g Cranberry) on episodes of UTIs. During the study time, there were 39 episodes of UTI in the Cranberry group compared to 67 episodes in the placebo group (p=0.016). Cranberry also significantly reduced clinical UTI with pyuria (p=0.037)[3] . 

## Masking urinary odour 

- Cranberry is often used to mask urinary odour associated with incontinence. To-date, there are no studies available to support this use. However, numerous anecdotal reports suggest it can be useful when taken on a regular basis[4] . 

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Caution with warfarin – possible interaction with Cranberry and vitamin C (conflicting reports). Monitor INR. 

- Caution with aluminium-containing compounds (e.g. phosphate binders) – vitamin C increases the amount of aluminium absorbed. Separate dose by at least 2 hours. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- If symptoms of UTI become more severe while taking Cranberry, or if pain or irritation persists for more than 48 hours, medical advice is recommended. The presence of blood in the urine warrants immediate medical attention. 

- Use with caution in people with iron overload conditions, such as haemochromotosis, as vitamin C increases iron absorption.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Digest-Zymes contains a comprehensive blend of enzymes to support healthy digestive function and to aid in the digestion of fats, proteins and carbohydrates, including fibre and lactose. 

- Poor digestion is one of the most common health complaints today. Several factors can contribute to the development of digestive issues, including poor eating habits (eating on the run and inadequate chewing of food) and poor dietary choices, such as excessive consumption of alcohol, refined carbohydrates and fat, and a diet low in raw foods. Raw foods contain enzymes which can help facilitate digestion. 

- Symptoms of poor digestion include indigestion and fullness lasting 2-4 hours after eating, bloating, excessive flatulence, abdominal cramps, alternating constipation and diarrhea, and undigested food in the stool. 

## Digestion 

- Digestion begins in the mouth where food is broken down by the salivary enzymes amylase and lingual lipase. The food (bolus) then travels down the esophagus into the stomach where gastric juices and enzymes are secreted to further breakdown macro and micronutrients. 

- Low stomach acid results in the pH of the stomach remaining unnaturally high, which predisposes the gram-positive flora to colonise and increases the susceptibility of the gastrointestinal tract to infection. A higher pH can impair the absorption of several vitamins and minerals, specifically, iron, vitamin B12, calcium, magnesium and zinc, which may increase the risk of deficiency. 

- The pancreas is comprised of an endocrine and exocrine portion. The exocrine tissue of the pancreas (the acini) produces digestive enzymes that are mixed with sodium bicarbonate and function to break down carbohydrate, proteins and fats. Problems occur when there is a dysfunction in the ability of the pancreas to produce enzymes or the body’s demand for enzymes exceeds the supply. 

- Stress can have a big impact on digestion. Digestion is under the primary control of the vagal nerve and the parasympathetic nervous system and is therefore stimulated by a relaxed state. Conversely, stress causes activation of the sympathetic nervous system and can impair gastrointestinal motility and function. 

## Digestive enzymes 

- Digestive enzyme supplementation can aid in the breakdown of fats, proteins and carbohydrates and may provide benefit in disorders in which compromised digestion may be involved[1] . 

- As a large percentage of Australians have diets that are typically low in enzymes (due to a predominance of processed, refined foods), the importance of digestive enzyme supplementation is especially relevant. 

- Amylase is a carbohydrate-degrading enzyme that aids in the breakdown of polysaccharides, such as starch. 

- Protease enzymes are involved in the breakdown of proteins to oligopeptides and amino acids. Bromelains are proteolytic enzymes that aid in the digestion and assimilation of proteins. Bromelain is the general name for the family of sulfhydryl-containing, proteolytic enzymes from the pineapple fruit and stem and has a wide pH range which allows them to be active in the stomach as well as the small intestine. The German Commission E approves the use of bromelain (combined with other digestive enzymes) for dyspepsia (indigestion)[2] . 

- Lipase is a lipid-degrading enzyme that assists in the digestion of dietary fats. Lipase hydrolyses triacylglycerols (the main lipid found in the diet) into diacylglycerols, monoacylglycerols, free fatty acids and glycerol. 

- Tilactase, more commonly known as lactase, is specific for digesting lactose, the primary disaccharide found in dairy products. It is involved in the breakdown of lactose to glucose and galactose. 

- Cellulase is an enzyme that breaks down plant fibre known as cellulose. A diet high in fibre, particularly insoluble fibre, can be

## Lactose intolerance 

- Lactose intolerance, or hypolactesia, is characterised by decreased lactase activity and affects approximately 75% of individuals worldwide, making it the most common enzyme deficiency[5] . 

- Individuals who are lactose intolerant do not produce sufficient lactase, the enzyme responsible for breaking down lactose (a sugar found in dairy products). As a result, these sugars pass undigested through the digestive system, causing digestive upset. 

- Symptoms associated with lactose intolerance include bloating, 

- flatulence, abdominal cramping and diarrhea. 

- Supplementing with tilactase (lactase) assists in the breakdown of lactose and can relieve gastrointestinal symptoms associated with lactose intolerance. 

## Microbial-derived enzymes 

- Digest-Zymes contains vegetarian friendly, non-animal derived microbial enzymes. The enzymes are produced through microbial fermentation using modern filtration technology which produces a non-toxic, non-pathogenic strain of the enzyme. Although microbialderived, the finished product contains no microbial residue. Modern filtration technology allows for a clean and pure product, consisting strictly of enzymes[6] . 

- Microbial-derived enzymes are highly stable and active throughout a wide pH range making them more active and functional for a longer distance through the digestive tract when compared to pancreatic enzymes, which are susceptible to being destroyed by gastric acid and pepsin. 

- The activity of microbial derived enzymes cannot be compared by weight (e.g. mg amounts). Instead, enzyme strength is measured through their expression of activity over a given period of time, expressed as quantifying units.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Echinacea, commonly known as ‘purple coneflower’ is a perennial herb native to North America. It was first used by Native Americans as a remedy for snakebites and infections of the nose and throat. 

- Echinacea species contain water-soluble polysaccharides, alkamides, flavonoids and caffeic acid derivatives, including echinacoside and chicoric acid. The concentration of these constituents can vary significantly depending on growing conditions, drying of the plant and the extraction process. The main active constituents are considered to be the alkamides, which are responsible for the mouthtingling effects of Echinacea. 

- Echinacea purpurea and Echinacea angustifolia contain structurally 

- different types of alkamides. 

- The 2-ene alkamides present in Echinacea angustifolia protect the alkamides found in Echinacea purpurea that are rapidly broken down by the liver, leading to less degradation. A combination of both species provides a complex alkamide profile and results in greater bioavailability[1] . 

## Immune health 

- Echinacea 4000 Complex supports immune system function and immune health. It is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine (WHM) to support the immune system to fight illness. 

- Echinacea has immunomodulatory effects on the body and supports both innate and specific immunity. Administration of Echinacea enhances macrophages, phagocytosis and cytokine production in humans[2] . 

- Echinacea can stimulate specific immune responses including the activation of innate immune cells and increased levels and activity of T lymphocytes, neutrophils and natural killer (NK) cells. These effects may be due to the polysaccharides present in Echinacea[3] . 

- Recent experiments demonstrate that alkamides are detectable in human blood in relevant concentrations after oral administration of Echinacea preparations. Alkamides show structural similarity with anandamide, an endogenous ligand of cannabinoid receptors. It was found that alkamides bind significantly to CB2 receptors, which 

is now considered as a possible mechanism of action of Echinacea alkamides as immunomodulatory agents[4] . 

- Echinacea  angustifolia contains unique 2-ene alkamides. These are only found in Echinacea angustifolia and exhibit selective affinity to CB2 receptors found mostly in immune cells[5] . 

## Common cold 

   - Echinacea purpurea and Echinacea angustifolia have been used traditionally in Native American medicine for centuries for respiratory tract infections and inflammatory conditions, including common cold, coughs, bronchitis and inflammation of the mouth and pharynx. 

   - Echinacea is traditionally used in WHM to relieve the symptoms of common cold, sore throat and mild upper respiratory tract infections, including mild fever and excess mucous. 

   - Echinacea angustifolia root is recommended as a supportive therapy for colds and upper respiratory tract infections by the German Commission E[6] . 

   - Both the German Commission E and the World Health Organisation approve the use of Echinacea purpurea herb as supportive therapy for colds and infections of the respiratory tract[7,8] . 

   - A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involving 755 healthy subjects assessed the safety and efficacy of Echinacea on common cold episodes. Subjects received 2400mg/day of Echinacea purpurea whole plant extract or placebo over a 4-month period. A daily dose of 4000mg of Echinacea was also given during acute cold episodes. A reduction in total number of cold episodes, cumulated episode days and pain-killer medicated episodes was observed in the Echinacea group compared to the placebo group[9] . 

   - A meta-analysis of 14 studies and 11 356 participants evaluated the effect of Echinacea extracts on common cold incidence and duration. Echinacea decreased the odds of developing the common cold by 58% and reduced the duration of a cold by 1-4 days. The studies used a dose ranging from 100mg to 2400mg/day. Published evidence supports the use of Echinacea for decreasing the incidence and duration of the common cold[10] .

## Omega-3 fatty acids 

   - Fatty acids are found in high concentrations in neuronal membranes and in the myelin sheath and play a role in neuronal membrane fluidity and function. Higher plasma omega-3 PUFA has been associated with a lower risk of age-related cognitive decline. 

- Omega-3 fatty acids are long-chain polyunsaturated essential fatty acids (EFA) that are necessary for good health and development. They are essential because the body cannot produce them, so adequate amounts must be consumed from the diet. 

- Satisfying omega-3 requirements through diet alone is difficult due to the increasing presence of heavy metals, polychlorinated biphenyls and other environmental toxins present in fish. Therefore, taking a concentrated fish oil supplement that is tested for purity and freshness can be a good way to supplement omega-3s in the diet. 

   - DHA is the major component of phospholipids in the brain and contributes to the maintenance of normal brain function. 

   - A placebo-controlled, cross-over study evaluating the effects of five weeks omega-3 supplementation (3g/day) on cognitive performance in 40 healthy, middle aged to elderly individuals found that supplementation improved cognitive performance, specifically resulting in better performance in the working memory test (p<0.05)[3] . 

- EPA and DHA have an anti-inflammatory action and help reduce inflammation in the body. The typical Western diet provides an overabundance of omega-6 fatty acids, which can favour an inflammatory response. Thus, higher amounts of omega-3 fatty acids in the diet or through supplementation are recommended. 

- A study of 20 to 34-year-olds found that EPA-rich supplementation enhanced neurocognitive function and suggested that the brain worked less hard yet had better cognitive performance[4] .

- Omega-3 fatty acids support healthy cardiovascular system function and heart health. DHA is the principal fatty acid incorporated into myocardial membrane phospholipids. 

   - Omega-3 fatty acids support eye health, particularly retina health. DHA is the major component of phospholipids in the retina and contributes to the maintenance of normal vision. 

- Omega-3 fatty acids exert their benefit on the cardiovascular system via a number of different mechanisms, including improved myocardial oxygen efficiency and heart rate, modulation of myocardial sodium and potassium ion channel function and improved endothelial function. ## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Folic Acid Complex contains high-strength folic acid, together with vitamins B6, B12 and iodine. 

- Folic acid is essential for the formation of thymidylate synthase, an enzyme required for DNA and RNA formation and cell replication and division. It is essential during foetal development and helps produce key chemicals for the brain and nervous system[1] . 

- Vitamin B12 is an important co-factor for folic acid metabolism. Both nutrients need to be present for chemical reactions to occur within the one-carbon metabolic pathway. This pathway is vital for the synthesis of DNA, RNA, neurotransmitters, membrane phospholipids, myelin and proper functioning of the central nervous system. If vitamin B12 is not present, folic acid cannot function properly regardless of sufficient intake. 

- Methylcobalamin is the metabolically active form of vitamin B12 that is readily used in the body. Alternative forms of vitamin B12, such as cyanocobalamin, require an additional step to achieve conversion to methylcobalamin in the body. 

- Vegans and strict vegetarians are at risk of vitamin B12 deficiency as they do not consume any animal products, the main dietary source of vitamin B12. 

## Healthy foetal development & healthy pregnancy 

- Folic Acid Complex contains folic acid and iodine to support healthy foetal development and a healthy pregnancy. 

- Adequate folic acid consumption for three months prior to conception and for the first three months of pregnancy greatly reduces the risk of serious birth defects, including spina bifida/neural tube defects. 

- Clinical practice guidelines recommend that women capable of becoming pregnant take a minimum of 400 micrograms of folic acid from fortified foods or supplements to prevent neural tube defects in infants. This recommendation is based on research showing that a higher intake of folic acid from food and supplements during pregnancy reduces the primary incidence of neural tube defects by between 41% to 69%[2] . 

- Iodine sufficiency during pregnancy is critical to proper foetal development. Iodine is a component of thyroid hormones triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4), hormones that influence growth and development. Iodine comprises 65% of the weight of T4 and 59% of the weight of T3[3] . During early pregnancy, when foetal thyroid gland development is incomplete, the foetus depends entirely on maternal T4, and therefore maternal iodine intake. 

- During pregnancy the foetus is totally dependent on maternal thyroxine for healthy brain, skeletal and central nervous system development. Inadequate levels of maternal thyroxine can lead to irreversible and detrimental effects on the brain. 

## Cognitive function & brain health 

- Folic Acid Complex contains folic acid and vitamin B12 to support cognitive function and brain health. 

- Folic acid is implicated in cognition and brain health due to its ability to improve nitric oxide levels in the brain and facilitate the synthesis of neurotransmitters. 

- Vitamin B12 plays a key role in supporting normal functions of the brain and nervous system. A panel comprised of the European Foods Safety Authority concluded that a cause and effect relationship has been demonstrated between dietary intake of vitamin B12 and normal neurological and psychological functions[4] . 

## Nervous system health 

- Folic Acid Complex contains iodine and vitamins B6 and B12 for nervous system health. 

- Iodine is an essential trace element required to produce thyroid hormones and for the proper functioning of the thyroid gland. Thyroid hormones have a direct relationship with many metabolic processes, including the growth and development of the central nervous system (CNS). 

- Vitamin B6 is important for healthy nervous system function. It is involved in the synthesis of several neurotransmitters, including GABA, serotonin, norepinephrine and dopamine. 

- Vitamin B12 is essential for the preservation of the myelin sheath around neurons and for the synthesis of neurotransmitters. 

## Cardiovascular system health 

- Folic Acid Complex contains folic acid and vitamins B6 and B12 for cardiovascular system health. 

- One of the most important folate-dependent reactions in the body is the conversion of homocysteine to methionine. Elevated homocysteine has been associated with an increased risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes.

- Folic Acid Complex contains folic acid and vitamins B6 and B12 to support healthy red blood cell production. 

- Folate-containing coenzymes are essential to produce DNA and RNA in growing and dividing cells. Rapidly dividing cells, such as blood cells and cells lining the digestive tract, are particularly dependent on folate. Folate helps maintain red blood cell health. 

- Folic acid and vitamins B6 and B12 are important co-factors required to activate enzymes that are essential for the formation of the haem components that form haemoglobin, a protein abundant in red blood cells responsible for transporting oxygen around the body. 

## Metabolism of protein, carbohydrates & fats 

- Vitamins B6 and B12 are co-enzymes required for various stages of protein, carbohydrate and fat metabolism. These nutrients are needed for several conversion reactions to occur during glycolysis and within the kerbs-cycle and electron transport chain pathways. 

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Several medications may deplete folate status, including antacids (PPIs), trimethoprim (antibiotic), pyrimethamine (antimalarial), triamterene (blood pressure), sulfasalazine (for ulcerative colitis) and oral contraceptives. Separate dose by 2-3 hours. 

- Caution with methotrexate (folic acid antagonist) – co-administration with folate may reduce the effects. Patients should take folate only under the supervision of a health professional. 

- Caution with antiepileptic medications – folic acid may reduce serum levels of these medications. Patients should take folate only under the supervision of a health professional. 

- Caution with anticonvulsant medications (phenobarbital/ phenobarbitone and phenytoin) – folic acid and vitamin B6 may reduce serum levels of these medications. Patients should take this combination only under the supervision of a health professional. 

- Caution with cholestyramine and colestipol (hypolipidaemic agents) - drugs may decrease the absorption of folate. Separate dose by at least 4-6 hours. 

- Caution with levodopa – coadministration with B6 alone should be avoided as B6 reduces drug effects. However, this effect is prevented by the administration of a dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor (e.g. benserazide, carbidopa) with levodopa, as is common clinical practice. 

- Caution with drugs containing iodine, e.g. amiodarone (antineoplastic agent) – concurrent use with iodine can increase iodine levels and may affect thyroid function. Monitor thyroid function.

- None noted at the recommended dose.

- Supplemental vitamin B6 may cause nausea, vomiting, headaches, paraesthesia and sleepiness (usually at higher doses). 

- Taking vitamin B6 at night may result in more vivid dreams.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- The Ginkgo biloba tree is believed to be the world’s oldest living tree, dating back more than 250 million years. The tree is now cultivated in Asia, Europe, North America, New Zealand and Argentina. The medicinal use of Ginkgo can be traced back to 2800 BC in Chinese medicine, where it was used for brain disorders, circulatory disorders, respiratory conditions, urinary tract conditions and as an antiparasitic. 

- Ginkgo contains more than 30 genuine flavonoids, of which the 

- flavanol glycosides, found in the leaves, are the most abundant. 

- Ginkgo Biloba 6000 contains Ginkgo extract standardised to 28.8mg of Ginkgo flavonglycosides per capsule. Flavonglycosides have antioxidant activity and reduce free radicals formed in the body. 

## Cognitive function & memory 

- Ginkgo Biloba 6000 supports cognitive function, brain health and memory. 

- The brain requires large amounts of energy to function properly in the form of glucose and oxygen. Decreased or impaired circulation impacts both membrane function and energy production. By maintaining blood flow to the brain, Ginkgo enhances oxygen utilisation and improves cellular uptake of glucose, thereby restoring energy production in the brain. 

- Ginkgo helps to increase nerve cell transmission rate, improve synthesis and turnover of brain neurotransmitters and helps to normalise acetylcholine receptors in the hippocampus, an area of the brain involved in emotions, feelings and memory processing. 

- Cerebral vascular insufficiency is particularly common in the elderly due to changes within the artery walls. This can lead to impaired mental performance, such as mood disturbance, short term memory loss and decreased alertness. Ginkgo increases blood flow to the brain to help maintain cognitive function and memory during ageing. 

## Blood circulation 

- Ginkgo Biloba 6000 supports healthy blood circulation, including to the peripheral areas of the body (legs, hands and feet) and maintains blood capillary health. 

- Ginkgo has numerous effects on the vascular system, mainly in the vascular endothelium (lining of blood vessels) and modifies blood vessel tone. Ginkgo has a vasodilatory effect that helps to normalise circulation while inhibiting relaxation of the blood vessels. 

- Insufficient peripheral circulation usually occurs from obstruction or narrowing of the peripheral arteries and leads to decreased blood flow during exercise or rest. This causes ischemia (decreased oxygenated blood) to the peripheral parts of the body causing pain and dysfunction. 

Ischemia can lead to the development of peripheral vascular difficulties, characterised by cold hands and feet, and intermittent claudication which causes cramp-like pain in the calf muscles. 

- Ginkgo inhibits platelet aggregation and adhesion of red blood cells. Platelet activating factor (PAF) is a potent inflammatory mediator and can initiate increased vascular permeability, smooth muscle contractions and decreased coronary blood flow. Ginkgo competes with PAF for binding onto PAF receptor sites and therefore inhibits PAF related events. 

- A meta-analysis of 5 placebo-controlled clinical trials of Ginkgo extract in patients with peripheral arterial conditions concluded that Ginkgo exerted a highly significant therapeutic effect[1] . Another 2 studies showed an increase in walking distance in patients with intermittent claudication after 6 months[2] , and an improvement of pain at rest in patients given 200mg of Ginkgo extract for 8 weeks[3] . 

## Cardiovascular health 

- Ginkgo Biloba 6000 supports cardiovascular system health. 

- Through its role as a vasodilator, Ginkgo improves blood flow through the arteries, veins and capillaries, increasing blood flow to these areas. 

- Ginkgo exerts its cardioprotective activity through its antioxidant, antiplatelet, antithrombotic and vasodilatory properties.

- Globally, 25 million Ginkgo trees are harvested each year to meet the demands for Ginkgo as a medicinal product. The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) lists Ginkgo as “endangered” due to the rapid decline in the number of trees around the world[4] . 

- Herbs of Gold Ginkgo Biloba 6000 uses Ginkgo extract that is 100% from sustainably sourced, plantation grown Ginkgo in order to meet the requirements of protecting endangered species.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Ginseng 4 Energy Gold contains a synergistic blend of four different ginsengs used in traditional Western and Ayurvedic medicine to support energy production and relieve weariness, fatigue and feelings of debility. 

- Ginseng 4 Energy Gold contains herbs known as adaptogens. ## Energy production & the stress response 

- Ginseng 4 Energy Gold contains four ginsengs plus Astragalus to support energy production. 

- Korean ginseng is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine to help enhance physical capacity and performance, especially in cases of physical stress. It is also used as an adaptogen to help increase energy and resistance to stress. 

- The Commission E has approved Korean ginseng and Siberian ginseng as tonics for invigoration and fortification in times of fatigue and debility or declining capacity for work and concentration[2,3] . 

- The activity of Korean ginseng appears to be based on whole body effects, rather than particular organs or systems, which lends support to the traditional view that Ginseng is a tonic that can revitalise the functioning of the body as a whole. 

- Siberian ginseng has been used for over 2000 years in China as a folk 

- remedy and as a tonic to restore vigour, improve general health and increase stamina. 

- American ginseng is traditionally used in Chinese medicine to support a healthy stress response in the body. After the USA won independence from Great Britain in 1783, the first USA-China trade ship carried 30 tons of American ginseng to China to kick-start their economy. The Chinese viewed the American ginseng as being complementary to their own native ginseng. Siberian ginseng is considered warm and ideal for people who have recovered from illness and need to regain their strength; on the other hand, American ginseng has cooler properties and is normally used to cool down mild fevers or summer heat. Chinese medicine considers it good for people with deficient yin or excessive yang. 

- Ashwagandha is often referred to as ‘Indian ginseng’ because it is used in much the same way in Ayurvedic medicine as Korean ginseng in traditional Chinese medicine, although it is considered less stimulating. Ashwagandha is a gentle adaptogen, traditionally used for improving stress adaptation responses in people who are both physically and emotionally stressed and exhausted. Ashwagandha improves the response to stress, possibly via an action on the adrenal glands, and possesses anti-inflammatory and sedative properties. Ashwagandha is used to assist with nervous exhaustion, convalescence and debility. 

- Both Astragalus and Korean ginseng are the principal herbs for strengthening Qi, the body’s vital force, and have been used for over 2000 years in traditional Chinese medicine to support stamina and endurance and to relieve fatigue.
