Magnesium glycinate is a form of magnesium amino acid chelate, with the magnesium attached to the amino acid glycine, which, as the smallest amino acid, is readily absorbed across the intestinal wall. Magnesium orotate is magnesium attached to orotic acid, which carries the mineral across cell membranes. 

- Magnesium is an essential nutrient for over 300 enzymatic processes in the body, required for DNA replication, energy production, muscle contraction and relaxation, cardiac rhythm, vascular tone, DNA and RNA synthesis, carbohydrate, protein and fat metabolism, bone formation, cell signalling, neurological function and brain function. 

- Magnesium is found in green leafy vegetables, nuts, seeds, whole grains and cacao. Today’s farming and agricultural practices have led to a decline in the magnesium content in foods, with estimates that magnesium content has decreased by as much as 80-90% in vegetables such as lettuce and spinach[2] . Modern dietary practices, such as cooking and bleaching grain, causes a loss of up to 80% of magnesium content. As a result, magnesium deficiency is becoming increasingly prevalent. Magnesium Forte helps prevent dietary magnesium deficiency. 

- Under normal dietary conditions, about 30% of ingested magnesium is absorbed. Magnesium homeostasis is maintained via the intestine (facilitating magnesium absorption), the bone (magnesium storage) and the kidneys (excretion). The largest amount of magnesium is stored in bone (50-60%), muscle (20-30%) and other soft tissues (20%). 

## Muscle health 

- Magnesium is an essential nutrient for muscle health and muscle contraction function. Magnesium works with calcium for muscle contraction and relaxation. Magnesium is a calcium antagonist, competing with calcium for binding sites. In the resting state, magnesium is present in concentrations 10 000 times higher than calcium in muscle cells. When the message comes for a muscle to contract, calcium is released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum and binds to troponin C and myosin to induce contraction. When magnesium levels are insufficient, not as much calcium is required to 

displace magnesium, resulting in muscle cramps and spasms. 

## Energy production & glucose metabolism 

- Magnesium supports energy production as it is involved in the metabolism of carbohydrates and fats to produce energy and is critical for the manufacture of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) within cells. ATP exists primarily as a complex with magnesium (MgATP). 

- Magnesium is an important cofactor in glucose metabolism and glycaemic control. It is essential for insulin receptor phosphorylation and regulates glucose uptake in muscle[3] . 

## Nervous system health 

- Magnesium supports healthy nervous system function as it is required for nerve conduction. It modulates the hypothalamic pituitary adrenal axis and can reduce the release of adrenalin and noradrenalin, supporting a healthy stress response in the body. 

## Cardiovascular system health 

- Magnesium helps maintain cardiovascular system health and heart health. It is essential for cardiac muscle contraction and production of energy within the heart muscle. Magnesium plays a role in the active transport of calcium and potassium ions across cell membranes, which is essential for nerve impulse conduction, muscle contraction and normal heart rhythm. It is also essential for the contractility of vascular smooth muscle cells in the arterial wall and influences endothelial function, thereby influencing vasodilation and vasoconstriction. 

## Bone health 

- Magnesium supports bone health and assists in the development and maintenance of bones and teeth. Approximately 50-60% of total body magnesium stores reside in the bone, where it binds at the surface of the hydroxyapatite crystals. Magnesium in bones serves as a reservoir of magnesium, which can be released from bone to maintain physiological extracellular concentrations when magnesium intake is low. 

## Menstrual cramps & spasms 

   - Magnesium Forte can help relieve symptoms of premenstrual tension including menstrual cramps and spasms and dysmenorrhoea. 

   - Dysmenorrhoea is defined as painful uterine cramps that precede or accompany menses and is caused by hypercontractility of the myometrium and arteriolar vasoconstriction. Magnesium can help alleviate this via its muscle relaxation and vasodilation activity as well as by inhibiting the biosynthesis of prostaglandin F2 (PGF2) alpha.

## **Magnesium Forte** 

- A systematic review of three small studies found that overall magnesium supplementation was more effective than placebo for pain relief and reduced the need for additional medication[4] . 

- There is no clear dosage recommendations, as studies used different dosage regimes, however, magnesium appears to be effective when taken daily, or taken between one and seven days prior to menses and for the first two or three days of menstruation. 

- Current research suggests that at least two months’ supplementation are required to see a benefit in other symptoms of premenstrual tension[5] . A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled cross over study investigated the effects of 200mg of magnesium as magnesium oxide for 2 menstrual cycles. In the second month, there was a greater reduction (p=0.009) in symptoms of PMS-H, including weight gain, swelling of extremities, breast tenderness and abdominal bloating[6] . 

## Pregnancy 

- Magnesium supports a healthy pregnancy as it is an essential nutrient for a range of biological reactions in the body and has a structural role in bone formation. 

- Pregnancy increases magnesium requirements. The recommend daily intake of magnesium increases from 320mg to between 350 and 400mg per day during pregnancy. 

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Caution with quinolone antibiotics – magnesium forms insoluble complexes with quinolones, decreasing drug absorption. Take drug 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium. 

- Caution with tetracycline antibiotics – tetracyclines form insoluble complexes with magnesium, reducing absorption of both. Separate dose by at least 3 hours. 

- Caution with bisphosphonates – magnesium can form complexes with drug and reduce absorption. Separate dose by 2 hours. 

- Caution with calcium channel blockers and other hypotensive medications – magnesium may have additive effects and enhance the hypotensive effect. Monitor blood pressure. 

- Caution with potassium-sparing diuretics – these drugs also have magnesium-sparing properties which could, theoretically, lead to increased magnesium levels. Monitor. 

- Caution with skeletal muscle relaxants – magnesium can potentiate effects. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- High dose magnesium is contraindicated in people with compromised renal function and heart block. 

- Caution in individuals with low blood pressure – magnesium supplementation can lower blood pressure. Monitor. 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- Magnesium can cause gastrointestinal irritation, nausea and diarrhoea in sensitive individuals, however, usually in much higher doses.

- The skin is the largest organ of the body, covering approximately 1.8m[2] and comprises approximately 10% of total body mass[3] . ## Sleep 

- Sleep is an essential process that refreshes the mind and allows the body to repair. Today, many people do not get the recommended 7-9 hours’ sleep, sleeping for 6-7 hours or less. 

- Poor sleep leads to fatigue, poor concentration and memory, mood disturbances, impaired judgement and reaction time and poor coordination. Lack of sleep long term is associated with poor health outcomes. 

- Poor sleep can be caused by many factors, including shift work, travel across time zones, illness, some medications, internet and social media usage and poor sleep hygiene. 

- Sleep occurs in phases. Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep occurs regularly during sleep, about once every 90-120 minutes and is the time where most dreams occur. Non-REM sleep makes up about 75%

of sleep time and is broken down into stages: 

- Stage 1: drowsiness, somewhere between asleep and awake 

- Stage 2: loss of awareness of surroundings, body temperature drops and breathing and heart rate slow 

- Stage 3 & 4 (deep sleep/‘delta sleep’): heart rate and breathing slow, muscles relax. This is the time body growth and repair takes place. 

- Magnesium Night Plus can be taken before bed to promote relaxation and sleep. It contains nutrients that support nervous system health and herbs traditionally used in Western herbal medicine (WHM) to promote sleep. 

- Glutamine is a precursor to gamma aminobutyric acid (GABA), an inhibitory neurotransmitter that reduces neuronal firing, promoting calmness and relaxation. GABAA receptors play a role in the initiation and maintenance of non-REM sleep. 

- Magnesium has a role in sleep regulation via its action as a 

- N-methyl-D-aspartic acid (NMDA) antagonist and GABA agonist. It is also a cofactor for serotonin synthesis, which is involved in sleep. 

- A double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled clinical trial was conducted in 46 elderly subjects with sleep difficulties. Eight week supplementation with 250mg of magnesium twice daily led to a statistically significant increase in sleep time (p=0.002), sleep efficiency (p=0.03) and concentration of serum melatonin (p=0.007) and significantly decreased sleep onset latency (p=0.02) and serum cortisol concentration (p=0.008)[3] . The study used 500mg of magnesium daily as oxide. As magnesium citrate and glycinate have significantly better absorption, it is reasonable to assume that a lower dose of organic magnesium would be sufficient. 

- In an analysis using data from the 2007-2008 NHANES (n=4552), higher calcium intake was associated with decreased difficulty falling asleep and a lower calcium intake was associated with nonrestorative sleep[4] . 

- Passionflower and California poppy are both used traditionally in 

- WHM as soporifics to induce sleep. 

- The King’s American Dispensatory (1898) describes Passionflower as “a rest-producing agent…specifically useful to allay restlessness and overcome wakefulness, when these are the result of exhaustion, or the nervous excitement of debility…It gives sleep to those who are labouring under the effects of mental worry or from mental overwork”[5] . 

- The King’s American Dispensatory says of California poppy “its action is pronounced valuable, quieting pain and producing calm sleep”[6] . 

- Passionflower is also traditionally used in WHM as a sedative and an antispasmodic, while California poppy is considered a sedative and an analgesic to relieve pain, so it may be beneficial for those with impaired sleep due to pain or discomfort. 

## Mild anxiety 

- Passionflower is traditionally used in WHM to relieve symptoms of mild anxiety. 

- Traditionally, Passionflower and California poppy are considered to be calmatives, to relax the nervous system and relieve restlessness and excess nervous energy. 

- The traditional use of Passionflower has been backed up by science as in vitro studies have shown that the herb affects GABAA and GABAB channels and affects GABA uptake into neurons. GABA is the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter that counterbalances the action of the excitatory neurotransmitter glutamate. 

- A double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled study investigated the effects of Passionflower for pre-operative anxiety. Sixty patients were randomised to receive 500mg Passiflora incarnata or placebo as a premedication 90 minutes before surgery. The anxiety scores were significantly lower in the Passionflower group than in the control group (p<0.001) with no effect on recovery of psychomotor function. 

The study concluded that Passionflower as a premedication reduces anxiety without inducing sedation[7] . 

- A pilot study, with a double-blind, randomised design, compared the efficacy of Passionflower with oxazepam (benzodiazepine) in 36 outpatients with generalised anxiety. Patients received either 45 drops Passionflower extract plus placebo, or 30mg oxazepam plus placebo drops for 4 weeks. Both Passionflower and oxazepam relieved anxiety – oxazepam had a more rapid onset of action, however, there were no significant differences between the two protocols at the end of the trial[8] . 

- A recent randomised, controlled, double-blind crossover clinical study compared the effects of Passionflower and midazolam for anxiety in 40 patients undergoing mandibular third molar extraction. Participants received either Passionflower 260mg or midazolam 15mg 30 minutes before surgery. Anxiety levels were evaluated by questionnaires, heart rate, blood pressure and oxygen saturation. There were no significant differences (p>0.05) between the two protocols, showing Passionflower has an anxiolytic effect similar to midazolam[9] .

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Mega B Complex contains all 8 B vitamins including B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B12, biotin (B7) and folic acid (B9), as well as choline and inositol. 

- B vitamins perform essential, closely inter-related roles in the body to support cellular functioning and act as co-enzymes in a vast array of catabolic and anabolic enzymatic reactions. Their most important role is to convert carbohydrates, protein and fat into energy. 

- Choline and inositol are both members of the B vitamin family. Choline is necessary for the structure and function of cells and inositol is involved in the transport and metabolism of fats. 

- B vitamins are not synthesised by the body and therefore must be taken through the diet. 

- In terms of their origins, B vitamins are typically synthesised by plants. However, humans obtain most of their B vitamins from higher up the food chain in foods of animal origin, such as meat, dairy and eggs. 

- B vitamins are water soluble, meaning the body is unable to store them in large amounts. As such, regular daily intake is required to support general health. 

- B vitamins work synergistically in the body, so are best when taken together. 

- Mega B Complex is suitable for preconception, pregnancy and breastfeeding, when increased vitamins are required. Mega B Complex provides a daily dose of 400 micrograms of folinic acid to support healthy foetal development. 

- Folinic acid (5-formlyTHF), is a more active form of folate than folic acid as it by passes the di-hydrofolate reductase step in the folic acid metabolism pathway. Individuals with a MTHRF gene mutation have difficulty producing the enzyme which converts folic acid to the active forms folinic acid and methylfolate. Providing folinic acid as an active form of folate bypasses this step. 

## Energy production 

- The B vitamins collectively function as coenzymes involved in mitochondrial energy production, supporting normal digestion and the conversion of food into energy. 

- B vitamins are essential to the proper functioning of the Krebs cycle in the mitochondria. The Krebs cycle is responsible for producing 

adenosine triphosphate (ATP), the primary energy carrier in all cells. 

## Nervous system health 

- Mega B Complex supports healthy nervous system function. 

- Vitamins B1, B5, B6, B12 and folinic acid play an important role in the synthesis of neurotransmitters to support the function and health of the nervous system. 

- Vitamin B1 is essential for the metabolism of acetylcholine, gamma aminobutyric acid (GABA) and serotonin. 

- Vitamin B5, commonly called the anti-stress vitamin, is involved in the synthesis of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine. Acetylcholine plays an important role in adrenal function and is required for the proper functioning of the adrenal cortex and the synthesis of steroid hormones, namely cortisone. 

- Vitamin B6 is involved in the conversion of tryptophan to niacin, the synthesis of GABA in the central nervous system as well as the metabolism of serotonin, norepinephrine and dopamine. 

- Folate and vitamin B12 play an important role in the development, differentiation and functioning of the CNS through methioninehomocysteine metabolism. Methionine becomes activated to S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe), which is indispensable for numerous reactions involving methylation, for example, the synthesis of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA), proteins, neurotransmitters and hormones. 

- Serotonin and dopamine are neurotransmitters that play a role in an individual’s mood and wellbeing. Dopamine plays a role in controlling the movements a person makes, as well as their emotional responses. Serotonin is used to transmit messages between nerve cells and contributes to feelings of wellbeing and happiness. 

- Vitamin B12 is also required for the proper functioning and development of the brain and nerve cells. It is essential for the myelin sheath that covers and protects the nerves of the central and the peripheral nervous systems, ensuring fast and effective nerveimpulse transmission. 

## Cardiovascular health 

- Mega B Complex maintains cardiovascular system health and blood health.

## **Mega B Complex** 

- Vitamins B6, B12 and folinic acid are required for homocysteine metabolism and assist the conversion of homocysteine to methionine. High homocysteine levels are associated with a higher risk of cardiovascular conditions. 

- Vitamins B6, B12 and folinic acid are important for the production of red blood cells, cell growth and cell reproduction. Vitamins B6 and B12 are also required for the synthesis of haemoglobin, the oxygencarrying pigment in red blood cells. 

## Skin health 

- Vitamins B2 and B5 support skin health. 

- Vitamin B2 promotes normal growth and tissue repair. It is required for the growth of skin, hair and nails while vitamin B5 regulates the epidermal barrier function and keratinocytes differentiation via CoA metabolism, playing an essential role in normal epithelial function. 

## Cognitive function 

- Folinic acid and vitamin B12 are important nutrients to support cognitive function and brain health. 

- More than 77 cross-sectional studies including more than 34,000 subjects have reported a significant association between low blood levels of folate and vitamin B12 and poor cognitive function[1] . 

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Contraindicated with pyrimethamine (antimalarial) – folate may reduce drug effectiveness. 

- Caution with tetracycline antibiotics - concurrent administration with B2 and B12 may decrease the effectiveness of the medication. Separate dose. 

- Caution with chloramphenicol (broad spectrum antibiotic) – folinic acid and B12 may impact drug metabolism. Separate dose. 

- Caution with anticholinergic drugs – may reduce absorption of vitamin B2. Separate dose. 

- Caution with carbamazepine and primidone – vitamin B3 and folate may impact drug metabolism, resulting in increased drug levels in the body. Monitor. 

- Caution with levodopa – vitamin B6 may reduce drug effects. However, this effect is prevented by the administration of a dopadecarboxylase inhibitor (e.g. benserazide, carbidopa) with levodopa, as is common clinical practice. 

- Caution with phenobarbital/phenobarbitone and phenytoin (anticonvulsants) - vitamin B6 and folate may reduce serum concentrations of these drugs. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- B vitamins are stimulatory in nature. To avoid any sleep interference, it is recommended you do not take B vitamin supplements at night before bed. 

- Taking at night may result in more vivid dreams (vitamin B6). 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- Supplemental B vitamins may cause nausea or mild gastrointestinal upset if taken on an empty stomach. Best taken with food to reduce risk. 

- Riboflavin can impart a bright yellow colour to urine.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Memory & Cognition Gold contains a combination of herbs and nutrients to support cognitive function and memory recall. 

- Brahmi, Ginkgo and Rosemary are herbs that provide antioxidant support to help reduce free radical damage in the body. The brain is particularly susceptible to oxidative stress as it is metabolically active, possesses high levels of pro-oxidant iron, and is composed of unsaturated lipids prone to lipid peroxidation. The blood-brain barrier prevents many exogenous antioxidants from quenching reactive oxygen species (ROS) in the brain. 

- Memory & Cognition Gold contains methylcobalmin (mecobalamin), the metabolically active coenzyme form of vitamin B12 that is ready for use in the body. 

- Memory & Cognition Gold contains methylfolate as Quatrefolic[®] , the glucosamine salt of (6S)-5-methyltetrahydrofolate. Quatrefolic[®] is an active form of folate, immediately available for its biological action without being metabolised in the body. 

## Brahmi 

- Brahmi is a well-known herb in India with a long history of use in Ayurvedic herbal preparations. The Ayurvedic action for Brahmi in Sanskrit is 'medhya rasayana', which translates to 'herbs which rejuvenate the mind[1] . 

- Brahmi is traditonally used in Ayurvedic medicine as a brain tonic to enhance brain health and improve memory and cognitive performance. It is noted in traditional texts to increase memory, learning ability and concentration. 

- Memory & Cognition Gold contains BacoMind[®] , a patented extract of Brahmi clinically researched for memory and cognition enhancing properties. It is a unique full-spectrum phytochemical composition containing 9 different bio-actives. BacoMind[®] is standardised for bacoside A, bacopaside I, bacopaside II, bacopasaponin C, jujubogenin isomer of bacopasaponin C, bacosine, luteolin, apigenin and β-sitosterol D glucoside. 

- Brahmi enhances cognitive performance and supports mental concentration and focus. BacoMind[®] has been clinically trialled for its memory and cognitive enhancing properties in children, adolescents and elderly individuals. 

- A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated the used of BacoMind[®] on 65 elderly individuals with memory impairment without cognitive deficit. Subjects were given 450mg/day BacoMind[®] extract for 12 weeks. Results showed improved cognitive functions such as attention and verbal memory in the BacoMind[®] group1. 

- Another randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study assessed the use of BacoMind[®] on 98 healthy elderly subjects. Participants were randomised to receive 300mg/day of BacoMind[®] extract or an identical placebo. Significant improvements in memory acquisition, memory retention and verbal learning were achieved after 12 weeks compared to baseline in the BacoMind[®] group[2] . 

- In an open-labelled study, 28 children and adolescents aged 4-18 years received a 225mg of BacoMind[®] for 4 months. A significant improvement (p<0.05) was seen in immediate and working memory as well as visual and auditory memory from baseline[3] . 

## Ginkgo 

- Memory & Cognition Gold contains Ginkgo standardised to Ginkgo flavonglycosides to support brain health and cognitive function. 

- The brain requires large amounts of energy to function properly in the form of glucose and oxygen. Decreased or impaired circulation impacts both membrane function and energy production. By maintaining blood flow to the brain, Ginkgo enhances oxygen utilisation and improves cellular uptake of glucose, thereby supporting energy production in the brain. 

- Ginkgo helps increase nerve cell transmission rate, improve synthesis and turnover of brain neurotransmitters and helps normalise acetylcholine receptors in the hippocampus, an area of the brain involved in emotions, feelings and memory processing[4] . 

- Ginkgo helps maintain cognitive function and memory during aging. 

- In a 30-day randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial, 61 participants aged 18 to 40 years were administered a battery of validated neuropsychological tests before and after treatment with either placebo or 6g Ginkgo daily for 30 days. Statistical analysis indicated significant improvements in speed of information processing, working memory speed (p<0.05) and memory consolidation (p<0.001)[5] .

## Rosemary 

- Memory & Cognition Gold contains Rosemary, a potent antioxidant to help reduce free radicals formed in the body. 

- Rosemary is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine to support brain health, cognitive function and mental clarity. It has been used to strengthen memory function and improve concentration since ancient times. 

- Dioscorides wrote of rosemary: ‘‘the eating of its flower in a preserve comforts the brain, the heart and the stomach; sharpens understanding, restores lost memory and awakens the mind”[6] . 

- In a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 28 students aged 20-25 years received 500mg of dried Rosemary twice daily, or placebo for 1 month. Prospective and retrospective memory performance was measured using self-reported questionnaires at baseline and after 1 month. The group receiving Rosemary had significantly enhanced memory performance compared to the placebo group[7] . 

## Nutrients 

- Memory & Cognition Gold contains phosphatidylserine as well as the active forms of folate and vitamin B12 ready for use in the body. 

- Phosphatidylserine is the major phospholipid in the brain and comprises 13-15% of the human cerebral cortex[8] . It is important for cellular communication, as it helps the transfer of signals between brain cells, and is vital for cognitive function. Phosphatidylserine has been widely studied for improving cognitive function and ageassociated memory impairment[9] . 

- Vitamin B12 supports brain health and healthy cognition. The European Food Safety Authority concluded that there is a causeand-effect relationship between the dietary intake of vitamin B12 and contribution to normal neurological and psychological functions[10] . Low B12 status is associated with more rapid cognitive decline in older adults[11] . 

- Ginkgo may reduce drug effectiveness. The main classes of drugs include antidepressants, anticonvulsants and immunosuppressants. 

- Caution with blood pressure medication – Ginkgo may reduce drug effectiveness. Monitor blood pressure. 

- Caution with iron supplements – Rosemary may reduce the absorption of iron. Separate dose by 2 hours. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- Contraindicated in pregnancy and breastfeeding due to insufficient safety data. 

- Caution in hyperthyroidism – Brahmi can theoretically elevate T4 levels. 

- Discontinue use 7 days before any surgery. 

- Avoid in people with epilepsy - Ginkgo may promote seizure activity. 

- Rosemary is high in salicylates. 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- Side effects are rare but can include mild gastrointestinal disturbances such as nausea, abdominal cramps and increased stool frequency (Brahmi).

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Men’s Multi + contains a blend of essential vitamins, minerals, nutrients and herbs to support men’s health. 

- Men’s Multi + contains antioxidant nutrients, including vitamin C, citrus bioflavonoids, vitamin E, zinc, selenium and alpha Lipoic acid to help reduce free radical damage. Vitamin C is the most important water-soluble antioxidant in the body, while vitamin E is a fat-soluble antioxidant whose major role is to protect polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA) from oxidation. Men’s Multi + also contains lycopene which, with zinc and selenium, supports prostate health. 

- Men’s Multi + contains nutrients, including vitamin C, vitamin E, vitamin D, zinc and selenium, and Siberian ginseng to support immune system function. 

- Men’s Multi + contains nutrients that support blood health and assist healthy red blood cell production. Iron, folate, vitamin B12 and copper help the formation of red blood cells in the body and support normal blood function. 

- Men’s Multi + contains chromium to assist sugar and carbohydrate metabolism. Chromium assists in the uptake of glucose into the cells by stimulating insulin uptake and enhancing its activity. Requirements for chromium are increased when consuming a diet high in sugar. 

## B vitamins 

- Men’s Multi + contains therapeutic doses of all the B group vitamins, plus the active form of folate and vitamin B12. 

- As B vitamins are water soluble, regular daily intake is required to 

support general health. B vitamins work synergistically in the body and are, therefore, best taken together. 

- B vitamins support energy production, assist sugar and carbohydrate metabolism and help convert carbohydrates and protein into energy. 

- Men’s Multi + contains methylfolate (5-MTHF), the active form of folate. Folate is the generic term for a large family of chemically similar compounds known as vitamin B9. Folic acid is a synthetic form of the vitamin and must be reduced to methylfolate for use in the body. 

- Many people have mutations on the MTHFR gene, which affects their ability to convert folic acid into the active form (40-70% reduction in activity of the MTHFR enzyme). Methylfolate is a good alternative in individuals with MTHFR mutations as it is ready for use in the body and does not require conversion. 

- Men’s Multi + contains methylcobalamin (mecobalamin), the metabolically-active coenzyme form of vitamin B12 that is ready for use in the body. Commonly used cyanocobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 that does not occur naturally in foods and needs to be converted to methylcobalamin for use in the body. Methylcobalamin differs from cyanocobalamin in that the non-toxic cyanide molecule is replaced by a methyl group. 

## Nervous system 

- Men’s Multi + supports nervous system health and a healthy stress response in the body.

## **Men's Multi +** 

- B vitamins are involved in nerve impulse transmission and the synthesis of neurotransmitters, including acetylcholine, gammaaminobutyric acid (GABA), dopamine and serotonin, so they have a role in emotional balance and mood. Vitamin B12 is important for the manufacture of the myelin sheath, the protective sheath surrounding many nerves. Vitamins B5 and B6 help support a healthy stress response in the body as they are required for the synthesis of the adrenal hormones adrenaline and noradrenaline. 

- Vitamin B5, as coenzyme A, is needed for healthy adrenal cortex function and the synthesis of steroid hormones, including cortisone. 

- Methylfolate and vitamin B12 support brain health, cognitive function and memory. 

## Skin health 

- Men’s Multi + contains nutrients, vitamin C, vitamin E, zinc and copper, that support healthy skin, connective tissue formation and wound healing. 

- Vitamin C is found in the epidermis and the dermis of the skin, where it acts as an antioxidant, protecting against free radical damage, including UV-induced photodamage. Vitamin C also enhances collagen synthesis and stabilisation, enhances keratinocyte differentiation and improves wound healing. Vitamin E is the major naturally-occurring lipid-soluble antioxidant protecting the skin from oxidative stress. 

## Thyroid health 

- Men’s Multi + contains iodine and selenium, which help maintain healthy thyroid function and assist thyroid hormone production. Iodine is a precursor for thyroid hormones, required for normal growth and metabolism. Selenium is required for normal thyroid hormone synthesis, activation and metabolism. 

## Sperm health 

- Men’s Multi + supports sperm health and sperm motility. The membranes of spermatozoa are very sensitive to oxidation. Vitamin C is present in seminal fluid and in sperm where it functions as an antioxidant. Vitamin E helps protect sperm membranes from oxidation and supports sperm motility. 

- Zinc is required for spermatogenesis and sperm health. It is highly concentrated in the tail of mature sperm and is important for sperm motility. Selenium supports optimal thyroid metabolism, important for sperm production, and supports normal sperm maturation and motility. 

## Vitamin D 

- Men’s Multi + contains 1000IU of vegan-friendly vitamin D3, the maximum daily dose in a listed medicine. Vitamin D supports bone density and strength. 

- Vitamin D assists the intestinal absorption of calcium and phosphorus, helping to maintain serum calcium concentrations. Research shows that in low vitamin D states, the small intestine absorbs approximately 10-15% of dietary calcium. When vitamin D levels are adequate, the small intestine can absorb 30-40%[1] . A diet deficient in calcium can lead to osteoporosis in later life. The National Osteoporosis Foundations guidelines (2014) recommend a daily intake of 8001000IU vitamin D daily with calcium for preventing osteoporosis in adults over 50 years of age[2] . 

- Vitamin D supports bone health independent of calcium. It is actively involved in bone formation and bone remodelling by osteoblasts and osteoclasts, resorption and mineralisation. Research shows that vitamin D with or without calcium can reduce the risk of all fractures by 8% to 17%, nonvertebral fractures by 14% to 49% and hip fractures by 9% to 30% in older adults[3] . 

- Vitamin D supports muscle function and helps maintain muscle strength. It has a role in the regulation and uptake of calcium in muscle cells, which is important for muscle strength, muscle contraction, mitochondrial function and insulin sensitivity. 

## Tribulus & Damiana 

- Men’s Multi + contains Tribulus, which has a long history of use in 

Greek, Chinese and Indian traditional medicine as an aphrodisiac to promote healthy libido. In traditional Ayurvedic medicine, Tribulus is considered “Vrishya” (aphrodisiac) and used to increase virility. 

- Damiana is traditionally used in Mexican and Western herbal medicine (WHM) as an aphrodisiac and nerve tonic. 

## Siberian ginseng & Ashwagandha

## Menopause 

- The word menopause means ‘stopping menstruation’ and is comprised of the Greek meno (monthly) and pausis (to stop). Menopause can only be diagnosed retrospectively, when the last menstrual period has occurred 12 months or more previously. Menopause occurring between the ages of 45–55 is considered normal, with the average age of menopause being 50–51 years. 

- Menopausal symptoms are experienced in varied combinations by different women, with some women experiencing severe symptoms while others experience none. It is estimated 20% of women have no symptoms, 60% have a few or mild symptoms, and the other 20% experience change across the spectrum. Symptoms last from a few months to ten years or more. Twenty-five percent of women experience symptoms for greater than five years and 10% experience symptoms for more than ten years[2] . 

- Perimenopause refers to the period before menopause, when menopausal symptoms begin. Menopausal transition occurs from the two to six years preceding cessation of menses to the twelve months after the final menstrual period. This is the period when symptoms are generally most prevalent. 

- The typical symptoms of peri-menopausal transition include irregular menses, hot flushes, sleeplessness or sleep difficulties, night sweats, weight gain, mood changes, joint pain and stiffness, lowered libido and vaginal dryness. These symptoms are the result of fluctuations in oestrogen and progesterone, rather than declining oestrogen. 

- The most well recognised symptom of menopause is hot flushes. The individual experience of hot flushes varies greatly among women. While some experience transient episodes of feeling slightly hot and sweaty, others may be drenched in perspiration, go red in the face and be troubled by palpitations. Bothersome hot flushes have been shown to be significantly related to oestrogen decline and elevated FSH levels. 

## Sage 

- Sage has a long history of traditional use in Western herbal medicine for treating sweating and menopausal hot flushes, as well as to alleviate associated menopausal symptoms and as a general tonic. 

- A trial was conducted in Switzerland in 2011 on 71 peri-menopausal women who were treated with a once-daily tablet of fresh Sage 

- leaves for 8 weeks. Efficacy was evaluated based on the change in intensity and frequency of hot flushes, and total score of the mean number of intensity-rated hot flushes (TSIRHF). There was a significant decrease in the TSIRHF by 50% within 4 weeks and by 64% within 8 weeks (p<0.0001). The mean total number of hot flushes per day decreased significantly each week from week 1 to 8. The mean number of mild, moderate, severe and very severe flushes decreased by 46%, 62%, 79% and 100% over 8 weeks, respectively[3] . 

- Sage binds to complex GABA benzodiazepines receptors in the brain, helping to increase oestrogen levels in the body and improve symptoms of spontaneous sweating and night sweats.

## Energy 

- Muscle Resuscitation supports energy production. 

- Magnesium and B vitamins are involved in the breakdown of carbohydrates, proteins and fats and have central roles in cellular energy production. Vitamin B1 is a vital coenzyme in the production of energy in cells. Vitamin B2 is an essential part of the coenzymes FMN and FAD that play central roles in ATP production. Vitamin B3 is a precursor for the coenzymes NAD+ and NADP, which are involved in cellular respiration and ATP production. The active form of vitamin B5, CoA, is involved in the breakdown of fatty acids and sugars into energy. 

- L-glutamine is broken down to produce energy. 

- Carnitine assists the transport of fat across cell membranes in muscle tissue for use as an energy source. 

- Muscle Resuscitation contains chromium, magnesium and zinc to assist healthy glucose metabolism. Chromium is a component of glucose tolerance factor (GTF), which enhances the action of insulin, facilitating glucose uptake into cells. 

## Exercise 

- Muscle Resuscitation can assist exercise capacity and performance as well as recovery after exercise. 

- Athletes and people who engage in strenuous exercise have increased requirements for magnesium. Exercise also increases the body’s requirements for other essential nutrients, including glutamine, vitamin B1, vitamin B2, chromium and zinc. Exercise can deplete magnesium through alterations in blood magnesium levels as well as increasing mineral (zinc and magnesium) excretion through sweat and urine. 

- Glutamine is stored primarily in skeletal muscles and levels can be depleted by approximately 20% after periods of physical activity. Supplemental L-glutamine assists muscle cell repair after exercise. 

- Potassium is an essential mineral for maintaining normal muscle contraction and taurine is the most abundant free amino acid in muscles. 

## Antioxidant 

- Muscle Resuscitation contains the antioxidant nutrients selenium, zinc and vitamin C to help protect against oxidative stress and free radical damage. Selenium is an important component of glutathione peroxidases 1-4, antioxidant enzymes that reduce potentially damaging reactive oxygen species (ROS). Zinc is an essential part of the antioxidant enzyme copper/zinc superoxide dismutase (Cu/Zn SOD). Strenuous exercise or physical activity increases oxidative stress and, therefore, requirements for antioxidants. 

## Immunity 

- Muscle Resuscitation contains key nutrients to support immune health. Vitamin C, zinc, selenium and L-Glutamine help maintain immune system health. L-Glutamine supports immune and digestive health after periods of physical stress, such as exercise. 

## Stress 

- Muscle Resuscitation supports a healthy stress response in the body. Requirements for magnesium and B vitamins are increased during periods of stress, including strenuous physical activity.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Medicinal mushrooms are edible fungi with a long history of medicinal use across many cultures worldwide. Traditionally associated with health-supporting properties, mushrooms have been used for centuries for an array of ailments and to support longevity, particularly in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and Eastern European traditions. 

- Mushroom extracts are derived from the fruiting body or mycelium. Mycelium is the main body and feeding membrane of a mushroom and grows underground or within the host plant, acting as a root system. A mushroom fruiting body is the flesh part of the mushroom which grows above ground or on the surface of its host and contains spores. Whole plant mushroom extracts contain a combination of both the fruiting body and mycelium. 

- Mushrooms contain biologically active polysaccharides, including beta-glucans, proteoglycans and related compounds in their fruiting bodies. Polysaccharides form the major class of immunologically active molecules in mushrooms and other fungi. 

- Mushroom fruiting bodies are considered “full spectrum” as they provide a wide array of nutritional components and compounds. Mycelium and fruiting bodies share similar cell wall structures and contain the polysaccharide complexes. However, concentrations vary, and beta-glucans are considered to be present in higher concentrations in the fruiting body compared to the mycelium. 

- Mushroom 5 Complex contains a combination of five medicinal mushrooms including Shiitake, Reishi, Cordyceps, Snow fungus and Turkey tail, derived from fruiting bodies and whole plant extracts. 

## Immune health 

- Mushroom 5 Complex maintains healthy immune system function and supports immune system health. 

- The effect on the immune system can be attributed to the bioactive polysaccharides, such as beta-glucans, which can affect innate and adaptive immune responses.

interferon and various cytokines. It also increases the activity of natural killer cells and macrophages.

Regular consumption resulted in improved immunity demonstrated by an increased expression of immune cell markers. Increased serum IgA implied improved gut immunity and a reduction in C reactive protein (CRP) suggested lowered inflammation[1] . 

- Reishi contains polysaccharides, such as β-D-glucans, heteropolysaccharides and glycoproteins, which can affect immune and immune-related cells and show immunomodulatory effects. 

- Cordyceps contains a high amount of polysaccharides, ranging from 3-8% of total weight, and these are responsible for its pharmacological properties[2] . 

- Cordyceps polysaccharides have antioxidant and immunomodulatory activity. In vitro studies show Cordyceps enhances the production of proinflammatory cytokines, TNF-α, and IL-6, as well as the anti-inflammatory cytokine, IL-10, in human peripheral blood[3] . 

- Turkey tail contains precursors to the proteoglycans polysaccharide peptide (PSP) and polysaccharide-K (Krestin, PSK), the constituents responsible for the immunological effects known to enhance innate and adaptive immune responses[4] .

3 Antioxidant 3 Skin health 3 Cardiovascular health 3 Immune support 

3 Vegan-friendly 3 High strength 3 Natural vitamin E 

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Vitamin E is a general term for a group of compounds with vitamin E activity. Alpha-tocopherol is the most abundant and biologically active form of vitamin E. 

- D-alpha-tocopherol is the naturally occurring isomer of vitamin E (known as ‘natural vitamin E’) and has the highest bioavailability of the forms of vitamin E. 

- Vitamin E, which is absorbed in the small intestine and stored in the liver, is relatively non-toxic. It is not stored as readily as the other fatsoluble vitamins with up to 60-70% of a daily dose excreted. 

- Requirements for vitamin E are increased by exposure to pollution, pesticides, additives and radiation. As vitamin E is a fat-soluble vitamin, fat malabsorption (e.g. Crohn’s disease, chronic pancreatitis, liver disease) can reduce its absorption. 

- Natural Vitamin E 500IU helps prevent vitamin E deficiency. 

## Antioxidant 

- Vitamin E is the most important lipid-soluble antioxidant. It protects polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) within the phospholipid layer of each cell membrane from free-radical damage and is, therefore, important for the maintenance of membrane integrity of all cells in the body. 

- Vitamin E works together with vitamin C and selenium (as glutathione peroxidases) to limit free radical damage and is recycled by vitamin C and glutathione peroxidase so it can be reused by tissues. Consequently, deficiencies in vitamin C or selenium can increase the need for vitamin E. 

- Vitamin E is required to protect dietary PUFAs from oxidation. Thus, the need for vitamin E increases with increased intake of PUFAs. A typical Western diet is high in PUFAs. 

## Cardiovascular health 

- Vitamin E helps maintain cardiovascular health. As an antioxidant, it inhibits platelet aggregation and adhesion, is anti-inflammatory, improves endothelial function and decreases lipid peroxidation. 

- Vitamin E assists blood circulation by decreasing platelet aggregation and adhesion. 

- Epidemiological studies show that higher intakes of vitamin E are associated with lower cardiovascular risk[1] . 

## Skin health 

- Vitamin E supports healthy skin, both internally and topically, and supports wound healing. 

The skin is exposed to numerous chemical and physical agents, such as ultraviolet light, that can cause oxidative stress and result in adverse effects such as erythema, oedema, skin thickening, wrinkling and photo-ageing[2] . Vitamin E is the major naturally-occurring lipidsoluble antioxidant that protects the skin from the adverse effects of oxidative stress, including photo-ageing. 

- Vitamin E helps relieve symptoms of mild eczema and dermatitis, especially itchy skin. A 2015 randomised, double-blind, placebocontrolled study found that 400IU vitamin E given to 70 patients with mild to moderate eczema significantly improved symptoms including itching, sleep disturbance and extent of lesions. Overall SCORAD index improved significantly (p<0.05) in those taking vitamin E[3] . 

- Another study using 400IU of vitamin E in 96 subjects with eczema found that eczematous lesions healed more quickly in patients receiving vitamin E as a result of decreased pruritus[4] . 

## Immune 

- Vitamin E helps maintain healthy immune function. It protects white blood cells from oxidative damage, enhances antibody production by white blood cells and enhances their ability to phagocytise bacteria. 

## PMS 

- Vitamin E can help reduce the symptoms of premenstrual syndrome. An early randomised, double-blind study found that 400IU d-alphatocopherol daily for 3 cycles significantly improved certain affective and physical symptoms of PMS[5] . 

- Specifically, vitamin E relieves menstruation pain. Two randomised, placebo-controlled studies using either 200IU vitamin E twice daily or 500IU daily, starting 2 days before menstruation and continuing for the first 3 days of bleeding, found that vitamin E reduced menstrual pain severity and duration. Beneficial effects were seen after 2 months and reached maximal effect after 4 months[6,7] . 

## Sperm health 

   - Vitamin E helps support sperm health and motility. 

   - Antioxidants are important for sperm health as the membranes of germ cells and spermatozoa are very sensitive to oxidation and high levels of oxidation can reduce sperm motility. Some research in humans has shown that vitamin E decreases the levels of malondialdehyde, an organic compound used as a marker of oxidative stress, and improves sperm motility[8] . 

- As an antioxidant, it helps protect the skin from oxidative damage.

## **DIRECTIONS FOR USE** 

Adults - Take 1 tablet once daily, with food, or as directed by your health professional. Tablet should be taken whole. 

## **60 modified release tablets** 

Do not break, crush or chew tablet before swallowing. Do not take more than 1 tablet per day. 

## **FEATURES & BENEFITS** 

3 Nicotinic acid (vitamin B3) 3 8-hour release 

3 Skin health 

3 Low risk of flushing 

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Niacin is a water-soluble vitamin required for the function of over 200 enzymes throughout the body. It is well-absorbed after oral administration and metabolised in the liver to nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADP). NAD and NADP are essential for energy metabolism, oxidation-reduction reactions and ADP-ribose transfer reactions involved in DNA repair and calcium mobilisation. 

- Niacin can be formed in the body from the amino acid tryptophan. It takes 60mg of tryptophan to make 1mg niacin. Poor protein intake, especially inadequate tryptophan, increases the risk of deficiency. 

- Niacin helps convert food into energy and assists in the metabolism of carbohydrates and dietary fats. It is a component of the glucose tolerance factor (GTF) that supports sugar metabolism. 

- Niacin supports skin health. It can dilate small blood vessels, improving 

- blood flow of nutrients and oxygen to the skin, heart and brain. 

- Niacin is often used in high doses to maintain cardiovascular health and a healthy lipid profile. Niacin can reduce fibrinogen concentrations in plasma and may stimulate fibrinolysis. It inhibits the mobilisation of free fatty acids from peripheral tissues and reduces hepatic synthesis of triglycerides and the secretion of low density lipoproteins and very low-density lipoproteins[1] . 

## Niacin vs nicotinamide 

- Two main forms of vitamin B3 are found in foods: nicotinic acid (niacin) and nicotinamide (niacinamide). Both can be converted into active forms of vitamin B3 in the body. 

- Both niacin and nicotinamide can perform all the essential biochemical functions of vitamin B3 in the body and prevent a deficiency, however, niacin has additional actions, such as cardiovascular effects and blood vessel dilation. 

- Nicotinamide does not cause the flush that is a common side effect of niacin supplementation. 

## Niacin flush 

- Niacin supplementation is commonly associated with flushing of the skin, known as the ‘niacin flush’, caused by the dilation of the capillaries. Although this effect is transient and harmless, it can be uncomfortable and concerning if people do not expect it. 

- The body usually adapts to niacin intake overtime and side-effects lessen in severity. Skin flushing is worse when niacin is taken on an empty stomach. 

- Flushing is usually caused by higher doses and immediate release niacin. Niacin 100mg Extended Release is unlikely to cause flushing. 

## Extended release 

- Niacin 100mg Extended Release is an extended-release product that releases niacin into the body over an 8-hour period. Extended-release forms are less likely to cause flushing than immediate-release forms. 

- It is important to differentiate extended-release from sustained-release forms. Sustained-release niacin preparations release niacin into the body over a 24-hour period and are associated with a higher risk of hepatotoxicity and gastrointestinal intolerance than unmodified niacin preparations. This may be because the liver is not given a break. 

- Extended-release niacin allows the vitamin to be absorbed over 8 hours, which reduces the incidence of flushing seen with immediaterelease forms, and hepatotoxicity, seen with sustained-release forms, as it still allows the liver to have a break. Increased risk of hepatotoxicity is not seen with extended-release niacin[2] . 

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Caution with anticoagulant or antiplatelet medication - niacin may increase the risk of bleeding in some patients. 

- Caution with bile acid sequestrants (e.g. cholestyramine) – drugs bind to niacin and decrease absorption. Separate dose by 4-6 hours. 

- Caution with statin medication. Co-administration of statins and niacin may increase the risk of developing myotoxicity, however, usually in much higher doses. Co-administration is often recommended for dyslipidaemia; it is recommended to use the lowest possible dose of both agents and monitor patient for signs of myotoxicity during concurrent use. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- Not recommended during pregnancy or lactation due to insufficient safety data on high doses of niacin. 

- Avoid consuming with alcohol. Alcohol can exacerbate the flushing associated with niacin. 

- Contraindicated in people with gout. Niacin can reduce urinary excretion of uric acid, potentially resulting in hyperuricemia. 

- Caution in people with blood sugar imbalance. High doses of niacin can impair glucose tolerance. However, doses under 1.5g daily have minimal effects on blood glucose. 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- Extended-release niacin is less likely to cause a niacin flush, however, it is still possible in sensitive individuals and may occur several hours after supplementation. Take on a full stomach to reduce risk of flushing. 

- Other unwanted effects (usually seen in immediate release forms and in high doses) include itching, mucous membrane irritation and diarrhoea.

- Hawthorn 4500 • Ubiquinol 100mg

## **Olive Leaf** 

## Immune support 

- Olive Leaf supports healthy immune system function. 

- Olive leaf has been found to have antimicrobial properties against viruses, bacteria and yeasts in animal and human studies. It inhibits assembly of viruses at the cell membrane, interfering with critical amino acid production, and stops viral shedding. Olive leaf can also inhibit bacteria, either by inactivating cellular enzymes critical for bacterial replication or via attack on the cell membrane[3] . 

- Olive leaf is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine as a febrifuge to relieve mild fevers. 

## Antioxidant 

- Olive leaf is recognised as a potent antioxidant that helps reduce free radicals formed in the body. It has been shown to have the highest radical-scavenging activity of 55 herbs studied – more than twice that of Green tea and St Mary’s thistle[4] . 

- Numerous Olive phenolics have strong free radical scavenging capacity, while also exerting synergistic behaviour when combined, as occurs naturally in the fruit and leaf. The phenolic antioxidants in Olive leaf, hydroxytyrosol, oleuropein and luteolin, exert antioxidant effects almost 2.5-fold those of vitamin C and E and are comparable to that of lycopene[5] . 

## Cardiovascular support 

- Olive leaf contains polyphenols, particularly oleuropein, which are associated with cardioprotective activity. The herb has demonstrated vasodilatory, anti-platelet aggregation, anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties that help support healthy cardiovascular system function. 

- In particular, oleuropein supports cardiovascular health by protecting membranes from lipid oxidation, affecting coronary blood vessel dilation, exerting antiarrhythmic action and improving lipid metabolism[6] . 

- A double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled cross-over acute intervention trial investigated the influence of Olive leaf extract containing 51.12mg oleuropein on vascular function and inflammation. A single dose of Olive leaf resulted in a significant reduction in IL-8 and reduced arterial stiffness compared to controls[7] . 

## Mild fluid retention 

- Olive leaf is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine for the relief of mild fluid retention and to assist the body in getting rid of excess water and harmful toxins. 

- Olive leaf’s diuretic action is attributed to the active oleuropein. 

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Caution with hypoglycaemic, antihypertensive and diuretic medications - Olive leaf may have additive effects. Monitor blood sugar or blood pressure. 

- Caution with chemotherapy drugs - Olive leaf’s antioxidant effect may interfere with therapy. Use only under professional supervision. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- Caution in kidney disorders - Olive leaf can cause a detoxification reaction adding further stress to the kidneys.

- None noted at the recommended dose.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- The Olive tree is native to the Mediterranean region and has a long history of medicinal use to promote health. The leaves were widely used as a remedy for the relief of fevers in Greece, Spain, Italy, France, Turkey, Palestine, Morocco and Tunisia. 

- Olive leaf is made up of secoiridoids (oleuropein and its derivatives), hydroxytyrosol, polyphenols, triterpenes, including oleanolic acid, and flavonoids, which support the tree’s resistance to damage from pathogens and insects. The primary constituent, oleuropein, is believed to be responsible for many of the therapeutic properties of the leaf. 

- Herbs of Gold Olive Leaf 7500 is high-strength, with each tablet containing the equivalent of 7.5g Olive leaf, standardised to 180mg of oleuropein. 

## Antioxidant 

- Olive Leaf 7500 acts as an antioxidant to reduce free radicals formed in the body. 

- Free radicals are unstable molecules that are naturally formed during exercise and when the body converts food into energy. The body is also exposed to free radicals from a variety of environmental sources, such as cigarette smoke, air pollution and sunlight. Free radicals can cause “oxidative stress,” a process that can trigger cell damage. 

- Antioxidants are substances that help to prevent or delay cell damage. 

- Numerous phenolics from Olive leaf have been shown to have strong antioxidant activity. According to in vitro tests, the flavonoids, rutin, catechin and luteolin exert antioxidant effects almost 2.5 times more potent than vitamin C and E, and at levels comparable to that of lycopene[1] . 

- Olive leaf has been shown to have the highest free radicalscavenging activity of 55 herbs when studied – more than twice of that of Green tea and St Mary’s thistle[2] . 

## Immune support 

- Olive Leaf 7500 supports healthy immune system function. 

- Olive leaf has been found to have antimicrobial properties against viruses, bacteria and yeasts in animal and human studies. Olive leaf inhibits assembly of viruses at the cell membrane, interfering with critical amino acid production, and stops viral shedding. Olive leaf can also inhibit bacteria, either by inactivating cellular enzymes critical for bacterial replication or via attack on the cell membrane[3] . 

## Cardiovascular support 

- Olive Leaf 7500 supports cardiovascular system function. 

- Olive leaf contains polyphenols, particularly oleuropein, which are associated with cardioprotective activity. The herb has demonstrated vasodilatory, anti-platelet aggregation, anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties that help support a healthy cardiovascular system. 

- In particular, oleuropein supports cardiovascular health by protecting membranes from lipid oxidation, affecting coronary blood vessel dilation, exerting antiarrhythmic action and improving lipid metabolism[3] . 

- A double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled cross-over acute intervention trial investigated the influence of Olive leaf extract containing 51.12mg oleuropein on vascular function and inflammation. A single dose of Olive leaf resulted in a significant reduction in IL-8 and reduced arterial stiffness compared to controls. 

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Caution with hypoglycaemic, antihypertensive and diuretic medications - Olive leaf may have additive effects. Monitor blood sugar or blood pressure. 

- Caution with chemotherapy drugs - Olive leaf’s antioxidant effect may interfere with therapy. Use only under professional supervision. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- Caution in kidney disorders - Olive leaf can cause a detoxification reaction adding further stress to the kidneys. 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- None noted at the recommended dose.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Iron is an essential mineral found in the body that plays a pivotal role in oxygen transportation and storage, immune health, as well as a multitude of enzyme reactions. Iron levels are tightly controlled within the body and levels are regulated by absorption rather than excretion. Many factors can hinder the amount of iron absorbed within the gastrointestinal tract. 

- There are two forms of dietary iron: haem and non-haem. In the diet, haem iron is derived from animal sources and is readily absorbed by the body. Non-haem iron is mainly derived from plant sources and is poorly absorbed when compared to haem iron. Non-haem iron is easily inhibited by dietary factors such as tea and coffee (polyphenols), wholegrains (phytic acid), chocolate, spinach and berries (oxalic acid), calcium, zinc and manganese, leading to poor solubility and absorption. 

- Organic Iron MAX contains 250mg of vitamin C to assist iron absorption. Vitamin C helps to solubilise non-haem iron, so it helps to increase iron absorption. Vitamin B2 also assists the body in absorbing iron. 

- Organic Iron MAX also contains cofactors vitamins B1, B2, B6, B12 and folate, important to assist iron metabolism and maintain healthy blood. 

- Organic Iron MAX contains the active forms of folate, methylfolate, and vitamin B12, methylcobalamin, that are ready for use in the body, without requiring metabolic conversion. 

- Spirulina, a blue-green alkaline algae, and spinach are rich sources of iron. 

## Ferrochel[TM] 

- Albion’s Ferrochel[TM] (ferrous bisglycinate amino acid chelate) is an organic form of non-haem iron with greater bioavailability that is well-tolerated and gentle on the digestive system. Ferrochel[TM] has been shown to have up to 90% bioavailability in clinical studies[1] . 

- Ferrochel[TM] consists of one molecule of ferrous iron bound to two molecules of glycine, creating small organic chelated iron molecules (similar to a dipeptide or small protein) that can easily pass through the intestinal wall. This chelation means that the iron remains intact 

and electrically neutral, so doesn’t break down in the stomach acid and is therefore delivered intact to the small intestine where it is easily absorbed. 

   - The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) states that ferrous bisglycinate has been used in numerous field trials and that in all cases, substantial improvements in iron status indicators (serum levels of haemoglobin and ferritin, total iron binding capacity and iron stores) have been reported in the groups supplemented with ferrous bisglycinate compared to the controls. Moreover, there was no evidence of iron overloading in non-iron deficient individuals and ferrous bisglycinate was well tolerated by adult males, pregnant females, non-pregnant females with normal iron status, as well as in iron deficient young children[2] . 

   - Studies have shown iron from Ferrochel[TM] to be better absorbed and better tolerated than other forms of iron. 

   - Iron salts, such as ferrous sulfate, become electrically charged when stomach acid breaks down the iron salt molecule, creating oxidation of vitamin E and blocking calcium uptake. This unbound iron is easily inhibited by other dietary factors and further impacts the mucous membranes of the gastrointestinal tract leading to gastric upset and digestive discomfort. 

   - One study testing the absorption of iron added to fortify foods found that iron absorption from Ferrochel™ was about twice the absorption as from ferrous sulfate (p<0.05)[3] . 

   - A double-blind study compared the absorption of Ferrochel™ with polymaltose iron in 20 children aged 1-13 years. Both treatments resulted in significant increases in haemoglobin levels, Mean Corpuscular Volume (MCV) and Red Cell Distribution Width (RDW) and a reduction of transferrin levels. However, only iron bisglycinate significantly increased ferritin (p<0.05). Ferritin is considered the most efficient indicator of a response to iron treatment. The study concluded that iron bisglycinate was more effective in replenishing iron stores, favouring a reduction in required supplementation time[4] .

## **Organic Iron MAX** 

## Maintain iron levels 

- Organic Iron MAX maintains iron levels in the body. 

- The recommended dietary intake of iron is 8mg per day for men of all ages and women aged over 50 years, and 18mg per day for women aged 18-50. The large increase reflects the high variability in needs related to female menstrual losses. 

- To achieve iron balance, adult men need to absorb about 1mg per day and adult menstruating women about 1.5mg per day, although this is highly variable. Towards the end of pregnancy, the absorption of 4-5mg per day is necessary. Requirements are higher during periods of rapid growth in early childhood and adolescence. 

## Blood health 

- Organic Iron MAX supports healthy blood. 

- Iron and vitamins B2, B6, B12 and folate assist the body to produce haemoglobin, the primary protein involved in oxygen transport in the body. 

- Most of the iron in the body is found in the haemoglobin of red blood cells and in the myoglobin of muscle cells where it is required for oxygen and carbon dioxide transport. Haemoglobin represents about two-thirds of the body’s iron. Haemoglobin is essential for transferring oxygen in the blood from the lungs to the tissues. Myoglobin, in muscle cells, accepts, stores, transports and releases oxygen. 

## Energy production 

- Organic Iron MAX supports energy production. 

- Iron is an integral part of several proteins in the body, including adenosine triphosphate (ATP). Iron serves as an activator for the biochemical process in which ATP is made, providing the primary energy carrier to all cells. 

- Caution with antacids - coadministration may reduce iron absorption and vitamin C may increase the amount of aluminium absorbed from these medications. Separate doses by at least 2 hours. 

- Caution with methotrexate – folate may affect drug efficacy. Use only under the supervision of a health professional. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- Iron, calcium and zinc all compete for absorption. Separate dose. 

- Contraindicated in iron overload conditions, such as haemochromatosis, haemosiderosis or iron loading anaemias such as thalassaemia and sideroblastic anaemia. 

- Tannins bind to iron and reduce absorption. Avoid taking iron with foods rich in tannins including tea, Bilberry and Raspberry leaf. 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- Iron supplements are known to cause gastrointestinal disturbances such as nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, heartburn and upper gastric discomfort and may cause stools to blacken. However, Ferrochel[TM] is gentle on digestion so side-effects are not expected.

## Nervous system health

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Pain Relief PEA has been formulated with high-strength PEA for acute or long-term use to help manage a variety of pain states, including mild joint pain, nerve pain and symptoms of mild arthritis. 

- Palmitoylethanolamide (PEA) is an endogenous fatty acid amide with neuroprotective, anti-inflammatory and analgesic actions. PEA is produced naturally in the body in response to injury and stress. 

- PEA is found in many plant and animal food sources, as well as in the cells and tissues of mammals. Food sources of PEA include peas, tomato, alfalfa, corn, soybean and peanut. It was first isolated from purified lipid fractions of soybeans, egg yolk and peanut meal[1] .

- strategy for the management of chronic pain in different conditions[2] . 

- The therapeutic dose of PEA used in clinical trials for pain relief is between 300mg and 1200mg daily. ## Levagen[®] + 

- PEA is a lipophilic (fat-loving) substance and has traditionally shown poor absorption in animal models. Levagen[®] + utilises LipiSperse[®] technology to increase bioavailability in the body. LipiSperse[®] enables PEA to easily disperse in the watery gastrointestinal tract and prevents the PEA crystals from agglomerating, increasing the surface area for superior absorption. 

- Levagen[®] + solubility and particle size are checked by Dynamic Light Scattering analysis and Laser Light Obscuration to enable optimal dispersion and efficacy. 

- A parallel, double-blind study compared the absorption of 300mg of Levagen[®] + and a standard PEA in 28 healthy adults. Levagen[®] + significantly increased plasma PEA concentration above baseline concentrations and by 1.75 times that of standard PEA (p<0.05) (see figure 1)[3] . 

## **Figure 1: PEA plasma concentrations** 

- Levagen[®] + has an acute onset of action, with pharmacokinetic studies showing rapid absorbtion, with peak plasma concentrations occurring 45 minutes post ingestion[4] . 

## Pain 

- Pain is a complex mechanism that exists to protect the body from danger and harm. 

- There are two main types of pain: acute pain, the normal response to an injury that is usually sudden and short-lived, and chronic pain that continues beyond the time expected for healing. 

- When pain becomes chronic, it can severely impact day-to-day functions and quality of life. Common causes of chronic pain include arthritis, musculoskeletal ailments, nerve pain and surgery. 

- Chronic pain is prevalent in Australia, with one in five Australians aged 45 and over living with persistent, ongoing pain[5] . In 2020, over 3.37 million Australians were living with chronic pain and the total financial cost of chronic pain in Australia was estimated to be $144.1 billion[6] . 

- Conventional pain medications generally work by either downregulating prostaglandins, and therefore the inflammatory response, or by changing the pain messages in the brain.  PEA has multiple mechanisms of action that differ from conventional steroidal and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), giving it the potential  to relieve pain without the common side-effects seen with other medication and the ability to be used in conjunction with other pain medications. 

## Mechanism of action 

- PEA acts via multiple mechanisms, acting directly or indirectly on several molecular targets to produce a therapeutic effect in both the central and peripheral nervous systems. 

- The analgesic activity appears to be achieved via two different mechanisms: direct receptor-mediated and an indirect “entourage effect”. 

- PEA directly targets nuclear peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPAR-α), which is a master-switch for a number of genes activating the inflammatory cascade, and cannabinoid-like G-protein-coupled receptors (GPR55). 

- PEA works indirectly on a number of molecular targets by potentiating the activity of other endogenous compounds or by inhibiting the metabolic degradation of these molecules, known as the “entourage effect”. It acts indirectly on cannabinoid (CB) receptors, particularly CB2 receptor, and indirectly activates transient receptor potential vanilloid type 1 (TRPV1) channels[7] . - Initially, it was thought that PEA was a CB2 receptor agonist, but subsequent research has shown that PEA only has very weak affinity for this receptor. Instead, it is believed that PEA produces indirect receptor-mediated effects by inhibiting the expression of fatty acid amide hydrolase (FAAH), the enzyme that degrades endogenous cannabinoid receptor ligand anandamide (AEA) and 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG), therefore increasing levels of these endocannabinoids which then potentiate the activity of these receptors[8] . 

- The anti-inflammatory effects of PEA are believed to be primarily related to its ability to modulate mast cell activation and degranulation. 

- An observational study investigated the efficacy of high dose PEA in reducing pain severity in patients with pain lasting greater than 6 months associated with different pathological conditions. 600mg of PEA was administered twice daily for 3 weeks followed by a single daily dose for 4 weeks in addition to standard analgesic therapies or as a stand-alone therapy. PEA significantly decreased mean pain intensity in all patients, independent of the cause of pain. Pain scores decreased from 6.4 at baseline to 2.5 at the end of treatment (p=0.0001)(see figure 2). Out of 564 patients who completed the study, 476 were undergoing standard therapies for chronic pain including opioids, anticonvulsants and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs[13] .

## Pain relief 

- PEA is well researched for its analgesic effects in a number of painrelated conditions. 

- A 2017 systematic review and meta-analysis concluded that PEA is well-tolerated and useful for the treatment of pain. This review covered 10 studies including data from 786 patients receiving PEA and 512 controls. PEA was associated with a significantly greater pain reduction compared to control conditions (p<0.001). Dosages ranged from 300mg to 1200mg daily, however, no significant association was found between the dose of PEA and measured efficacy. Treatment duration ranged from 10 days to 180 days and PEA was well tolerated with fewer dropouts than the control groups[11] . 

- Another systematic review and meta-analysis including 12 studies found that PEA progressively reduced pain intensity significantly more than controls and that pain relief was independent of patient age or gender, and not related to the type of chronic pain. This review confirmed the safety of PEA with no difference in haematology, blood chemistry or urine analyses before or after treatment and no adverse effects reported[12] . 

## Osteoarthritis 

- An Australian study with a comparative, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled design evaluated the safety and efficacy of two doses of Levagen[®] PEA in 111 patients aged between 38 and 76 years with mild to moderate osteoarthritis. The trial ran over 8 weeks and assessed 300mg or 600mg per day given in 2 divided doses (equivalent to 2 or 4 capsules of Pain Relief PEA daily). After 8 weeks, total WOMAC* scores (covering pain, stiffness and physical function) reduced significantly compared to placebo, from 41.2 to 23.9 in the 300mg group (p=0.037) and from 43.2 to 20 in the 600mg group 

- (p=0.001) (see figure 3)[14] .

- In this study, PEA resulted in a gradual reduction in pain which was significant compared to placebo at week 8. WOMAC stiffness scores also reduced significantly compared to placebo. Participants also recorded a reduction in the use of rescue medication with the use of PEA compared to placebo. 

- This study demonstrated that PEA was well tolerated at both dosages with no serious adverse effects reported and no changes recorded in haematological and biochemical parameters.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- ParaStrike contains high-strength European wormwood (Wormwood), Black walnut and Barberry, combined with essential oils to help rid the body of intestinal worms. 

- ParaStrike contains Thyme and Oregano essential oils. These oils are microencapsulated and spray dried onto the tablet to help protect the naturally occurring active compounds which are highly susceptible to changes caused by external factors such as light, oxygen and heat. 

- ParaStrike is formulated for both children and adults with different dosing requirements based on age. The lifecycle of an adult worm means it may live for up to 6 weeks. As such, the treatment regime needs to cover a 6-week period to ensure adult worms and newly hatched eggs are destroyed and eliminated, reducing the risk of reinfestation. While a child is more likely than an adult to become infested, the risk of passing infestation from a child to an adult is high, so treatment for the whole family is commonly recommended. 

## Worms 

- A parasite is any organism that lives in or on another organism and steals nutrition from the host at the host’s expense. Parasites are generally grouped into three categories: helminths (parasitic worms and flukes), protozoa (single celled organisms such are giardia, toxoplasma, plasmodium and cryptosporidium) and arthropods (associated with vector diseases carried by mosquitos, fleas, ticks, mites and lice). 

- Parasitic infections occur due to many factors: urbanisation (crowding together); intensive farming systems; greater movement and relocation of animals; land and marine development; inadequate effluent disposal; parasitic drug resistance and the spread of vector insecticide resistance. 

- Parasites typically infect the digestive system, although they can invade other tissues and organs and can cause a broad range of symptoms, the most significant of which are gut and digestive dysfunction. 

- Pinworms are the most common type of worm infection found in Australia. Children, particularly pre-school and school-aged children, 

are more susceptible to pinworm infections, although adults can easily become infected. Usually, if one person in the household has a worm infection, it is more than likely that other members of the family will also become infected. A female pinworm can lay up to 15 000 eggs a day[1] . 

- Worms are spread directly by children (or adults) who scratch their bottoms and then carry the worm eggs back to their mouth with their hands or indirectly, in food, dust or other articles of bedding or clothing. The eggs can survive for up to two weeks outside the body. Around 4 weeks after the eggs are swallowed, they hatch in the small intestine and the female travels down the digestive tract and exits the body via the anus to lay a new batch of eggs on the surrounding skin, often at night.

   - The key constituents of Black walnut thought to be responsible for its therapeutic action include naphthoquinones (juglone & plumbagin) and tannins[2] . 

   - Barberry contains the alkaloid berberine, a signature component of Barberry with antimicrobial (bacteria and fungi) and antiparasitic properties giving berberine a broad-spectrum action. The root bark contains the highest number of alkaloids when compared to the stem bark. Barberry also has a mild laxative effect so helps eliminate waste and toxins, an important element to cleansing the body of parasites.

## Digestive health 

- ParaStrike contains herbs traditionally used to support digestive system function. Some of the more common symptoms of worm infections include digestive disturbances, so these herbs can help offset some digestive symptoms related to parasitic die off. 

- Black walnut is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine for its laxative action and to relieve constipation. It also has an astringent action, due to a high tannin content. 

- Barberry is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine to relieve symptoms of indigestion and dyspepsia, to relieve diarrhoea and to support healthy liver function. Barberry bark is intensely bitter, traditionally used for its relaxing effect on the digestive system. 

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Contraindicated with anticoagulant and antiplatelet medications such as warfarin – Wormwood may increase bleeding risk and Thyme essential oil may interact by inducing phase I and phase II liver enzymes. 

- Contraindicated with fluoroquinolone and tetracycline antibiotics, and anti-infective medications – Barberry may reduce their effectiveness. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- Contraindicated in pregnancy and lactation – the thujone in Wormwood can have a contraction effect on the uterus, while berberine can be harmful to the developing brain of the unborn child. 

- • Contraindicated in gastric or duodenal ulcers – Wormwood can increase gastric fluid potentially making these conditions worse. 

- Caution in high blood pressure - Thyme essential oil may theoretically increase blood pressure. Monitor. 

- Caution in acute/severe hepatocellular disease, liver cancer, intestinal spasm or ileus - Wormwood and Barberry can impact liver function when liver health is poor. 

- Wormwood may cause allergic reactions in people sensitive to the Asteraceae family. 

- This product is not suitable for long-term use. Use only at the dose and directions indicated on the bottle. 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- Thyme oil may cause mild gastrointestinal irritation, such as heartburn, diarrhoea, nausea and vomiting. 

- Mild gastrointestinal symptoms, headaches or fatigue may occur as a result of parasitic die-off. These symptoms are a common detox reaction to the toxins released when the parasites start to die and, when mild, should resolve within a few days.
