## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Vitamin B12 or cobalamin is an essential water-soluble vitamin required for DNA synthesis, cell reproduction and fatty acid and amino acid metabolism. The primary source of vitamin B12 is from animal products such as meat, fish, eggs, dairy and organ meats. 

## Energy production 

   - Sublingual B12 1000 supports energy production and aids the metabolism of carbohydrates, protein and fats. Vitamin B12 is involved in the synthesis of the citric acid cycle intermediate, succinyl-CoA. Succinyl-CoA plays an important role in the production of energy from lipids and proteins. 

- Cyanocobalamin is the form of vitamin B12 commonly used in nutritional supplements and is readily converted to 5-deoxyadenosylcobalamin and methylcobalamin, the active forms of vitamin B12 in the body. 

## Nerve & brain health 

   - Sublingual B12 1000 supports nervous system function and nerve health. Adequate intake of vitamin B12 is essential for normal neurological function. It plays a vital role in the synthesis and maintenance of myelin, the protective sheath surrounding nerves. 

- Oral supplementation of cyanocobalamin is dependent on stomach acid and intrinsic factor (IF) for absorption into the body. Sublingual administration is beneficial for those who have low stomach acid and is an alternative to oral (swallowed) tablets and injections. 

   - Sublingual B12 1000 supports brain health and cognitive function. The European Food Safety Authority concluded that a causeand-effect relationship has been established between the dietary intake of vitamin B12 and contribution to normal neurological and psychological functions[2] . 

- Gastric acid secretions and IF diminish as part of the ageing process, therefore many elderly people are at risk of a vitamin B12 deficiency. The long-term use of certain medications, such as inhibitors of stomach acid secretion, can adversely affect vitamin B12 absorption. 

- Vegans and strict vegetarians are also at risk of vitamin B12 deficiency as they do not consume any animal products, the main dietary source of vitamin B12. 

## Cardiovascular system 

- Sublingual B12 1000 maintains cardiovascular system health. Vitamin B12 participates in the synthesis and regeneration of methionine from homocysteine, helping to maintain healthy homocysteine levels. Methionine donates ‘methyl groups’ required for the methylation reactions to occur. Homocysteine is an amino acid-like compound that has been linked to an increased risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes when levels are elevated. 

## Signs & symptoms of B12 deficiency 

- Fatigue, weakness and shortness of breath 

- Poor concentration, memory and muscular coordination 

- Irritability 

- Numbness and tingling in hands and feet 

   - Sublingual B12 1000 supports red blood cell health. Vitamin B12, along with B6 and folic acid, is an important co-factor required to activate enzymes that are essential for the formation of the haem components that form haemoglobin, a protein abundant in red blood cells and responsible for transporting oxygen around the body[3] . 

- Poor immunity 

- Inflammation of mucous membranes in the mouth or sore tongue 

## Sublingual vs intravenous B12 

- Sublingual administration of vitamin B12 overcomes the challenges of intramuscular (IM) injections and can be considered as a first line option. Sublingual tablets are a non-invasive, pain-free and costeffective form of B12 supplementation. IM injections can be painful and costly and require administration by a health professional.

- A large retrospective study involving 4281 participants compared the efficacy of sublingual versus standard IM administration of vitamin B12 in restoring B12 levels. 830 patients (19.3%) were given 1000 micrograms B12 IM injections and 3451 patients (80.7%) were given 1000 micrograms sublingual tablets, both containing cyanocobalamin. The mean standard deviation difference between serum B12 levels before and after supplementation was statistically significantly higher in the sublingual group vs IM injection group (p<0.001). The sublingual tablet significantly increased the odds ratio of an increase of serum B12 levels compared to the IM group (p<0.001). In a sub-group of people with serum vitamin B12 levels <300mg/L (borderline deficiency), the sublingual preparation was superior to IM injections in raising serum vitamin vitamin B12[1] .

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Bacopa monnieri is a traditional Indian herb that has been used in Ayurvedic medicine for 3000 years and is commonly known as Brahmi or Bacopa. 

- Brahmi is well-known for its beneficial effects on memory and cognition and has a reputation as a brain tonic. The pharmacological activity of Brahmi is attributed to the saponin bacoside and bacopasaponin constituents. 

- Super Brahmi 6000 contains an extract of Brahmi standardised to bacosides, known as BacoMind[®] . BacoMind[®] is a patented extract of Brahmi, clinically researched for memory and cognition enhancing properties. It is a unique full-spectrum phytochemical composition containing 9 different bio-active derivatives. 

- BacoMind[®] is standardised to contain bacoside A, bacopaside I, bacopaside II, bacopasaponin C, jujubogenin isomer of bacopasaponin C, bacosine, luteolin, apigenin and β -sitosterol D glucoside. 

## Traditional use 

- Brahmi is a well-known herb in India with a long history of use in Ayurvedic herbal preparations. The Ayurvedic action for Brahmi in Sanskrit is ‘medhya rasayana’, which translates to ‘herbs which rejuvenate the mind’. 

- Brahmi is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine as a brain tonic to enhance brain health and improve memory and cognitive performance. It is noted in traditional texts to increase memory, learning ability and concentration. 

- Brahmi is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine as nervine to support the nervous system. It has been used to aid recovery from exhaustion, stress and debility with aggravation of ‘vata’. Vata is responsible for movement in the nervous system, muscles, heart and mind. An aggravation or imbalance of vata can manifest as anxiety states. 

## Antioxidant 

- Brahmi is an antioxidant and helps reduce free radicals in the body. It has direct free-radical scavenging activity and increases the activity of endogenous antioxidant systems. 

- The brain is particularly susceptible to oxidative stress as it is metabolically active, possesses high levels of pro-oxidant iron, and is composed of unsaturated lipids prone to lipid peroxidation. The blood–brain barrier prevents many exogenous antioxidants from quenching reactive oxygen species (ROS) in the brain. 

- An experimental animal model study assessed the neuroprotective role of bacoside A against oxidative stress in the brains of rats exposed to cigarette smoke. Concentrations of enzymatic and nonenzymatic antioxidants were measured after exposure. Daily administration of bacoside A significantly increased brain levels of glutathione, vitamin C, vitamin E and vitamin A[1] . 

## Memory & cognition 

- Super Brahmi 6000 improves memory recall, supports cognitive function and enhances cognitive performance. 

- The primary psychoactive constituents of Brahmi are the steroidal saponins, bacoside A and bacoside B. Bacoside A assists in the release of nitric oxide that allows the relaxation of blood vessels to enable smooth blood flow throughout the body. 

- Emerging research demonstrates Brahmi has several mechanisms of action—acetylcholinesterase inhibition, choline acetyltransferase activation, beta-amyloid reduction, increased cerebral blood flow, and monoamine potentiation[2] . 

- A systematic review analysing six randomised, controlled trials concluded that Brahmi acts as a memory enhancer and has the ability to improve the learning and free recall of information. All trials supplemented for 12 weeks, with dosages ranging from 300-450mg of standardised extracts[3] . 

## BacoMind[®] clinical trials 

- BacoMind[®] has been clinically trialled for its memory and cognitive enhancing properties in children, adolescents and elderly persons. 

- A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated the used of BacoMind[®] on 65 elderly individuals with memory impairment without cognitive deficit. Subjects were given 450mg/day BacoMind[®] extract for 12 weeks. Results showed improved cognitive functions, such as attention and verbal memory in the BacoMind[®] group[4] .

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Adequate calcium intake is essential at every stage of life and important for the prevention of osteoporosis later in life. While bone mass accrues in the earlier stages of life, maintaining appropriate calcium levels in the body is important for ongoing bone strength and for reducing the risk of fractures later in life. 

- After 30 years of age, bone mass begins to decline in both men and women. Osteoporosis affects 1 in 3 women and 1 in 5 men globally, regardless of geographical location[1 ] and over 1 million Australians are affected by osteoporosis[2] . 

- Boron is important for the metabolism and utilisation of the bone building nutrients calcium, magnesium and vitamin D. Boron plays an important role in extending the half-life of vitamin D, which is essential for the body’s ability to absorb calcium. 

- Magnesium, vitamin D and vitamin K are required for calcium to be absorbed in the body. Calcium cannot function without sufficient magnesium, while calcium, vitamin D and vitamin K all work together in a delicate balance to achieve proper bone density. 

- Equisetum arvense, Horsetail, is a perennial herb and one of the highest natural sources of silica. Silica accelerates the process of calcification and deposition in bone. It also improves bone matrix quality and facilitates bone mineralisation. 

## Bone health 

- Super Calcium Plus with Boron is a comprehensive calcium supplement containing two forms of calcium, calcium citrate and hydroxyapatite, with boron for bone health. Calcium citrate is an organic form of calcium that is highly soluble, offering greater bioavailability than other forms of calcium, approximately 25% greater bioavailability than calcium carbonate when given with a meal[3] . 

- Super Calcium Plus with Boron also contains vitamin D to support the absorption of dietary calcium as well as other nutritional cofactors. 

- Calcium is an important mineral to help prevent osteoporosis when dietary intake is inadequate, and a diet deficient in calcium can lead to osteoporosis in later life. 

- Calcium is essential for building bone and maintaining bone strength; 99% of the body’s calcium is located in the bone matrix. The remaining 1% is found in the blood and other fluids, and is 

essential for regulation of heartbeat, muscle contraction, release of neurotransmitters, nerve signalling and blood clotting. 

- Calcium is well known for its role in bone health, with bone containing more than 90% of the body’s total calcium content. Calcium plays an important role in bone remodelling, the process where bone is deposited by osteoblasts and resorption is carried out by osteoclasts. In the bone deposition process, bone is created by calcium and phosphate ions binding to create hydroxyapatite crystals. 

- Calcium homeostasis is tightly regulated by parathyroid hormone, phosphorous, vitamin K and vitamin D. Together they determine the level of calcium absorption and excretion or retention via the kidneys and control the bone remodelling process in the developing skeleton. 

- Boron is a trace mineral involved in the development and maintenance of healthy bones, while being involved in the efficient absorption of calcium and the activation of vitamin D. 

- Magnesium is essential for absorption and metabolism of calcium. Magnesium also affects the concentrations of both parathyroid hormone and the active form of vitamin D, which are major regulators of bone homeostasis. Magnesium helps to maintain healthy bones, bone strength and healthy teeth. 

- Manganese is a cofactor for several enzymes involved in bone formation and the building of osteoblasts. 

- The major function of vitamin D is to maintain blood calcium concentrations by enhancing the ability of the small intestine to absorb calcium from the diet. 

## Healthy teeth 

- Super Calcium Plus with Boron contains calcium, vitamin D and magnesium to support healthy teeth. 

- Calcium is stored in both the teeth and the bones where it provides structure and strength while magnesium assists by supporting the absorption of calcium. 

- Vitamin D supports strong teeth as part of its role in regulating calcium and phosphate.

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Caution with tetracycline and quinolone antibiotics – drug bioavailability may be reduced with calcium, magnesium or manganese supplementation. Take antibiotics either 2 hours before or 4-6 hours after calcium.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- The thyroid is a butterfly-shaped gland located just under the voice box (larynx) and is made up of mainly microscopic sacs called thyroid follicles. The function of the thyroid gland is to take iodine and convert it to the thyroid hormones T4 and T3. T4, also known as thyroxine, contains four molecules of iodine, while T3, triiodothyronine, contains three molecules of iodine. 

Figure 1: The link between the adrenal glands and thyroid 

- T4 and T3 are also influenced by thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH). TSH is produced by the pituitary gland in response to signals from the hypothalamus. TSH stimulates the thyroid gland, promoting it to produce more of the thyroid hormones T4 and T3. 

- T4 is the storage hormone and must be converted into the active hormone T3 by the body. T3 is about 5 times more potent than T4 and only T3 can enter the cell receptors. Receptors throughout the body use T3 to regulate oxygen use, basal metabolic rate (BMR), body temperature, cellular metabolism and growth and development. 

## Thyroid function 

- Thyroid Support contains iodine, tyrosine, selenium and zinc, nutrients that are important for thyroid gland health and thyroid hormone production. 

- Tyrosine, iodine, selenium and zinc are required for the synthesis of thyroid hormones and for the conversion of the inactive T4 to the active T3. Tyrosine is a precursor to the thyroid hormones and is also essential for the proper functioning of the adrenal, thyroid and pituitary glands. 

- Iodine, especially, is an essential component of both T3 and T4, comprising 65% of the weight of T4 and 59% of the weight of T3[1] . 

- Ashwagandha assists the production of thyroid hormones by enhancing T4 concentrations[2] . 

## Antioxidant 

- Zinc and vitamin C act as antioxidants, reducing free radical damage to cells and organs in the body and supporting their normal function. Antioxidants protect the thyroid gland from oxidative damage. 

- Zinc is a powerful antioxidant and free radical scavenger. Zinc's role as an antioxidant is achieved through numerous mechanisms including protecting vitamin E from depletion, acting as an important structural component of the antioxidant enzyme superoxide dismutase and reducing free radical production. 

- Vitamin C is antioxidant by scavenging oxygen and nitrogen free radicals, regenerating antioxidant vitamin E and maintaining reduced glutathione. 

## Immune health 

- Thyroid Support contains vitamin C, selenium and zinc to support immune health. 

- While the thyroid gland is a key part of the human endocrine system, it works closely with both the immune system and nervous system to regulate metabolism. A healthy immune system is required for the optimal functioning of the thyroid gland.

- Thyroid Support contains both Ashwagandha and zinc to support the nervous system and a healthy stress response in the body.

## **Thyroid Support** 

- The hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis is a hormone-based system that regulates the body’s reaction to stress. Increased stress can increase the release of cortisol from the adrenal glands, which influences thyroid function at the HPA axis by inhibiting the release of TSH from the pituitary gland as well as inhibiting the conversion of T4 to T3. 

- Ashwagandha is an adaptogen that supports the adrenal glands. Ashwagandha is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine to help the body adapt during times of physical and mental stress and to relieve feelings of weakness, fatigue and general debility. 

- Vitamin C is important in the synthesis of adrenal hormones and is depleted from the adrenal glands during times of stress. 

- In traditional Ayurvedic medicine, Ashwagandha is classified as a “rasayana”, meaning it has rejuvenating qualities. 

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Contraindicated with anti-thyroid medications. 

- Contraindicated with levodopa - competes with tyrosine for uptake, reducing efficacy. 

- Caution with antidepressant drugs (MAOIs, SSRIs and tricyclic antidepressants) - concurrent use with tyrosine may have an additive effect or result in elevated blood pressure. 

- Caution with levothyroxine and CNS stimulants – tyrosine may have additive effects. Separate dose by 2 hours and monitor use. 

- Caution with immunosuppressant drugs - selenium and Ashwagandha may theoretically interfere with immunosuppressant therapy due to their immunostimulant activity. 

- Caution with warfarin and other anticoagulants – selenium may increase blood thinning effect. Monitor. 

- Caution with Eltrombopag – selenium may reduce drug absorption. Separate dose by 4 hours. 

- Caution with drugs containing iodine, e.g. amiodarone (antineoplastic agent) - concurrent use with iodine can increase iodine levels and may affect thyroid function. Monitor thyroid function. 

- Caution with CNS stimulants and sedatives - concurrent use with Ashwagandha may have an additive effect. Monitor. 

- Caution with NSAIDs, cefalexin, penicillamine and tetracycline and quinolone antibiotics – zinc forms complexes with these drugs, reducing absorption of both. Separate dose by 3 hours. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- Contraindicated in pregnancy and breastfeeding – safety data regarding high dose tyrosine is unavailable and Ashwagandha may have abortifacient action. 

- Contraindicated in hyperthyroidism and Graves’ disease – both tyrosine and Ashwagandha may increase T4. 

- Contraindicated in those with melanoma, adrenal tumours or pheochromocytoma. 

- Caution in peptic ulcer disease – Ashwagandha may cause gastrointestinal irritation. 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- Tyrosine may increase blood pressure in susceptible individuals. Monitor blood pressure. 

- Tyrosine supplementation may cause sensitive individuals to experience migraine headache, mild gastric upset, nausea, fatigue, heartburn, arthralgia, nervousness or problems sleeping.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Triple Strength Omega-3 is a highly concentrated fish oil supplement that provides high-strength eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) to support general health and wellbeing. 

- Triple Strength Omega-3 fish oil is derived from small species of fish including anchovies, mackerel and sardines, sourced off the coast of Peru, Chile, Turkey or Morocco.

The fish oil undergoes deacidification and stripping from environmental pollutants, ethyl transesterification, molecular distillation and winterisation to ensure quality and purity. 

- Triple Strength Omega-3 uses sustainably sourced oil, being both FOS and IFOS certified. Friend of the Sea (FOS) is the leading international standard for producers of fish oil, reflecting responsible and sustainable fisheries and aquaculture. The International Fish Oil Standards[TM] (IFOS) is the only third-party testing and certification program for fish oils and sets the world’s highest standards for purity, potency and freshness. 

- Triple Strength Omega-3 is odourless and low reflux, with a natural lemon flavour in the oil and a delicious natural vanilla flavour added to the capsule to mask fishy taste and smell. 

## Omega-3 fatty acids 

- Omega-3 fatty acids are long-chain polyunsaturated essential fatty acids (PUFA) that are necessary for good health and development. They are essential because the body cannot produce them, so adequate amounts must be consumed from the diet. 

- Satisfying omega-3 requirements through diet alone is difficult due to the increasing presence of heavy metals, polychlorinated biphenyls and other environmental toxins present in fish. Therefore, taking a concentrated fish oil supplement that is tested for purity and freshness can be a good way to supplement omega-3s in the diet. 

- EPA and DHA have an anti-inflammatory action and help reduce inflammation in the body. The typical Western diet provides an overabundance of omega-6 fatty acids, which can favour an inflammatory response. Thus, higher amounts of omega-3 fatty acids in the diet or through supplementation are recommended.

## Cardiovascular health 

- Omega-3 fatty acids support healthy cardiovascular system function and heart health. DHA is the principal fatty acid incorporated into myocardial membrane phospholipids. 

   - A randomised, double-blind, comparison study found that the combination of glucosamine sulfate and omega-3 fatty acids was superior to glucosamine sulfate alone in relieving symptoms of osteoarthritis, including morning stiffness and pain in hips and knees[8] . 

- Omega-3 fatty acids exert their benefit on the cardiovascular system via a number of different mechanisms, including improved myocardial oxygen efficiency and heart rate, modulation of myocardial sodium and potassium ion channel function and improved endothelial function. Studies have demonstrated that fish oils improve endothelial relaxation by enhancing vasodilation[3] . 

   - Typically, fish oil supplementation is 1g/day. Much higher doses are needed to exert an anti-inflammatory action, with most guidelines recommending 2.7g or more of long chain omega-3s (equivalent to 3 capsules daily). 

- Omega-3 fatty acids also inhibit platelet aggregation. EPA is the precursor to the series 3 prostaglandins (PGE3) that reduce platelet stickiness. EPA is metabolised in leukocytes, to leukotriene B5, which reduces platelet adhesion, and in endothelial cells to produce prostacyclin I3, which relaxes blood vessels and reduces platelet aggregation. 

## Muscle health 

   - Omega-3 fatty acids support muscle health and function as they have intrinsic anabolic properties in skeletal muscles and can blunt the loss of skeletal muscle. 

   - Several studies show that varying doses of EPA and DHA reduce muscle pain and soreness after exercise and help post-exercise recovery, potentially via antioxidant and anti-inflammatory actions[9,10] . 

- The Australian Heart Foundation recommends that adults consume about 500 milligrams of marine-sourced omega-3 oil per day by eating 2-3 serves of oily fish a week or by taking fish oil supplements to lower their risk of coronary heart disease[4] . 

- A double-blind, randomised, controlled trial found that 6 months of omega-3 supplementation increased thigh muscle volume and handgrip strength. The authors suggested that 6-months of omega-3 essential fatty acids can prevent 2-3 years of normal age-associated losses in muscle mass and function[11] . 

## Brain and eye health 

- Omega-3 fatty acids support brain function, cognitive health and memory. 

   - The inclusion of fish oil supplementation to strength training has been found to improve muscle strength and functional capacity in women, but not in men[12,13] . 

- Fatty acids are found in high concentrations in neuronal membranes and in the myelin sheath and play a role in neuronal membrane fluidity and function. DHA is the major component of phospholipids in the brain and contributes to the maintenance of normal brain function. 

## Skin health 

   - Omega-3 fatty acids support skin health. 

   - EPA is important for skin health, helping modulate the inflammatory response, maintain stratum corneum permeability barrier and protect from photodamage. 

- A placebo-controlled, cross-over study evaluating the effects of five weeks omega-3 supplementation (3g/day) on cognitive performance in 40 healthy, middle aged to elderly individuals found that supplementation improved cognitive performance, specifically resulting in better performance in the working memory test (p<0.05)[5] . 

## Emotional wellbeing 

   - Omega-3 fatty acids support healthy emotional and mood balance. 

- A study of 20- to 34-year-olds found that EPA-rich supplementation enhanced neurocognitive function and suggested that the brain worked less hard yet had better cognitive performance[6] . 

   - Omega-3 supports membrane fluidity in the brain, improving neurotransmitter binding and signalling, and reduce inflammatory cytokines, which may improve neurotransmitter function, including both serotonin and dopamine transmission[14] . 

- A systematic review and meta-analysis in healthy adults aged 18 and older found that episodic memory improved with DHA and EPA supplementation. The study found that >1g/day DHA/EPA improved episodic memory, regardless of cognitive status at baseline (p<0.04)[7] . 

   - A study investigated the effects of omega-3 fatty acid supplementation in healthy individuals. Thirty-three subjects were given 4g of fish oil, equivalent to 1600mg of EPA and 800mg of DHA, and 16 were given olive oil as a placebo for 35 days. On day 1 and day 35, subjects filled in the Profile of Mood States (POMS) psychometric scale, which assesses anger, anxiety, fatigue, confusion, sadness and vigour. Supplementation with omega-3s strongly reduced the arachidonic acid/eicosapentaenoic acid ratio (14.26 ± 8.87 vs 4.29 ± 2.6, p<0.0001) and improved mood profile, with an increase of vigour and a decrease in other mood states, including anger, anxiety, fatigue, sadness and confusion[15] . 

- Omega-3 fatty acids support eye health, particularly retina health. DHA is the major component of phospholipids in the retina and contributes to the maintenance of normal vision. 

## Joint health 

- Omega-3 fatty acids support joint health and may help relieve symptoms of mild arthritis due to their anti-inflammatory actions. EPA and DHA exert their anti-inflammatory actions via a number of mechanisms, primarily by competing with omega-6 PUFA arachidonic acid (AA) for metabolism by cyclo-oxygenases and lipoxygenases, resulting in the production of less pro-inflammatory eicosanoids. 

   - A meta-analysis of eight randomised, controlled trials with a total of 367 women found that supplementation with EPA and DHA positively influenced mood. In seven of the eight studies, the dose of EPA was higher than DHA, with the authors postulating that EPA may influence mood by acting through eicosanoid mechanisms to increase cerebral blood flow[16] .

## **Triple Strength Omega-3** 

## Women’s health 

- Triple Strength Omega-3 can relieve menstrual pain (dysmenorrhoea). 

- Dysmenorrhoea is characterised by painful menstruation that can limit participation in normal activities. Typically, pain occurs shortly before or at the onset of menstruation and lasts 1-3 days. Pain is believed to be caused by inflammation, as prostaglandins accumulate in the uterine muscle a few days leading up to menstruation, promoting smooth muscle contraction. Primary dysmenorrhoea may result from an imbalance between antiinflammatory eicosanoids derived from omega-3 fatty acids (vasodilator effects) and pro-inflammatory eicosanoids derived from omega-6 fatty acids (vasoconstriction effects). Therefore, supplementing with anti-inflammatory omega-3 fatty acids may benefit individuals suffering from menstrual pain. 

- An early study found that 1080mg of EPA and 720mg of DHA (equiv. 2 capsules of Triple Strength Omega-3) significantly reduced the Cox Menstrual Symptom Scale from baseline value of 69.9 to 44.0 (p<0.0004) in adolescents with dysmenorrhoea[17] . 

- A more recent double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover study investigated the effects of fish oil supplementation in 38 women aged 18-22 with dysmenorrhoea. The study found that 550mg EPA and 205mg DHA (approx. 1 capsule of Triple Strength Omega-3) significantly reduced low back pain and abdominal pain (p<0.05) and reduced the need for rescue medication (NSAIDs)[18] . 

- Caution with antihypertensive drugs – fish oils may have additive effects. Monitor. 

- Caution with orlistat – drug inhibits the absorption of fat in the gut. Separate dose by 2 hours. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- Individuals with bleeding disorders should only take fish oil supplements under medical supervision. 

- Discontinue use 1 week before surgery. 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- Fish oils up to 3-4g/day are generally very well tolerated. Higher doses can cause halitosis, heartburn, dyspepsia, nausea, loose stools and rash in some individuals.

## Pregnancy & breastfeeding 

- Omega-3 fatty acids support healthy foetal development and brain function in breast-fed healthy infants. 

- DHA supports healthy eye, brain and central nervous system development, especially during the 3[rd] trimester and early postnatal period where maximal growth occurs. 

- Adequate DHA during breastfeeding is important as infants receive DHA from their mothers’ milk. Additionally, infant plasma omega 6:3 ratio improved[22] .

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Tyrosine is a non-essential amino acid (synthesised endogenously from the essential amino acid phenylalanine) and is an essential precursor for a wide range of diverse and far-reaching biochemical reactions in the body. 

- The name tyrosine is derived from the Greek word ‘tyros’, meaning cheese, and was first discovered in cheese-derived casein in 1846 by chemist Justus von Liebig. Tyrosine can also be obtained from dietary proteins in dairy products, meats, fish, eggs, nuts, beans, oats and wheat. When dietary intake of tyrosine is inadequate, phenylalanine is converted to tyrosine. Dietary needs of tyrosine are dependent on phenylalanine intake. When phenylalanine intake is adequate (about 9 mg/kg daily), dietary tyrosine intake should be about 7mg/kg daily[1] . 

- Tyrosine absorption takes place in the small intestine and is then transported to the liver where it is involved in a number of biochemical reactions including protein synthesis and oxidative catabolic reactions. Any tyrosine not metabolised by the liver enters systemic circulation and is directed to various tissues where it is involved in the synthesis of neurotransmitters and hormones, incorporated into protein structures or deaminated for gluconeogenesis. Peak plasma levels occur 2 hours after administration and remain elevated for around 6-8 hours. 

## Nervous system health 

- Tyrosine is an essential precursor for the synthesis of catecholamines adrenaline, noradrenaline and dopamine. Supplementation with tyrosine aids adrenal function helping during periods of prolonged stress, to support the body and improve stress adaptation. 

- Tyrosine can readily cross from systemic circulation into the brain, functioning in the synthesis of dopamine. Dopamine is the neurotransmitter responsible for motivation and reward. 

- Tyrosine has been shown to enhance the release of catecholamines when neurons are firing at an increased rate due to stress, but not at their basal rates.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) is comprised of two closely related molecules: ubidecarenone (also known as ubiquinone) and ubiquinol. Ubiquinone is the fully oxidised state of CoQ10, while ubiquinol is the fully reduced or active form. 

- Ubiquinol is the metabolically active form of CoQ10 that is ready for use in the body. Other forms of CoQ10, such as ubidecarenone, are converted to ubiquinol prior to use. Ageing leads to a decrease in the function of the enzyme that converts ubidecarenone to ubiquinol, resulting in decreasing ubiquinol levels. For anyone over the age of 40, ubiquinol is the preferred CoQ10 supplemental form. 

- Ubiquinol is more bioavailable than ubidecarenone, demonstrating greater absorption and uptake by the body. 

- A randomised, double-blind, crossover study examined the bioavailability of both ubiquinol and ubiquinone using an acute intake of 100mg in 10 healthy subjects with 2 weeks between treatments. In the ubiquinol group, plasma concentrations were significantly higher compared to ubiquinone at 6, 8, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hours post-intake (p<0.001). The area under the curve (AUC) for ubiquinol 72 hours post-intake was 4.3-fold greater than for ubiquinone[1] . 

- The ubiquinol in Ubiquinol 100mg is sourced from world-wide ubiquinol specialist, Kaneka, who use innovative patented technology to stabilise ubiquinol (which, under normal circumstances, is readily oxidised by air and converted into ubidecarenone). 

- Ubiquinol 100mg contains ubiquinol produced in a natural fermentation process by yeast. It is in a rice bran oil base, which provides a stable base. Rice bran oil has a high content of tocotrienols (antioxidants in the vitamin E family), which provide greater stability from oxidation than soy oil. 

## Antioxidant 

- Ubiquinol is a potent lipid-soluble antioxidant that helps protect the body from oxidative damage. Specifically, it protects cell membranes from oxidation, supporting cell membrane integrity and cell functioning. 

- Ubiquinol also supports the antioxidant network by prolonging the activity of vitamins C and E and recycling them back into their antioxidant form. 

## Energy production & exercise

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) is comprised of two closely related molecules: ubidecarenone (also known as ubiquinone) and ubiquinol. Ubiquinone is the fully oxidised state of CoQ10, while ubiquinol is the fully reduced or active form. 

- Ubiquinol is the metabolically active form of CoQ10 that is ready for use in the body. Other forms of CoQ10, such as ubidecarenone, are converted to ubiquinol prior to use. Ageing leads to a decrease in the function of the enzyme that converts ubidecarenone to ubiquinol, resulting in decreasing ubiquinol levels. For anyone over the age of 40, ubiquinol is the preferred CoQ10 supplemental form. 

- Ubiquinol is more bioavailable than ubidecarenone, demonstrating greater absorption and uptake by the body. 

- A randomised, double-blind, crossover study examined the bioavailability of both ubiquinol and ubiquinone using an acute intake of 100mg in 10 healthy subjects with 2 weeks between treatments. In the ubiquinol group, plasma concentrations were significantly higher compared to ubiquinone at 6, 8, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hours post-intake (p<0.001). The area under the curve (AUC) for ubiquinol 72 hours post-intake was 4.3-fold greater than for ubiquinone[1] . 

- The ubiquinol in Ubiquinol 150mg is sourced from world-wide ubiquinol specialist, Kaneka, who use innovative patented technology to stabilise ubiquinol (which, under normal circumstances, is readily oxidised by air and converted into ubidecarenone).

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Zinc is an essential trace element known to play an important role in all human living cells. The human body contains about 2g of total zinc, with more than 85% found in skeletal muscle and bone[1] . 

- Zinc plays a crucial role in the pathways involved in inflammation, immunity, carbohydrate and protein metabolism, DNA metabolism and repair, reproduction, vision, taste and bone health. 

- Zinc is required for the synthesis of new tissue and is an important cellular building block. A complex homeostatic system maintains zinc levels within a narrow range balancing absorption and excretion. 

- Zinc is widely distributed in foods. Meats, fish and poultry are the major contributors to the diet, but cereals and dairy foods also contribute substantial amounts. The presence of zinc in foods as a complex rather than as free ions affects its bioavailability. The environment within the gastrointestinal tract, which can be affected by other dietary constituents, markedly influences the solubility and absorptive efficiency of zinc. 

- Zinc is more difficult to absorb from plant-based foods. Many plant sources of zinc also contain high phytate levels, such as wholegrains and seeds, which inhibit the absorption of the mineral. The requirement for dietary zinc may be as high as 50% greater for vegetarians. 

- Ultra Zinc + helps maintain zinc levels in the body. To address established zinc deficiency, 25-50mg of zinc per day is recommended[2] . Signs of zinc deficiency include impaired immune function, reduced sense of taste and smell, poor wound healing, poor cognitive function, irritability and dermatitis. 

- To date, there is no established reliable marker for measuring an individual’s zinc status. Zinc is stored intracellularly and only a small percentage is found in the plasma, meaning plasma zinc levels are not a precise measure. 

- Ultra Zinc + contains high-strength vitamin A with 1500IU per capsule. Vitamin A is an essential nutrient required for growth and development, immune function, eye health and the maintenance of epithelial surfaces. 

## Antioxidant 

- Zinc is a powerful antioxidant and free radical scavenger. Zinc's role as an antioxidant is achieved through numerous mechanisms 

including protecting vitamin E from depletion, acting as an important structural component of the antioxidant enzyme superoxide dismutase and reducing free radical production. 

- Vitamin A has free radical scavenging properties and, when bound to protein kinase C, is an essential cofactor in redox activation of the mitochondrial signaling pathway. 

## Immune system health 

- Zinc is an important mineral for healthy immune system function. It is essential for the normal development and function of immune cells, for mediating non-specific immunity, such as neutrophils, monocytes and natural killer cells and for affecting the development of acquired immunity and T-lymphocyte function. 

- Poor zinc status has been shown to impair cellular mediators of the body’s innate immune system, reducing the body’s natural resistance to infectious agents. 

- Vitamin A  supports healthy epithelial cells in the body and is therefore a key nutrient for maintaining skin barrier to infection and healthy immune system function. Adequate vitamin A is also important for T cell function and the prevention of prolonged inflammatory reactions[3] . 

## Skin health 

- Ultra Zinc + supports skin health and wound healing. The skin is the third most zinc-rich tissue in the body, with 5% of total body zinc[4] . Zinc is present in both the epidermis and dermis, though at levels five-fold higher in the epidermis. In skin physiology, zinc stabilises cell membranes, serves as an essential cofactor for several metalloenzymes and participates in basal cell mitosis and differentiation. 

- Vitamin A is a key nutrient for normal cellular differentiation and 

- epithelial integrity. Vitamin A deficiency can lead to dry skin. 

- Both zinc and vitamin A are often recommended for acne. One study found that the serum vitamin A and zinc levels were significantly lower in patients with acne than in age and sex matched healthy individuals in the control group (p<0.001). It also showed a negative correlation between acne severity and zinc levels[5] . 

- In another study, plasma vitamin A concentrations were significantly lower in patients with acne than age-matched healthy controls (p=0.007)[6] .

## Vision & eye health 

- Ultra Zinc + supports eye health and vision.

Zinc is a cofactor in a number of ocular enzymes, including copperzinc superoxide dismutase, which functions as an antioxidant by catalysing the conversion of free radicals to hydrogen peroxide.

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Contraindicated with retinoid medication (including acitretin, isotretinoin, accutane or roaccutane) – vitamin A supplements should not be taken concurrently due to potential vitamin A toxicity. 

- Caution with NSAIDs, cephalexin, penicillamine and quinolone antibiotics and tetracycline antibiotics – zinc interferes with their absorption and vitamin A may reduce their effectiveness. Separate dose by 3 hours. 

- Caution with amiloride (diuretic) – drug can reduce zinc excretion, leading to zinc accumulation. 

- Caution with eltrombopag – zinc may reduce drug absorption. Separate dose by 4 hours. 

- Caution with levodopa – vitamin B6 reduces drug effects. However, this effect is prevented by the administration of a dopadecarboxylase inhibitor (e.g. benserazide, carbidopa) with levodopa, as is common clinical practice. 

- Caution with phenobarbital/phenobarbitone and phenytoin (anticonvulsants) – vitamin B6 may reduce serum concentrations. Monitor. 

- Caution with oral contraceptives – concurrent use may increase vitamin A levels. 

- • Caution with aspirin and paracetamol – zinc and vitamin A may reduce their effectiveness. Separate dose by 2 hours. 

- Caution with calcium supplements – zinc and calcium compete for common intestinal absorption sites. Separate zinc and calcium supplements by at least 2 hours.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Vitamin B1 (thiamine) is a water-soluble vitamin that is involved in carbohydrate metabolism and nervous system health. As body reserves of thiamine are small, a steady intake is important to avoid deficiency. Vitamin B1 100mg helps prevent vitamin B1 deficiency. 

- There is approximately 30mg of thiamine in the average adult, with about half of this stored in muscle tissue. It is also found in high concentrations in the heart, liver, kidneys and brain[1] . 

- Vitamin B1 is absorbed in the small intestine. It is generally well absorbed, however, several dietary factors can decrease absorption, including alcohol, thiaminase, sulfite preservatives, high intakes of tea and coffee and folate or protein deficiency. A high alcohol intake is the greatest risk factor for thiamine deficiency, as alcohol both impairs the absorption and enhances the excretion of the vitamin, doubling the risk of deficiency. 

- Strenuous exercise, fever, excessive alcohol consumption, pregnancy and lactation and adolescent growth periods can increase thiamine requirements. The elderly may also have an increased requirement for thiamine. 

- Food sources of thiamine include meats, wheatgerm, wholegrain cereals, peas, beans and peanuts, milk, Brewer’s yeast and yeast extracts. Wheatgerm provides an important source of thiamine in the diet, however, thiamine is sensitive to heat and light, so can be lost in processing. 

- Thiamine hydrochloride is the most common form of supplemental vitamin B1. It consists of 89% thiamine and 11% hydrochloric acid. 

- Excess thiamine is cleared from the body via the kidneys; as such, there is no evidence of toxic effects from oral administration. 

- Vitamin B1 plays a role in the metabolism of several neurotransmitters, including acetylcholine, GABA and serotonin, and, therefore, plays a role in maintaining healthy mood.

Eighty percent of patients treated with riboflavin alone had a 50% or greater reduction in monthly migraine days[1] . 

- Common clinical symptoms of riboflavin deficiency include inflammation of the throat, mouth (stomatitis), and tongue (glossitis); cracking of the tissue around the corners of the mouth (angular cheilitis) and moist, red, scaly skin. 

   - Following this, a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled study investigated the effects of 400mg riboflavin or placebo daily for 3 months on 55 patients with migraine. Riboflavin was found to be superior to placebo in reducing attack frequency (p=0.005) and headache days (p=0.012). For headache days, the number of patient responders (at least 50% improvement) was 15% for placebo and 59% for riboflavin (p=0.002; NNT 2.3)[2] . 

- Vitamin B2 is essential for the activation of other B complex vitamins. FAD is required for the formation of niacin from tryptophan and FMN is required for the formation of the active vitamin B6. Vitamin B2 also participates in folate metabolism. FAD is a cofactor for methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHRF), which converts folate into its active form. 

   - More recently, a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled study involving 98 patients receiving either 400mg riboflavin daily or placebo for 3 months was performed. The duration and frequency of headache were significantly less in the second and third months of the study in the riboflavin group vs placebo (p=0.012 and p=0.001, respectively)[3] . 

- Vitamin B2 promotes normal growth and tissue repair. It is required for the growth of skin, hair and nails and a deficiency of vitamin B2 can lengthen wound healing time. 

- Vitamin B2 helps maintain a healthy immune system. It is required for humoral antibody formation and helps maintain tissue barriers to infection. 

- A 2017 systematic review concluded that riboflavin is a well-tolerated and inexpensive treatment, demonstrating efficacy in the reduction of adult patient’s migraine headache frequency as well as duration[4] .

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Vitamin B3 is a water-soluble B complex vitamin important for energy production within cells, cell-signalling and DNA synthesis and repair. 

- Nicotinamide, also known as niacinamide, is the main form of vitamin B3 present in dietary sources and supplements. Vitamin B3 is also available as niacin (or nicotinic acid), which can be associated with skin flushing. 

- Herbs of Gold Vitamin B3 500mg contains nicotinamide, the amide form of nicotinic acid which does not cause the dilation of capillaries and flushing seen with high doses of niacin. 

- Nicotinamide is found in meat, fish, poultry, wholegrain breads, 

- fortified cereals, molasses and Brewer’s yeast. 

- Vitamin B3 is rapidly absorbed in the small intestine and found in high concentrations in the liver, muscles, kidneys and heart. Excess vitamin B3 is methylated in the liver and excreted in the urine. 

- Vitamin B3 can be formed in the body from the amino acid tryptophan, however, it takes approximately 60mg of tryptophan to form 1mg of niacin, with an approximate conversion rate of 60:1. This conversion requires adequate iron, riboflavin and vitamin B6. 

- As tryptophan is also a precursor to serotonin and dietary tryptophan is preferentially converted to vitamin B3 in deficiency states, low levels of vitamin B3 can result in serotonin depletion and mood alterations.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Vitamin B6, otherwise known as pyridoxine, is a water-soluble vitamin involved in carbohydrate, protein and lipid metabolism. Vitamin B6, unlike other B vitamins that are regularly excreted from the body, is stored extensively in muscle tissue. 

- Pyridoxine hydrochloride is the most common supplemental form of vitamin B6. After absorption in the small intestine, pyridoxine is transformed into pyridoxal 5-phosphate (P5P), the active form, either in intestinal cells or the liver and then distributed to tissues. 

- Vitamin B6 100mg contains high-strength pyridoxine hydrochloride with activated vitamin B6 as P5P. 

- P5P is a coenzyme involved in more than 150 enzymatic reactions in the body[1] . It is necessary for transamination reactions that allow the formation of non-essential amino acids, the conversion of tryptophan to niacin (vitamin B3) and serotonin and for the synthesis of glucose from glycogen. 

- Vitamin B6 is found in wholegrain cereals, organ meats, legumes, eggs and yeast extracts. Like most B vitamins, B6 is sensitive to light, heat, air and mechanical disruption, so its content in food can be reduced by physical processing, cooking, sterilisation and freezing. One study found that cooking loss of vitamin B6 in chicken ranged from 55-89%[2] . 

- Aging, excess alcohol and caffeine intake, poor diet, certain medications and chronic stress can increase an individuals’ requirements for vitamin B6. 

## Nervous system health & emotional wellbeing 

- Vitamin B6 is important for healthy nervous system function. It is crucial for the synthesis of sphingolipids, essential constituents of the lipid-rich myelin sheath surrounding nerves. 

- Vitamin B6 supports emotional wellbeing as it is involved in the synthesis of several neurotransmitters, including gamma aminobutyric acid (GABA), serotonin, norepinephrine and dopamine. 

- Serotonin and dopamine are neurotransmitters that play a role in an individual’s mood and wellbeing. Dopamine plays a part in controlling the movements a person makes, as well as their emotional responses. Serotonin is used to transmit messages between nerve cells and contributes to wellbeing and happiness. 

## Blood health 

- Vitamin B6 helps maintain healthy blood. It is necessary for the synthesis of the haem component of haemoglobin, which transports oxygen in red blood cells. 

- Vitamin B6 also has a role in homocysteine metabolism. High homocysteine is an independent risk factor for adverse cardiovascular outcomes. The conversion of homocysteine to cysteine requires two P5P-dependent enzymes: cystathionine synthase and cystathionase. Vitamin B6 is best prescribed with folate and vitamin B12 for homocysteine management. 

## Immune system health 

- Vitamin B6 supports healthy immune system function. Vitamin B6 participates in the functioning of the entire immune system. 

- Vitamin B6 plays a key role in humoral and cell-mediated immunity. It supports antibody production and the communicative interactions between cytokines and chemokines, immune chemicals responsible for orchestrating a highly specific immune response[4] . Thus, a deficiency may suppress immune system function, increasing the body’s susceptibility to infection. 

## Premenstrual tension (PMT) 

   - Vitamin B6 is a cofactor in the synthesis of neurotransmitters and an immediate precursor to serotonin and dopamine. It is also involved in GABA synthesis and enzymatic steps of tryptophan and tyrosine metabolism. Its deficiency may lead to reduced concentrations of noradrenaline and serotonin. Research suggests vitamin B6 may be beneficial in managing psychological symptoms of PMS. Low levels of vitamin B6 increases prolactin levels, resulting in more psychological symptoms during the premenstrual period. 

   - The neurotransmitters GABA and serotonin play key roles in mood, anxiety and pain perception. B6 is also important for magnesium transportation into the cell membrane. 

   - A 2016 systematic review of 12 randomised, placebo-controlled trials concluded that using vitamin B6 may reduce the overall symptoms of PMT. There seems to be no dose-related response to treatment, with dosages ranging from 40-300mg daily for the duration of 1-3 menstrual cycles[5] . 

- A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial found that daily supplementation with high dose vitamin B6 (100mg/day) improved self-reported mood outcomes[3] . 

- A deficiency in vitamin B6 has been associated with alterations in mood.

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Caution with chemotherapeutic agents – evidence regarding the use of vitamin C in conjunction with chemotherapy treatment is still emerging. Use only under medical supervision. 

- Caution with warfarin and anticoagulant/antiplatelet medication – high dose vitamin C may theoretically increase bleeding risk. Monitor. 

- Caution with aluminium based antacids – vitamin C increases the amount of aluminium absorbed. Separate dose by 2 hours. 

- Caution with NSAIDs, cephalexin, penicillamine and quinolone antibiotics and tetracycline antibiotics. Zinc forms complexes with these drugs, reducing the absorption of both. Separate dose by 3 hours.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- While once only known for its role in bone health, the diverse role of vitamin D in the body is still under discovery. Vitamin D acts like a hormone in the body, with vitamin D receptors found right throughout the body, including in skeletal and cardiac muscle, all immune cells, many cells involved in cardiovascular homeostasis, brain cells, and reproductive tissues, suggesting its essential role in whole body function. 

- Vitamin D is essential for the body to absorb calcium effectively, which is important for bone health and muscle function. The main source of vitamin D is exposure to sunlight, although small amounts can be obtained through some foods, such as fatty fish and fortified margarine and milk.

## Muscle health 

- Vitamin D supports muscle health and muscle strength. 

- Adequate vitamin D assists both muscle function and muscle strength, playing an important role in the elderly and postmenopausal women contributing to a reduction in injury and falls[4] . 

## Support healthy pregnancy 

- Vitamin D supports a healthy pregnancy and healthy foetal development. 

- Low vitamin D status in a breastfeeding mother directly correlates to low vitamin D in breastmilk. Adequate vitamin D is required for both musculoskeletal and neurological growth and for the development of the newborn. 

## Calcium absorption & bone health 

- Vitamin D supports bone health by assisting calcium absorption in the intestines and influencing bone remodelling. Vitamin D is necessary for osteocalcin, which binds calcium to bone. 

- Vitamin D maintains appropriate serum calcium concentrations by enhancing the ability of the small intestine to absorb calcium from the diet. In a low vitamin D state, the small intestine can only absorb approximately 10%–15% of dietary calcium. However, with adequate vitamin D, intestinal absorption of dietary calcium rises to approximately 30%–40%[1] . 

- The National Osteoporosis Foundation (NOF) recommend vitamin D intake of 800-1000 IU daily along with calcium for preventing osteoporosis in adults over 50 years of age[2] . 

- Clinical research shows taking vitamin D3 orally with calcium supplements can decrease postmenopausal bone loss, help prevent osteoporosis, and decrease the risk of all fractures by 8% to 17%, nonvertebral fractures by 14% to 49%, and hip fractures by 9% to 30% in older adults[3] . 

- Vitamin D helps to strengthen teeth as part of its role in regulating calcium and phosphate.

- Caution with atorvastatin – vitamin D may decrease bioavailability. Monitor. 

- Caution with orlistat (weight loss) – may impair the absorption of vitamin D. Separate dose by 2 hours. 

- Caution with digoxin – concurrent vitamin D may elevate serum calcium levels which can increase toxicity of cardiac glycosides. Monitor calcium levels. 

- Caution with thiazide diurectics – can cause an increase in serum calcium levels when coadministered with vitamin D. Monitor serum calcium levels.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Vitamin K is a group of structurally similar, fat-soluble vitamins that are needed in the body to help the blood clot and for binding calcium in bone. 

- Vitamin K occurs naturally in two forms: phylloquinone (vitamin K1) and menaquinone (vitamin K2). Menadione (vitamin K3) is a synthetic form that does not occur naturally. 

- Vitamin K1 is made from plants and found in foods such as broccoli, spinach, cabbage, asparagus, green tea and chlorophyll. Vitamin K in foods is not affected by heating, but can be destroyed by freezing. Vitamin K2 is mainly of microbial origin and present in animal products and fermented foods such as meat, cheese, eggs, natto and sauerkraut and also made by bacteria in the gut. The concentration of vitamin K2 in foods is very low and digestion and utilisation of vitamin K2 from foods becomes less efficient with ageing[1] . One exception to this is natto, a traditional Japanese food made from whole fermented soybeans, known to contain very high levels of vitamin K2 - in fact it is the world’s richest food source of vitamin K2. The high consumption of natto in Japan has been postulated as the reason that Japan has a lower fracture risk than other countries[2] . 

## Vitamin K2 

- Vitamin K2 is a group of compounds composed of a methylated naphthoquinone ring and an isoprenoid side chain of variable length (usually 4-15 units). Menaquinones are further classified according to the length of their side chain, referred to as MK-n, where n denotes the number of isoprenoid units. Currently, MK-4 and MK-7 are the most common forms of vitamin K2, with MK-7 displaying higher bioavailability and functionality.

## Postmenopausal women 

- Current research confirms vitamin K2 as a key vitamin for postmenopausal women. 

## Vitamin K2 functions 

- Vitamin K2 is a cofactor for the γ-glutamyl carboxylase enzyme, which catalyses the conversion of glutamic acid residues to γ-carboxyglutamic acid (Gla). The Gla family of proteins are involved in important metabolic processes including blood coagulation, bone mineralisation and artery health. 

- One of vitamin K2’s most important functions is the γ-carboxylation of osteocalcin (OC), an important marker of bone turnover that is secreted by osteoblasts. Vitamin K-dependent processes convert undercarboxylated osteocalcin (ucOC) to carboxylated (active) osteocalcin (cOC). 

- When serum vitamin K is deficient, serum ucOC will be increased and cOC levels will be decreased. The extent of osteocalcin carboxylation is the most sensitive marker for vitamin K2 status and is expressed as the ratio between cOC and ucOC. In healthy adults, approximately 30% of the circulating osteocalcin occurs in the undercarboxylated form[9] . 

- A study in healthy postmenopausal women aged 50-69 investigated the effects of different doses (0, 50, 100 or 200 micrograms) of MK-7 to ascertain the minimum effective dose to affect the cOC/ucOC ratio in blood. MK-7 dose-dependently improved osteocalcin γ-carboylation, demonstrating a 7% increase in cOC and a 20% decrease in ucUC at a dose of 100 micrograms or more[10] . 

## Bone health 

- Vitamin K2 supports bone mineral density (BMD) and promotes bone quality and strength. 

- cOC (activated by vitamin K-dependent enzymes) binds to hydroxyapatite to facilitate the deposition of calcium into bones, promoting bone mineralisation. 

- Unsurprisingly, Japanese research shows that consumption of natto, high in vitamin K2, is associated with better bone health. 

- A cross-sectional analysis of 1662 community dwelling elderly Japanese men aged 65 or over found that subjects with greater intake of natto had significantly higher BMD and lower risk of low BMD at the total hip and femoral neck, believed to be a result of the vitamin K2 content in natto[11] . 

- Women reach a peak bone mass around the age of 25 to 30, with the hormone oestrogen playing an important role in maintaining bone strength. Menopause, generally occurring between the ages of 45 and 55, causes a drop in oestrogen levels, resulting in increased bone loss. It is estimated that women lose up to 10 percent of their bone mass in the first five years after menopause[14] . 

- Therefore, maintaining bone strength and BMD in postmenopausal women is a key factor in healthy ageing. 

- A 3-year randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study investigated the effects of 180 micrograms of MK-7 on bone health in 244 healthy postmenopausal women. Supplementation with MK-7 significantly improved vitamin K status, as seen by significantly decreased circulating ucOC levels by 51±21% as compared to placebo (+ 4±49%)(p<0.001), and increased cOC 21±19% as compared to placebo (+3±16%)(p<0.001). MK-7 supplementation decreased the age-related decline in BMD at the lumbar spine and femoral neck, but not at the total hip, with reduced loss in vertebral height of the lower thoracic region. MK-7 supplementation also favourably affected bone strength[15] . 

- Another study investigated the effects of 50 or 90 micrograms of MK-7 on bone loss at the femoral neck. Supplementation with 90 micrograms of MK-7 for one year resulted in lower bone loss in postmenopausal women (p=0.006), but had no effects in men. Interestingly, this study showed no additional benefit of adding calcium (500mg/day) and vitamin D (10 micrograms/day)[16] . 

## Cardiovascular health 

- Studies have found that long-term use of MK-7 supplements beneficially affects cardiovascular and artery health. 

- Vitamin K2 supports cardiovascular health through regulation of calcium homoeostasis. Vitamin K2 activates a protein known as matrix Gla protein (MGP), which is an inhibitor of vascular calcification. MGP is synthesised in vascular smooth muscle cells, cartilage and bones. MGP binds free-floating calcium to prevent deposition in arteries to help support artery health. 

- Vascular calcification can result in reduced arterial elasticity and increased arterial stiffness, which is an independent predictor of cardiovascular risk. Observational studies show lower calcification in subjects with the highest intake of menaquinones, however, this effect was not seen with vitamin K1[17] .

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Vitex agnus-castus (Chaste tree) has a long history of traditional use in Western herbal medicine (WHM) for the relief of menstrual irregularities and symptoms of premenstrual tension (PMT). 

## Vitex 1000 for menstrual regulation 

   - Irregular periods can be caused by many factors, including but not limited to, sporadic ovulation, decreased progesterone or increased prolactin. 

- The dried fruit from the Vitex plant contains several active constituents including flavonoids, iridoids, alkaloids and volatile oils. 

   - Vitex works by increasing the release of luteinizing hormone from the pituitary gland, which raises progesterone and normalises the second half of the menstrual cycle. 

- The mode of action of Vitex is multifaceted. Vitex acts on dopamine (D2) receptors in the anterior pituitary gland, decreasing high prolactin levels. Prolactin is a hormone that primarily functions to help women produce milk after childbirth. However, in non-breastfeeding mothers, elevated prolactin can block the production of other hormones in the body, including oestrogen and progesterone. Elevated prolactin levels are associated with menstrual irregularities and symptoms of PMT[1] . 

## Vitex & the oral contraceptive pill (OCP) 

   - Vitex is generally not considered suitable to be used alongside the OCP. 

   - Vitex may reduce the effectiveness of contraceptives as it can act as a precursor to the hormones involved in ovulation. This may negate the ovulation-inhibiting effects of the OCP. As a result, women using Vitex alongside birth control could experience an increased risk of unplanned pregnancy[5] . 

- Low doses of Vitex have been shown to increase luteinising hormone (LH) while decreasing follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), working indirectly on achieving oestrogen and progesterone balance within the body. Oestrogen dominance in females is linked to mood disorders, including PMS, and menstrual irregularities. 

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- It is recommended Vitex be taken in the morning, before breakfast, as this is the time the pituitary gland is the most receptive. 

- Contraindicated with fertility drugs or IVF – the addition of Vitex could potentially cause hyperstimulation of the ovaries. 

## Premenstrual syndrome 

   - Caution with hormone replacement therapy, oral contraceptive pills and progesterone drugs – given Vitex’s hormone modulating effect, it may theoretically interfere with the action of these drugs. 

- Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is a combination of emotional, physical, psychological and mood disturbances that generally occur after a female ovulates and before the onset of a menstrual period. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- Emotional symptoms can include irritability, crying, oversensitivity and mood swings, while physical symptoms may present as fatigue, bloating, breast tenderness, skin issues such as acne or appetite changes and food cravings. 

   - Avoid use in individuals with tumours sensitive to oestrogen or progesterone. 

   - Vitex is not generally recommended in females under 20 years of age as the natural hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis can be easily disrupted. 

- It is estimated that as many as 90% of women experience at least one PMS symptom most months and about 50% of women experience several PMS symptoms each month[2] . 

   - Vitex is most effective during the first three to six months of use. After that, its effect on the pituitary starts to diminish. It is recommended to take a break from Vitex for two months before resuming use. 

- For some women who suffer from PMS, the symptoms are severe enough to interfere with regular day-to-day activities. 

- Not recommended during pregnancy without medical advice and breastfeeding due to insufficient studies relating to safety. 

## Vitex 1000 for PMS 

- Several clinical studies have been conducted on Vitex for premenstrual syndrome. A phytopharmaceutical formulation of an extract of Vitex fruit was used in 1634 females suffering from PMS symptoms. Self-assessment questionnaires were used to assess symptoms such as headache, anger, irritability, mood, breast fullness and bloating. After taking Vitex for three menstrual cycles, 93% of females reported either a decrease in the number of symptoms or complete cessation of complaints[3] . 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- In some cases, Vitex may initially worsen PMS symptoms.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Women’s Multi + contains a blend of vitamins, minerals, nutrients and herbs in a one-a-day supplement to support women’s health. 

- Women’s Multi + contains Grape seed extract equivalent to dry herb 12g. Grape seed contains oligomeric proanthocyanidins which are potent antioxidants to reduce free radicals formed in the body. Grape seed also supports healthy veins, blood vessels and microcirculation. 

- Women’s Multi + contains antioxidant nutrients vitamin C, citrus bioflavonoids, vitamin E, zinc and selenium to help reduce free radical damage. Vitamin C is the most important water-soluble antioxidant in the body, while vitamin E is a fat-soluble antioxidant whose major role is to protect polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA) from oxidation. It acts as an antioxidant in the lipid phase of cell membranes. 

- Women’s Multi + contains nutrients that support immune system function, including vitamin C, vitamin E, vitamin D, zinc and selenium. 

- Women’s Multi + contains nutrients that support blood health and assist healthy red blood cell production. Iron, folate, vitamin B12 and copper help the formation of red blood cells in the body and support normal blood function. 

- Women’s Multi + contains chromium to assist sugar and carbohydrate metabolism. Chromium assists in the uptake of glucose into the cells by stimulating insulin uptake and enhancing its activity. Requirements for chromium are increased when consuming a diet high in sugar. 

## B vitamins 

- Women’s Multi + contains therapeutic doses of all the B group vitamins, plus the active form of folate and vitamin B12. 

- As B vitamins are water soluble, regular daily intake is required to support general health. B vitamins work synergistically in the body and are, therefore, best taken together. 

- B vitamins support energy production, assist sugar and carbohydrate metabolism and help convert carbohydrates and protein into energy. 

- Women’s Multi + contains methylfolate (5-MTHF), the active form of folate. Folate is the generic term for a large family of chemically similar compounds known as vitamin B9. Folic acid is a synthetic form of the vitamin and must be reduced to methylfolate for use in the body. 

- Many people have mutations on the MTHFR gene, which affects their ability to convert folic acid into the active form (40-70% reduction in activity of the MTHFR enzyme). Methylfolate is a good alternative in individuals with MTHFR mutations as it is ready for use in the body and does not require conversion. 

- Women’s Multi + contains methylcobalamin (mecobalamin), the metabolically-active coenzyme form of vitamin B12 that is readily bioavailable for use in the body. Commonly-used cyanocobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 that does not occur naturally in foods and needs to be converted to methylcobalamin for use in the body. Methylcobalamin differs from cyanocobalamin in that the non-toxic cyanide molecule is replaced by a methyl group. 

## Nervous system 

- Women’s Multi + supports nervous system health and a healthy stress response. 

- B vitamins are involved in nerve impulse transmission and the synthesis of neurotransmitters, including acetylcholine, gamma aminobutyric acid (GABA), dopamine and serotonin, so they have a role in emotional balance and mood. Vitamin B12 is important for the manufacture of the myelin sheath, the protective sheath surrounding many nerves. Vitamins B5 and B6 help support a healthy stress response in the body as they are required for the synthesis of the adrenal hormones adrenaline and noradrenaline. Vitamin B5, as coenzyme A, is needed for healthy adrenal cortex function and the

- Methylfolate and vitamin B12 support brain health, cognitive function and memory. 

## Skin health 

- Women’s Multi + contains nutrients, vitamin C, vitamin E, zinc and copper, that support healthy skin, connective tissue formation and wound healing. 

- Vitamin C is found in the epidermis and the dermis of the skin, where it acts as an antioxidant, protecting against free radical damage, including UV-induced photodamage. Vitamin C also enhances collagen synthesis and stabilisation, enhances keratinocyte differentiation and improves wound healing. Vitamin E is the major naturally-occurring lipid-soluble antioxidant protecting the skin from oxidative stress. 

## Thyroid health 

- Women’s Multi + contains iodine and selenium, which help maintain healthy thyroid function and assist thyroid hormone production. Iodine is a precursor for thyroid hormones, required for normal growth and metabolism. Selenium is required for normal thyroid hormone synthesis, activation and metabolism. 

## Vitamin D 

- Women’s Multi + contains 1000IU of vegan-friendly vitamin D3, the maximum daily dose in a listed medicine. Vitamin D supports bone health in women and helps maintain bone density and strength in post-menopausal women. 

- Vitamin D assists the intestinal absorption of calcium and phosphorus, helping to maintain serum calcium concentrations. Research shows that in low vitamin D states, the small intestine absorbs approximately 10-15% of dietary calcium. When vitamin D levels are adequate, the small intestine can absorb 30-40%[1] . A diet deficient in calcium can lead to osteoporosis in later life. The National Osteoporosis Foundations guidelines (2014) recommend a daily intake of 8001000IU vitamin D daily with calcium for preventing osteoporosis in adults over 50 years of age[2] . 

- Vitamin D supports bone health independent of calcium. It is actively involved in bone formation and bone remodelling by osteoblasts and osteoclasts, resorption and mineralisation. Research shows that vitamin D with or without calcium can reduce the risk of all fractures by 8% to 17%, nonvertebral fractures by 14% to 49% and hip fractures by 9% to 30% in older adults[3] . 

- Vitamin D supports muscle function and helps maintain muscle strength. It has a role in the regulation and uptake of calcium in muscle cells, which is important for muscle strength, muscle contraction, mitochondrial function and insulin sensitivity.

- Caution with cardiac glycosides (e.g. digoxin) - vitamin D can elevate serum calcium levels, which may lead to increased inflow of calcium into myocardial cells, increasing toxicity of cardiac glycosides. Monitor calcium levels. 

- Caution with orlistat – may impair the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins. Take Women’s Multi + at least 2 hours after orlistat. 

- Caution with phosphate and drugs containing phosphate - vitamin D increases the absorption of phosphates which may lead to hyperphosphataemia. Monitor. 

- Separate the dose from colestyramine and colestipol – may reduce absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, vitamin B3 and folate. Space administration as far apart as possible. 

- Caution with calcium channel blockers - vitamin D may reduce the effectiveness of these drugs. Use under medical supervision. 

- Caution with blood thinning medications, including warfarin - vitamins E and C, selenium and Grape seed may interfere with the activity of vitamin K in producing blood clotting factors and lead to increased clinical effects of oral anticoagulants. Monitor. 

- Caution with NSAIDs, cefalexin, penicillamine and quinolone and tetracycline antibiotics – form insoluble complexes with magnesium and zinc, decreasing absorption. Seperate dose by 3 hours.

## **TECHNICAL INFORMATION** 

- Zinc and vitamin C are two of the most important nutrients known to man. They are both required for hundreds of processes in the body, including antioxidant protection and healthy immune system function. 

- Zinc is an essential trace element known to play an important role in all human living cells. The human body contains about 2g of total zinc, with more than 85% found in skeletal muscle and bone[1] . 

- Zinc plays a crucial role in the pathways involved in inflammation, immunity, carbohydrate and protein metabolism, DNA metabolism and repair, reproduction, vision, taste and bone health. 

- Zinc is required for the synthesis of new tissue and is an important cellular building block. A complex homeostatic system maintains zinc levels within a narrow range balancing absorption and excretion. 

- Zinc is widely distributed in foods. Meats, fish and poultry are the major contributors to the diet, but cereals and dairy foods also contribute substantial amounts. The presence of zinc in foods as a complex rather than as free ions affects its bioavailability. The environment within the gastrointestinal tract, which can be affected by other dietary constituents, markedly influences the solubility and absorptive efficiency of zinc. 

- Zinc is more difficult to absorb from plant-based foods. Many plant sources of zinc also contain high phytate levels, such as wholegrains and seeds, which inhibit the absorption of the mineral. The requirement for dietary zinc may be as high as 50% greater for vegetarians. 

- Zinc Forte + C helps maintain zinc levels in the body. To address established zinc deficiency, 25-50mg of zinc per day is recommended[2] . Signs of zinc deficiency include impaired immune function, reduced sense of taste and smell, poor wound healing, poor cognitive function, irritability and dermatitis. 

- To date, there is no established reliable marker for measuring an individual’s zinc status. Zinc is stored intracellularly and only a small percentage is found in the plasma, meaning plasma zinc levels are not a precise measure. 

- Vitamin C is an essential water-soluble nutrient for humans which cannot be made or stored in the body, so must be taken in the diet on a regular basis. 

- Vitamin C has several important functions in the body, including supporting the immune system, aiding collagen production for wound healing and skin health, maintaining bone health and supporting the absorption of dietary iron. 

- Zinc Forte + C combines high-strength zinc and vitamin C in a delicious raspberry flavoured powder that is naturally sweetened with Stevia and free from artificial colours and flavours. 

## Antioxidant 

- Zinc Forte + C contains antioxidant nutrients to reduce free radicals formed in the body. 

- Vitamin C is antioxidant by scavenging oxygen and nitrogen free radicals, regenerating antioxidant vitamin E and maintaining reduced glutathione. 

- Zinc is a powerful antioxidant and free radical scavenger. Zinc's role as an antioxidant is achieved through numerous mechanisms including protecting vitamin E from depletion, acting as an important structural component of the antioxidant enzyme superoxide dismutase and reducing free radical production. 

## Immune health 

   - Both vitamin C and zinc are important for a healthy immune system. 

   - Vitamin C concentrations in the body rapidly decline during times of infection and stress. Supplementation of vitamin C has been found to improve components of the human immune system such as antimicrobial and natural killer cell activities, processes known to fight infection. 

   - Likewise, zinc undernutrition or deficiency has been shown to impair cellular mediators of the body's innate immune system. Therefore, both vitamin C and zinc play important roles in immune function and the bodies natural resistance to infectious agents. 

   - Vitamin C levels are quickly depleted when an individual is put under stress; lack of vitamin C dramatically increases the chance of catching an infection. 

   - Vitamin C has been shown to not only help prevent the common cold, but also reduce the severity and duration of a cold once one exists[3] .
