## **Zinc Forte + C** 

The combination of zinc and vitamin C has been shown to reduce the duration and severity of common cold symptoms due to their immune-supporting actions[4] . 

## Skin health 

- Zinc Forte + C supports healthy skin. 

- Normal skin contains high concentrations of vitamin C as vitamin C is actively accumulated into the epidermal and dermal cells of the skin. Vitamin C supports epithelial barrier function against pathogens and promotes the oxidant scavenging activity of the skin, thereby potentially protecting against environmental oxidative stress and providing antioxidant protection against UV-induced photodamage. 

- Six percent of total body zinc is in the skin. Zinc is present in both the epidermis and dermis, though at levels five-fold higher in the epidermis. In skin physiology, zinc stabilises cell membranes, serves as an essential cofactor for several metalloenzymes, and participates in basal cell mitosis and differentiation. 

- Both vitamin C and zinc have a positive effect on the inflammatory processes in the skin and assists wound healing. Vitamin C is a co-factor in enzymes directly involved in the synthesis of collagen, while also providing antioxidant protection against UV-induced photodamage. 

- Vitamin C, through its role in collagen synthesis, helps maintain healthy blood vessels in the body and is a component of haemoglobin, assisting in the production of red blood cells. 

- Zinc is often recommended for acne. One study found that the serum zinc levels were significantly lower in patients with acne than in age and sex matched healthy individuals in the control group (p<0.001). It also showed a negative correlation between acne severity and zinc levels[5] . 

- Zinc is theorised to be beneficial in acne due to its role in the maintenance of cell replication and wound repair, regulation of inflammation, immune function and inhibition of 5α-reductase, which blocks the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone and supresses sebaceous gland activity[6] . 

## **DRUG INTERACTIONS** 

- Caution with NSAIDs, cephalexin, penicillamine and quinolone and tetracycline antibiotics – zinc forms complexes with these drugs, reducing absorption of both. Separate dose by 3 hours. 

- Caution with amiloride (diuretic) – drug can reduce zinc excretion, leading to zinc accumulation. 

- Caution with eltrombopag – zinc may reduce drug absorption. Separate dose by 4 hours. 

- Caution with calcium supplements – zinc and calcium compete for common intestinal absorption sites. Separate zinc and calcium supplements by at least 2 hours. 

## **CAUTIONS** 

- Use in caution if there is a history of renal calculi (kidney stones) as vitamin C (ascorbic acid) may increase the risk of recurrence of calcium oxalate calculi. 

- Caution in iron overload conditions, such as haemochromatosis, as vitamin C can increase iron absorption. 

## **SIDE EFFECTS** 

- High dose of zinc (50-150mg/day) may a cause mild gastrointestinal upset. Taking zinc with foods reduces the incidence of side-effects.

## Male reproductive health 

- Zinc plays an important role in maintaining male reproductive health. It is important for the normal functioning of the prostate gland and essential for the healthy formation and maturation of sperm. 

- There is a strong correlation between zinc status and sperm count, morphology and motility. 

- Vitamin C has also been shown to improve semen parameters in men. A 2018 study of seminal parameters in 40 men showed the addition of vitamin C demonstrated a statistically significant (p<0.05) improvement in all sperm parameters including count, motility, morphology and viability[8] . 

## Taste 

- The area of the brain responsible for the sensations of taste and smell needs adequate levels of zinc to function efficiently. 

- Adequate zinc helps maintain normal taste sensation. 

## Absorption of dietary iron 

- In the presence of vitamin C, the body absorbs iron far more efficiently. This is significant for vegetarians and vegans where absorption of iron from non-heme (plant-based) sources is generally lower than heme-based (animal) sources.
